kill-bill-whole-bloody-affair.title: Kill Bill: The Whole Bloody Affair
kill-bill-whole-bloody-affair.syn:
On the day of her wedding rehearsal, a pregnant bride is gunned down by her former assassin crew, the Deadly Viper Assassination Squad, shot in the head and left in a coma for four years. When she wakes, she draws up a list: O-Ren Ishii in Tokyo, Vernita Green in Los Angeles, Budd and Elle Driver in the desert, and last, her former lover Bill.

This time Tarantino recombines Kill Bill, once released in two parts, into a single complete film, running from the snowy blood-soaked fight at the House of Blue Leaves all the way to the final conversation in Mexico.
kill-bill-whole-bloody-affair.bio: Quentin Tarantino was born in 1963 in Tennessee and, working in a video store in Los Angeles, taught himself film through watching enormously. He debuted in 1992 with Reservoir Dogs, and Pulp Fiction won the Palme d’Or at Cannes in 1994. His work is known for non-linear structure, dense dialogue and homage to B-movies, kung fu, samurai and western films. Kill Bill came out in two parts in 2003 and 2004; The Whole Bloody Affair is the version he has long regarded as the complete single film.
kill-bill-whole-bloody-affair.st:
Shooting began in June 2002, and in the edit the producers realized the running time would pass four hours and suggested splitting it, which led to the first part in 2003 and the second in 2004. Tarantino always wrote and shot it as one film. At Cannes in 2006 he showed the combined version with minor editorial adjustments, after which it was only occasionally shown, for instance at his own New Beverly Cinema.

In December 2025 Lionsgate gave this version its first wide release in US theaters, stressing that the best way to see it is on 70mm or 35mm film. Compared with the two separate films, it removes the cliffhanger ending of Vol. 1 and the recap that opens Vol. 2 so the story runs through without a break, and adds a new animated sequence of about seven and a half minutes built around the past of O-Ren Ishii, produced by a Japanese team. An intermission is kept.

The story itself is the Bride’s revenge on her former colleagues and on Bill, and Tarantino uses the genre language of kung fu, samurai and Italian-style westerns to make a collage-like epic in homage to film history. The cast includes Uma Thurman, Lucy Liu, Vivica A. Fox, Michael Madsen, Daryl Hannah, Gordon Liu and David Carradine.
highlights: The full version drops the Vol. 1 cliffhanger and the Vol. 2 recap, so the story runs straight through.
A new animated sequence of about seven and a half minutes about O-Ren Ishii, made by a Japanese team.
Tarantino says it is best seen on 70mm or 35mm film, and this version has rarely been shown publicly.
Kung fu, samurai and western homages are dense, and the tone shifts noticeably from first half to second.
kill-bill-whole-bloody-affair.contentNote: Also informed by a published overseas content advisory. The running time and cut may differ from this screening; consider your individual needs.
kill-bill-whole-bloody-affair.editorial: For fans of genre cinema and Tarantino, and for anyone who wants to see the two parts as one film. It runs over four hours and contains a great deal of violence and gore, so plan your time and choose accordingly.

the-odyssey.title: The Odyssey
the-odyssey.syn:
After the Trojan War, Odysseus, king of Ithaca, sets out on the sea route home, only to be punished by the gods and repeatedly blocked by monsters and temptations, a journey that lasts ten years.

Far away in Ithaca, his wife Penelope and son Telemachus struggle to hold the palace against a crowd of suitors coveting the throne. Adapted from Homer’s epic, it tells how a man passes through an entire mythic world to return to his own home.
the-odyssey.bio: Christopher Nolan was born in London in 1970 and drew attention with Memento for its non-linear storytelling and complex time structures; he later directed The Dark Knight, Inception, Interstellar, Dunkirk, Tenet and Oppenheimer, working with Syncopy, the company he runs with Emma Thomas, and insisting on film and IMAX photography. After Oppenheimer he turned to Homer; it is his first film on Greek myth and the first shot entirely with IMAX film cameras.
the-odyssey.st:
Written, produced and directed by Nolan, and made by Universal Pictures and Syncopy, the film is reported to have cost around $250 million, the biggest investment of his career. It was announced in late 2024 and opened in July 2026. Drawing on Homer’s epic, it follows Odysseus, king of Ithaca, who after the Trojan War spends ten years wandering as he tries to return to his wife Penelope and son Telemachus. Matt Damon plays Odysseus, Anne Hathaway Penelope, Tom Holland Telemachus and Zendaya Athena, with Robert Pattinson, Lupita Nyong’o, Charlize Theron, Samantha Morton and John Leguizamo also in the cast.

It is the first narrative feature shot entirely on IMAX 70mm film cameras. IMAX cameras had been too loud for synchronized sound, and newly developed lighter, quieter models were used this time. According to Nolan, the production shot about two million feet of film over roughly ninety-one days across several countries, including Greece, Sicily and Scotland, filming the sea voyages on real water; the cinematographer is his longtime collaborator Hoyte van Hoytema.

It had its world premiere in London in July 2026 before opening worldwide, and many outlets called it one of the year’s biggest big-screen events. This farewell screening is in laser IMAX.
highlights: The first narrative feature shot entirely on IMAX 70mm film cameras.
About two million feet of film across several countries, with the sea voyages shot on real water.
A large ensemble led by Matt Damon, Anne Hathaway, Tom Holland and Zendaya.
Nolan’s first film on Greek myth, bringing Homer to the screen for the first time.
the-odyssey.contentNote: Available story information indicates: War, conflict or threat of war; Missing loved ones; Dangerous situations or accidents. This film contains flashing lights such as lightning, which may affect photosensitive viewers; people with photosensitive epilepsy or sensitivity to bright or strobing light should take precautions. Other detailed depiction and intensity have not been verified; consider your individual needs.
the-odyssey.editorial: Made for the IMAX screen, with large-format image and sound design as the draw; laser IMAX is recommended. It runs nearly three hours with war and sea sequences; see the content note for the flashing-light warning.
warnings: War, conflict or threat of war

dune-part-three.title: Dune: Part Three
dune-part-three.syn:
The story takes place seventeen years after Dune: Part Two. Paul Atreides has become emperor of the universe, and the holy war launched in his name sweeps the entire empire.

The greater his power, the narrower the future he can see. The Tleilaxu Face Dancer Scytale secretly plots to overthrow him, and court, religion and prophecy interweave into a new conspiracy. Adapted from Frank Herbert’s novel Dune Messiah, it is the finale of Villeneuve’s Dune trilogy.
dune-part-three.bio: Denis Villeneuve, born in 1967 in Quebec, drew attention with Incendies, Prisoners and Sicario before directing Arrival and Blade Runner 2049, and established himself in large-scale science fiction with the Dune films. His images favor vast space, quiet pacing and questions about religion, power and fate. Dune: Part Three is the closing chapter of his trilogy.
dune-part-three.st:
Adapted from Frank Herbert’s novel Dune Messiah, with a screenplay by Villeneuve and Jon Spaihts, the story is more political and philosophical than the first two films. Paul Atreides has become emperor but finds himself trapped by prophecy and holy war. The production reportedly began in Budapest in July 2025 and wrapped in November, with locations including Abu Dhabi. The cinematographer is Linus Sandgren, the editor Joe Walker, and Hans Zimmer returns to compose.

Timothée Chalamet, Zendaya, Florence Pugh and Rebecca Ferguson return, Robert Pattinson joins as the Face Dancer Scytale, and Anya Taylor-Joy plays Alia. Warner Bros. and Legendary dated it December 18, 2026, the same day as Avengers: Doomsday, which the internet nicknamed “Dunesday.”

The film is still in post-production, so full ratings and its world-premiere details have not yet been published.
highlights: Adapted from Dune Messiah, with a story more political and religious than the first two films.
Chalamet, Zendaya and Pugh return, with Robert Pattinson joining as Scytale.
Photographed by Linus Sandgren, scored by Hans Zimmer.
Opens the same day as Avengers: Doomsday, nicknamed “Dunesday.”
dune-part-three.contentNote: Available story information indicates: War, conflict or threat of war; Discrimination or abuse of power. Detailed depiction and intensity have not been verified; consider your individual needs.
dune-part-three.editorial: The series finale; watch the first two films first. The film has not yet been released, so ratings, content notes and the screening version will follow the final cut.
warnings: War, conflict or threat of war

avengers-doomsday.title: Avengers: Doomsday
avengers-doomsday.syn:
Fourteen months after the events of Thunderbolts*, heroes from three universes must band together: the Avengers of Earth-616, Wakanda and the new Avengers, the Fantastic Four of Earth-828, and the original X-Men from another universe.

They face a threat officially classed as “existence-level”: Doctor Doom. Robert Downey Jr. returns to Marvel, this time as the villain.
avengers-doomsday.bio: Anthony and Joe Russo, from Cleveland, Ohio, began with television comedies such as Arrested Development and Community before moving to Marvel, where they directed Captain America: The Winter Soldier and Civil War and Avengers: Infinity War and Endgame. They return for Avengers: Doomsday, written by Michael Waldron and Stephen McFeely.
avengers-doomsday.st:
The film was announced at San Diego Comic-Con in July 2024, with the Russo brothers returning to direct and Robert Downey Jr. appearing not as Iron Man but as a new villain, Doctor Doom. It was originally dated May 2026 and pushed to December 18, 2026 to allow time to finish production. It was reportedly shot at Pinewood Studios in England and elsewhere.

The cast brings together the Avengers, the Fantastic Four, the New Avengers and the X-Men, including Chris Evans, Chris Hemsworth, Anthony Mackie, Tom Hiddleston, Pedro Pascal, Vanessa Kirby, James Marsden and Channing Tatum. It will be followed by Avengers: Secret Wars in December 2027, and together the two close the Marvel Multiverse Saga.

The film has not been released, and its ratings and world-premiere details are pending.
highlights: Robert Downey Jr. returns, this time as the villain Doctor Doom.
The Avengers, Fantastic Four, New Avengers and X-Men share the screen.
The Russo brothers return to the Avengers, written by Michael Waldron and Stephen McFeely.
Avengers: Secret Wars follows in December 2027.
avengers-doomsday.contentNote: Available story information indicates: Crime, threat or interpersonal conflict; Disaster themes. Detailed depiction and intensity have not been verified; consider your individual needs.
avengers-doomsday.editorial: Series fans will get the most out of it; it helps to know recent Marvel films and shows. The film has not been released, and ratings and content notes will follow the final cut.

we-live-in-time.title: We Live in Time
we-live-in-time.syn:
Almut is a former figure skater and now a chef; Tobias has just been through a divorce. An unexpected car accident brings the two together, and they fall in love, move in, and quarrel over whether to have a child.

Almut is diagnosed with ovarian cancer and goes into remission after treatment, and the two have a daughter, Ella. When the cancer returns, she decides to enter the Bocuse d’Or world cooking competition. The film scrambles chronology, leaping back and forth between meeting, giving birth and saying goodbye, to piece together a ten-year love.
we-live-in-time.bio: John Crowley, born in 1969 in Ireland, built his experience in theatre and television before making films including Brooklyn, Boy A and The Goldfinch. He previously worked with Andrew Garfield on Boy A in 2007; this is a reunion. Brooklyn brought a Best Picture Oscar nomination, and he is known for handling emotion with a restrained camera.
we-live-in-time.st:
The screenplay is by the British playwright Nick Payne, best known for the stage play Constellations. The film does not tell the story chronologically but moves back and forth across a decade: the chef Almut and the recently divorced Tobias meet by accident, start a family, and then face Almut’s ovarian cancer diagnosis. The film lets viewers know the ending first and then slowly returns to how they fell in love.

The first pairing of Florence Pugh and Andrew Garfield is the biggest draw. Bryce Dessner composed the score, Stuart Bentley shot it and Justine Wright edited. It had its world premiere at the Toronto International Film Festival on September 6, 2024, and was released by A24 in the United States.

Reviews widely praised the chemistry of the leads, though some found the script’s emotional manipulation heavy-handed.
highlights: A non-linear structure that gives away the ending first and then returns to how the couple fell in love.
Florence Pugh and Andrew Garfield’s first pairing; their chemistry is the common subject of reviews.
Nick Payne’s script carries a stage-play ear for dialogue and humor.
World premiere at TIFF 2024, released by A24.
honors: 入选｜2024 Toronto International Film Festival · World Premiere
入选｜2024 San Sebastián International Film Festival · Closing Film (Out of Competition)
we-live-in-time.contentNote: Available story information indicates: Illness, treatment or care; Death and bereavement; Sexual or reproductive themes; Dangerous situations or accidents. Detailed depiction and intensity have not been verified; consider your individual needs.
we-live-in-time.editorial: A story of love and illness, parenthood and time, light in pace and heavy in feeling. It includes cancer and fertility-related storylines; viewers with recent related experience should think first.

for-better-or-worse.title: For Better or For Worse
for-better-or-worse.syn:
Li Xinran, an actress once plagued by depression, meets Piao Yuanbo, who has just left monastic life, at a party celebrating his return to lay life. They fall in love, marry, have their first child, and begin a new life with a few million yuan in savings.

Inexperience and extravagance whittle the savings away bit by bit. Yuanbo stakes all his hope on a handpan instrument factory in the mountains of Anji, but a second child is born, a partner leaves and the debts keep growing. Quarrels and reconciliations take turns, and the two learn, in the mire, to let go of their imagination of a perfect life.
for-better-or-worse.bio: Qin Xiaoyue is a Chinese documentary director and screenwriter. Her earlier film Nest records a family’s parting and reunion and won Best Documentary Feature at the FIRST International Film Festival. She is used to following ordinary families for long periods, paying attention to strength and vulnerability within intimate relationships.
for-better-or-worse.st: The film records the couple through long-term following, with the director also taking part in the filming, calling it “an extremely exhausting and extremely thrilling shoot.” The filmmakers neither romanticize marriage nor judge who is right or wrong; instead they let the audience see how two people struggle and compromise together. The film was in the main competition of the 2025 FIRST International Film Festival.
highlights: This isn't a fiction film. The fights, the make-ups and the silences are real, and the camera sits very close.
The ups and downs of the handpan workshop run underneath, almost in step with the marriage.
honors: 提名｜2025 FIRST International Film Festival · Best Documentary Feature
for-better-or-worse.contentNote: Available story information indicates: Depression; Financial hardship or exploitation; Relationship conflict or coercion. Detailed depiction and intensity have not been verified; consider your individual needs.
for-better-or-worse.editorial: About the real friction of an intimate relationship. See business, parenting and quarrels on one line of life; the documentary's value also lies in the moments left unresolved.

resident-evil.title: Resident Evil
resident-evil.syn: Bryan (Austin Abrams), a medical courier, is given a job to deliver a shipment into Raccoon City. When he arrives, a virus is spreading out of control and the whole city falls overnight, mutated monsters hunting the living in the streets. Trapped in the catastrophe, Bryan can only look for a way out amid the chaos and try to get out alive.
resident-evil.bio: Zach Cregger came from comedy as a member of the troupe The Whitest Kids U' Know before turning to directing, emerging with the 2022 horror film Barbarian and becoming one of the most watched genre directors with Weapons in 2025. Resident Evil is his first time taking on a major game franchise; he co-wrote it with Shay Hatten and also produced.
highlights: An original story: the hero is a medical courier with no combat training, not a game hero.
It runs alongside the Raccoon City outbreak, with the camera occasionally switching to a game-style first-person view.
Photographed by Dariusz Wolski, running about ninety minutes with a tight pace.
Many outlets rated it the best of the series, extending Cregger’s genre reputation from Barbarian and Weapons.
resident-evil.contentNote: Available story information indicates: Horror or threat; Crime, threat or interpersonal conflict. Detailed depiction and intensity have not been verified; consider your individual needs.
resident-evil.editorial: A choice for genre fans; no knowledge of the games is needed. It contains heavy gore and jump scares, so viewers sensitive to zombies, violence or confined spaces should think first.
resident-evil.st:
The rights holder Constantin Film had planned to put the series on hold, and the project restarted when Cregger pitched a new idea after the success of Barbarian. He did not remake the game plot; instead he invented an original story running parallel to the Raccoon City outbreak. The hero Bryan is an ordinary medical courier with no combat training who knows none of the games’ heroes, and who takes a delivery into Raccoon City General Hospital for a bonus.

The film is produced by Columbia Pictures and PlayStation Productions and was reportedly shot in the Czech Republic in late 2025, with Dariusz Wolski as cinematographer and Tom Hammock as production designer. Cregger weaves in game-like camera perspectives, such as sudden first-person views, giving the film a game’s sense of play while keeping the pace tight; the running time is about an hour and a half.

The film opened worldwide from September 2026, and many outlets called it the best entry in the series, though some critics found it Cregger’s lightest work.

no-mobile.title: No Mobile
no-mobile.syn: In the winter of 2023, the artist Hao Yang left his phone at home and set out alone on a 134-day offline journey through China. With only paper maps, cash, letters and face-to-face conversation, he traveled through 68 cities and counties in 24 provincial-level regions. Facing ubiquitous QR codes, reservations and online payments, he ran into one unexpected obstacle after another, and also rediscovered trust and chance encounters between people. The film records this personal experiment with digital daily life, asking how we perceive the world when life no longer depends on screens.
no-mobile.bio: Hao Yang works in contemporary art, using painting, moving image, calligraphy and walking as his media. He studied and researched art in the UK, and from 2023 to 2024 completed a 134-day trip across China with no phone and no internet, which he developed into a documentary and non-fiction writing.
no-mobile.st: The director answers a daily life surrounded by digital systems with 134 days of offline wandering: going without a phone and the internet meant layers of obstacles in payment, transport and lodging, and also brought the possibility of chance encounters, concentration and a renewed sense of time. The director Hao Yang will join the audience for a conversation after this screening. The film runs 14:30–16:21 on October 31; the post-screening talk begins at 16:21 and is expected to end at 17:20.
highlights: When everything starts with a QR code, how do you keep travelling offline?
134 days, 24 provincial-level regions and 68 cities and counties: an experiment in technology and personal freedom.
31 Oct 16:21–17:20: Q&A with director Yang Hao in person.
honors: 入围｜2025 Sweden Film Awards · Finalist (as stated on the poster)
入围｜2025 Austin International Art Festival · Finalist (as stated on the poster)
入选｜2025 Internationales Festival Zeichen der Nacht · Official Selection (as stated on the poster)
入选｜2025 Peshawar International Film Festival · Official Selection (as stated on the poster)
no-mobile.contentNote: The available synopsis has been reviewed, but no specific sensitive content has been established. This is not an all-ages assurance or a full content assessment.
no-mobile.editorial: For rethinking digital life. Focus on how maps, cash and face-to-face talk change a journey; don't read it as a claim that everyone should go offline.

gr26-001.title: Ben'imana
gr26-001.syn: In post-genocide Rwanda, a reconciliation organizer faces her own trauma when her daughter becomes pregnant.
gr26-001.bio: Marie-Clémentine Dusabejambo was born in Rwanda in 1987 and is based in Kigali. Before her debut feature she directed four shorts: Lyiza (2011), Behind the Word (2013), A Place for Myself (2016) and Icyasha (2018), mostly about memory, forgiveness and education after the genocide. Ben'imana is her first feature and the first film by a Rwandan director selected for the Cannes Official Selection; at Cannes 2026 it won both the Caméra d'Or and the FIPRESCI Prize in Un Certain Regard.
highlights: Won both the Caméra d'Or and the Un Certain Regard FIPRESCI Prize at Cannes; the first film by a Rwandan director in the Cannes Official Selection.
A gacaca in 2012: survivors and the families of perpetrators brought into one village to speak in public.
The survivor Vénéranda's faith in reconciliation collides with the trauma her daughter's unexpected pregnancy brings back.
The director's first feature, continuing the concern with memory, forgiveness and education seen in her short Lyiza.
gr26-001.st:
The film had its world premiere in Un Certain Regard at Cannes in May 2026. It is set in 2012 around a gacaca, the village-level community trial through which Rwanda tried cases and sought confession and reconciliation after the genocide. In interviews the director says Ben'imana means 'people of God', which is also what being Rwandan means; she made the film to pay tribute to her country's mothers, who found the strength to stand with dignity after error and the unspeakable, and the capacity to give and forgive, even when they did not always succeed.

It was co-written by Dusabejambo and Delphine Agut, produced by Samantha Biffot, and is sold internationally by MK2. In an interview with Africultures she describes roughly a decade of maturation, in which she first had to find how to represent ourselves, first in words and then in images.

At the closing ceremony on 23 May it won the Caméra d'Or from among 29 films (jury president Monia Chokri), plus the FIPRESCI Prize for Un Certain Regard. According to the director and African media, it is also the first African film to win the Caméra d'Or.
gr26-001.editorial: The film deals with trauma and the memory of violence after a genocide, so go in prepared. Watch how 'speaking out' is filmed: who speaks first at the gacaca and who stays silent, and how the mother's convictions pull against her daughter's private situation.
gr26-001.contentNote: Available story information indicates: Genocide and historical trauma; Family conflict or separation; Sexual or reproductive themes. Detailed depiction and intensity have not been verified; consider your individual needs.

gr26-002.title: The Road Not Taken
gr26-002.syn: A successful presenter struggles with marriage, parenthood and illness as memory loss changes her understanding of herself and her family.
gr26-002.bio: Peter Chan, born in Hong Kong, is a director and producer whose credits include Comrades: Almost a Love Story, Perhaps Love, American Dreams in China, Dearest and Leap. He is known for approaching realist subjects through ordinary people's feelings and circumstances. The Road Not Taken (Tomorrow Will Be Better) reunites him with Zhou Xun after Perhaps Love, reportedly 21 years later.
highlights: Peter Chan and Zhou Xun reunite after 21 years; shot entirely in Chengdu.
Premiered in Toronto's Special Presentations; opening film of the Golden Rooster domestic showcase.
Uses Alzheimer's disease as an entry point and stays with the patient's inner perspective.
Led by Zhou Xun, Wang Xiao, Tian Zhuangzhuang and Lin Xiaojie, with Wen Qi in a special appearance.
gr26-002.st:
The film was written by Zhang Ji and Wu Huiling, with Zhang Ji as chief planner, and stars Zhou Xun, Wang Xiao, Tian Zhuangzhuang and Lin Xiaojie, with Wen Qi in a special appearance. According to reports, Zhou Xun initiated the project and chose Peter Chan to direct. Chan visited an Alzheimer's care facility in Chengdu and adopted the carers' advice to families, roughly 'go with the flow, know when to stop', as a guiding principle; he reportedly rewrote the script to avoid a preachy disease drama and to stay with the patient's inner point of view. Zhou observed residents of care homes and drew on documentary footage for the role.

Shooting began on 8 May 2026 at Chengdu's Xicun Dayuan and took place entirely in Chengdu, with some scenes at the Emei Film Studio park, making it a 'made in Sichuan' Chinese-language film. At the opening Chan said it felt like going back to basics: a quiet film about family relationships.

It premiered in September 2026 in the Special Presentations section of the 51st Toronto International Film Festival and had its Asian premiere on 6 November as the opening film of the Golden Rooster domestic film showcase; the producers say it will be released in China within the year.
honors: 入选｜2026 Golden Rooster Film Screening · 国产新片展映
gr26-002.editorial: A family film that moves from marriage and parenting to memory loss without forced sentiment, good to see with parents or a partner. It deals with illness and divorce and may hit close to home.
gr26-002.contentNote: Available story information indicates: Illness, treatment or care; Ageing and care. Detailed depiction and intensity have not been verified; consider your individual needs.

gr26-003.title: When the Bottle Turns
gr26-003.syn: An elderly widower travels to ask about his late wife's reincarnation and meets a wandering poet along the way.
gr26-003.bio: Lodan is a Tibetan director and screenwriter, born in 1988 by Qinghai Lake and raised in a pastoral area; he graduated from the Beijing Film Academy. His early short Knot was honoured at the 16th World Ethnic Film Festival. When the Bottle Turns is his feature, and Pema Tseden advised at the script stage as a supervising producer.
highlights: A Tibetan-language road movie about an old man seeking his late wife's reincarnation.
Pema Tseden advised at the script stage; supervised by Lu Wei.
A FIRST and Golden Rooster Pitch work-in-progress project.
Minimalist storytelling; wind, prayer flags and footsteps form the sound design.
gr26-003.st:
A Tibetan-language road movie: Dampa, an old man near the end of his life, keeps dreaming of his late wife and decides to travel to a monastery to ask a lama about her reincarnation; on the way he meets a wandering poet who refuses mobile phones and modern transport. The filmmakers say the theme is the characters' attitude toward loneliness and death, with two outlooks complementing each other as release and redemption.

The project was supervised by Lu Wei with Dachue Tai and Liu Xiaodai producing; it was selected for the work-in-progress section of the FIRST Film Festival in 2024 and for the Golden Rooster Pitch WIP section the same year. The film showed at the 20th FIRST Film Festival in July 2026.

Some critics compare it to Abbas-style minimalism: few characters, little dialogue, with the weight placed on the road, the light and silence; the sound design lets wind, prayer flags and footsteps speak.
honors: 入选｜2026 Golden Rooster Film Screening · 国产新片展映

screeningNotes.11/6-18:20-xm-gr26-1-hall-4: Post-screening event · Director / Writer: Loden; Producer: Chen Caiyun, Liu Xiaodai (subject to who actually attends)

gr26-003.editorial: A slow, sparsely spoken poetic film for viewers willing to slow down and take it as a meditation on death and companionship.
gr26-003.contentNote: Available story information indicates: Death and bereavement. Detailed depiction and intensity have not been verified; consider your individual needs.

gr26-005.title: Donkey Princess
gr26-005.syn: A princess uses a magical bracelet to search for her banished lover after her grieving father forbids love throughout the kingdom.
gr26-005.bio: Cristóbal León and Joaquín Cociña are a Chilean directing duo known for strongly handmade mixed-media work. Their debut The Wolf House combined clay, puppetry and papier-mâché in stop-motion, moving from a seemingly juvenile storybook premise into trauma and horror. Donkey Princess is their third feature, continuing their hybrid live-action explorations and returning to adult fairy-tale terrain.
highlights: World premiere in Locarno's International Competition, August 2026; the third feature by the Wolf House directors.
Reworks Perrault's Donkey Skin: a princess defies a ban on love.
Handmade animation, sets and live action blend as worlds keep changing.
A Chile-France-Uruguay-Netherlands-Germany co-production.
gr26-005.st:
The film had its world premiere in Locarno's International Competition in August 2026, a Chile-France-Uruguay-Netherlands-Germany co-production written by the two directors with Alejandra Moffat. It reworks Charles Perrault's fairy tale Donkey Skin: Princess Diana defies a ban on love and travels across worlds and genres, trying both to preserve her relationship with Lalo and to remain faithful to her father's love.

It begins in a medieval Chilean court, where figures such as King Arthur (Francisco Melo) take several incarnations, and the settings and styles keep shifting as the princess escapes; the handmade, rough-edged textures are joined by increasingly visible live-action performance. Variety called it an inventive, shape-shifting adult fairytale in which a princess escapes the kingdom but not the patriarchy, turning more sober as it goes on.

Some critics feel the story lingers less than The Wolf House but still praise its imagination and handmade charm.
gr26-005.editorial: A visually dense fantasy fairy tale with a fairly clear storyline, for viewers who like handmade textures and strange imagination. It touches the shadow of a father-daughter relationship and turns heavy.
gr26-005.contentNote: Available story information indicates: Death and bereavement; Discrimination or abuse of power; Confinement or displacement. Detailed depiction and intensity have not been verified; consider your individual needs.

gr26-006.title: Red Rocks
gr26-006.syn: Children explore and compete along the French Riviera, where friendship, jealousy and first love transform a summer adventure.
gr26-006.bio: Bruno Dumont was born in 1958 and is one of the most distinctive French directors working today. He first appeared at Cannes in the Directors' Fortnight in 1997 with The Life of Jesus, which received a special mention for the Caméra d'Or; Humanité (1999) and Flanders (2006) each won the Grand Prix of the Cannes jury, and Slack Bay and France also competed for the Palme d'Or. Li'l Quinquin (2014) turned him towards absurdist comedy, and The Empire (2025), a parody of the sci-fi blockbuster, won a prize in Berlin and divided critics. Red Rocks returns him to the Directors' Fortnight with a cast of children aged roughly five to seven; the section itself called it a fresh departure in his body of work.
highlights: The leads are five-to-seven-year-olds with almost no adults in sight: they ally, quarrel and adventure, and the coast becomes their own society.
Red cliffs, sea-jumps and small motorbikes: wide-angle lenses and long, static takes make the children's bodies and adventures both funny and perilous.
A Romeo-and-Juliet-style love story as its frame, but a light tale about children, class and freedom.
Dumont is known for severity and absurdity; critics have called this his most accessible film in years.
gr26-006.st:
Red Rocks (original title Les Roches rouges) screened on 20 May 2026 in the Cannes Directors' Fortnight as a special screening, followed by a masterclass by the director. According to the section, the film was shot on the French Riviera with very young children, adopts a documentary-like approach and deliberately uses wide-angle lenses. Dumont wrote, directed and edited it himself; the leads are non-professionals, with Kaylon Lancel as Géo and Kelsie Verdeilles as Ève.

Several outlets note that it is framed as a Romeo-and-Juliet-style love story but spends most of its time on the children climbing red rocks, jumping into the sea and riding small motorbikes. Screen Daily called it Dumont's most accessible film in years; Variety observed that its long, static, mostly wordless takes make the adventures seem less eventful than they sound. There is hardly any adult presence, only a gendarmerie boat that tries to warn the children off the rocks and is given short shrift.

It then screened in the Zabaltegi-Tabakalera section of the 2026 San Sebastián Film Festival and opened in France on 23 September 2026. DMovies sees it as a return to the docudrama mode of Li'l Quinquin, with local vernacular, landscape and non-professional actors, where the puerile meets the epic.
gr26-006.editorial: If you want to see Dumont at his gentlest, start here. There is little plot; it plays more like an observation of one summer. Watch how the children ally and grow jealous, and how the camera keeps the adult gaze out.
gr26-006.contentNote: Available story information indicates: Distress or pressure affecting children. Detailed depiction and intensity have not been verified; consider your individual needs.

gr26-007.title: The Diary of a Chambermaid
gr26-007.syn: A Romanian domestic worker in France joins a theatrical production while longing to return home to her daughter for Christmas.
gr26-007.bio: Radu Jude was born in Bucharest in 1977 and is one of the sharpest satirists to emerge since the Romanian New Wave. He won the Golden Bear in Berlin in 2021 for Bad Luck Banging or Loony Porn; Do Not Expect Too Much from the End of the World (2023), Dracula (Locarno, 2025) and Kontinental '25 (Berlin) carried on his mix of absurdity, online imagery and social critique. The Diary of a Chambermaid is his first feature selected for Cannes and and his first foreign-language (French) film; he has said it is neither an adaptation of Mirbeau's novel nor a remake of earlier versions, some of them by great filmmakers including Luis Buñuel.
highlights: A 'variation' rather than an adaptation: Mirbeau's 1900 novel has been filmed by Renoir and Buñuel among others; Jude sets it in today's Bordeaux.
A Romanian woman works as a domestic while rehearsing The Diary of a Chambermaid in an amateur troupe; the maids on stage and in life mirror each other.
The employers speak kindly, yet condescension sits in the cracks; the film teases the old contrast between 'barbaric East' and 'civilised West'.
His first feature selected for Cannes, and his first foreign-language (French) film.
gr26-007.st:
The film premiered on 15 May 2026 in the Cannes Directors' Fortnight. Its title card uses the word 'variation': it reworks Octave Mirbeau's 1900 novel The Diary of a Chambermaid, which has previously been filmed by Jean Renoir, Benoît Jacquot and Luis Buñuel among others. Jude moves the story to the present day: in Bordeaux, a Romanian woman works for a bourgeois French family while joining an amateur theatre company that is staging The Diary of a Chambermaid.

Lead Ana Dumitrașcu appeared in Jude's Dracula and in Romania's 2021 Oscar entry; French actors Vincent Macaigne, Mélanie Thierry and Marie Rivière also star. Cinematographer Marius Panduru and editor Cătălin Cristuțiu are long-time collaborators, and the film is produced by SBS Productions of France with Romania's Avanpost.

Cineuropa described it as Jude 'going back to beautiful basics': a lightly metatheatrical piece about a Romanian mother in a Bordeaux bourgeois home, teasing the patronising employers through the old contrast between the 'barbaric East' and 'civilised West'. It then played in the Wavelengths section at Toronto.
gr26-007.editorial: For viewers who care about labour, migration and class. You need not read the novel first; notice how the employers' words signal kindness while drawing a line, and how the 'maid' on stage says what she cannot.
gr26-007.contentNote: Available story information indicates: Social inequality or workplace mistreatment; Migration or displacement; Family conflict or separation. Detailed depiction and intensity have not been verified; consider your individual needs.

gr26-008.title: zi
gr26-008.syn: A young violinist in Hong Kong encounters images of her future self and strangers who alter her experience of time.
gr26-008.bio: Kogonada is a Korean-American director who first became known for his video essays. His feature debut Columbus (2017) premiered at Sundance, followed by the science-fiction film After Yang and the romantic fantasy A Big Bold Beautiful Journey (2025). The latter, a studio-funded star vehicle, was widely panned; zi is his return to independent, experimental filmmaking.
highlights: World premiere in Sundance NEXT, January 2026; shot in three weeks in Hong Kong.
A violinist haunted by visions of her future self wanders Hong Kong.
Ryuichi Sakamoto's music and Hong Kong street scenes carry the film's texture.
Starring Haley Lu Richardson, Jin Ha and Michelle Mao.
gr26-008.st:
The film had its world premiere in Sundance's NEXT section in January 2026, was picked up by Grasshopper Film and opened in the US on 6 November, running 99 minutes. It was reportedly shot in just three weeks in Hong Kong in October 2025 in a low-budget, run-and-gun style; IndieWire reports that Kogonada asked six friends to fly themselves there to take part. Benjamin Loeb shot it, the soundtrack includes music by Ryuichi Sakamoto, and the cast is Michelle Mao as Zi, Haley Lu Richardson as Elle and Jin Ha as Min.

It follows a young violinist, Zi, as she wanders Hong Kong, glimpsing visions of her future self and fearing a diagnosis that could end an upcoming tour; she meets the American Elle, who leads her to Elle's friend Min. Reviews generally praise its texture and mood, while finding the story slight and some dialogue stiff.

Several critics read it as a response to the director's studio project, trading narrative convention for spontaneity and drift.
gr26-008.editorial: More a mood poem than a plotted drama, for viewers who want to feel the atmosphere of a city and loneliness. If you prefer clear cause and effect, it may feel drifting.
gr26-008.contentNote: Available story information indicates: Psychological distress or uncertainty. Detailed depiction and intensity have not been verified; consider your individual needs.

gr26-009.title: Iron Boy
gr26-009.syn: A boy forced to wear metal braces discovers music and friendship while struggling to help save his father's farm.
gr26-009.bio: Louis Clichy was born in 1979 and is a French animator and director. He worked as an animator at Pixar on WALL-E and Up and co-directed the animated features Asterix: The Mansions of the Gods (2014) and Asterix: The Secret of the Magic Potion (2018). Iron Boy (original title Le Corset) is the first feature he has directed on his own. It leaves the CG of those films for a hand-painted 2D style built on watercolour and Chinese ink, and draws on his memories of growing up working-class in the French countryside; the lead is voiced by his son, Gary Clichy.
highlights: Special Jury Prize in Cannes Un Certain Regard, then three Annecy prizes: Jury Award, Audience Award and the Gan Foundation Award for Distribution.
It began with an image: a boy in a corset standing as straight as the letter I in a flat field, flipping the horizon when he lowers his head.
Beauce in the 1980s, hand-painted 2D in watercolour and Chinese ink, with an ethereal score of classical organ and choral music.
The lead is voiced by the director's son Gary Clichy, and the story draws on his own upbringing and his move from son to father.
gr26-009.st:
Iron Boy premiered on 19 May 2026 in the Un Certain Regard section at Cannes, where it won the Special Jury Prize; it then took three awards at the Annecy International Animation Film Festival (the Jury Award, the Audience Award for a feature, and the Gan Foundation Award for Distribution), and drew overwhelmingly positive reviews in a major year for animation at Cannes. Sony Pictures Classics handles it in the US.

In an interview published by Cannes, Clichy said the project had been with him for a long time. It began with an image he once enjoyed animating: a boy in a corset, standing as straight as the letter I in an expanse of flat fields, who flips the horizon when he leans his head. Having moved from son to father, he returned to the story and to the need to explore the father-son relationship in a tragicomic way. It is set in the Beauce region in the 1980s, among a farming family, electricity pylons and churches, with an ethereal score of classical organ and choral music.

The characters from outside the rural setting, the organist, the girlfriend and the priest, were voiced by Alexandre Astier, Brune Moulin and Jean-Pascal Zadi, who bring a variety of acting that the director says he likes.
gr26-009.editorial: A good family watch. The story is in no hurry to 'overcome' anything; notice how farm labour and the church organ open two lives for the same child, and enjoy the watercolour fields and skies.

gr26-010.title: The House on the Moon
gr26-010.syn: Chang'e journeys to the dark side of the moon to find the missing Hou Yi in a science-fiction reimagining of Chinese mythology.
gr26-010.bio: Nelson Yeo is a Singaporean director. His first narrative feature, Dreaming & Dying, won the Golden Leopard in Locarno's Cineasti del presente competition and the best first feature prize in 2023; The House on the Moon brings him to Locarno's international competition for the first time.
highlights: A story set after Chang'e's flight to the moon, told in her own narration.
World premiere in Locarno's international competition, reportedly its only Chinese-language entry.
Science fiction meets wuxia, with fights staged like dreamlike dance.
A Singapore–Taiwan co-production shot on Taiwan's north coast and the Guanyin dunes.
gr26-010.st:
Inspired by the myth of Chang'e, Hou Yi and Feng Meng, this is a Taiwan–Singapore co-production in science-fiction wuxia, with Indonesia and Germany reportedly involved. Yeo has said that making this childhood fantasy was once as far off as reaching for the moon. Lin Shi'an plays Chang'e, Huang Guanzhi Hou Yi and Zhang Huaiqiu Feng Meng, with Lee Kang-sheng also appearing; Huang and Zhang both play period roles for the first time, with a good deal of classical Chinese in the dialogue.

The film starts after Chang'e's flight to the moon, opening with her narration, which gives her agency rather than treating her as a mythic symbol; Feng Meng is written with faint queer undertones. The fight scenes are deliberately soft, using dropped frames, slow motion and close-ups of body parts, more dreamlike dance than traditional hard, fast wuxia. It was shot at locations including Elephant Trunk Rock on Taiwan's north coast and the Guanyin sand dunes in Taoyuan.

It had its world premiere in the international competition of the 79th Locarno Festival in August 2026, reportedly the only Chinese-language film in the main competition; its Taiwan premiere is the 2026 Golden Horse Film Festival.
gr26-010.editorial: A light, slightly humorous retelling of myth that mixes science fiction and wuxia. Expect something other than traditional hard-hitting wuxia; it has some queer-coded elements.

gr26-011.title: Ah girl
gr26-011.syn: In 1990s Singapore, a seven-year-old moves between her separated parents' homes and uses imagination to protect her childhood.
gr26-011.bio: Ang Geck Geck Priscilla (Hong Yuju) is a Singaporean director and screenwriter. Ah girl is her first feature as writer-director, drawn from her own childhood; before it she made three short films centred on the character Ah Girl.
highlights: World premiere in Rotterdam's Bright Future; won the Youth Jury Award.
Shot in 4:3, seeing the world from a child's limited point of view.
Ong Xuan Jing won best actress at the Hong Kong festival's Firebird Awards.
Three Golden Horse nominations: new director, new performer and adapted screenplay.
gr26-011.st:
Set in a 1990s Singapore HDB estate, the film follows seven-year-old Ah Girl caught between two households after her parents separate. Ang says she had already made three shorts about Ah Girl before the feature; friends suggested her next one be happier, so she wanted this one to carry more hope and to truly celebrate the girl and let her shine.

According to reports the project struggled for funding; she worked three jobs at once, then received Singapore government funding and put in her own savings and investment from friends. The film is shot in 4:3, like 1990s television, and an IFFR programmer praised how camera height and format let viewers experience the world from a child's limited perspective.

It had its world premiere on 31 January 2026 in the Bright Future section of the 55th International Film Festival Rotterdam, where it won the Youth Jury Award; in April Ong Xuan Jing won best actress in the Firebird Awards of the Hong Kong International Film Festival; in October it received three Golden Horse nominations; it opens in Singapore in November.
gr26-011.editorial: A family drama about parents' separation seen through a child's eyes, delicate rather than melodramatic; gentle in pace, with laughter and pain in the details.

gr26-012.title: The Evil Inside
gr26-012.syn: A former cabaret star wakes in a sinister care home and uncovers a deadly gambling game while searching for her daughter.
gr26-012.bio: Lingo Hsieh is a Taiwanese director and writer known for fantasy, thriller and horror. Her 2014 short The Evil Inside won a Golden Harvest Awards prize, she completed her first feature Corpse Memory in 2015, and in 2019 she co-created and directed the series Ximending Soul.
highlights: Expanded from Hsieh's award-winning short; the producers say it draws on real events.
Joan Chen's first lead role in a Taiwanese film.
A showroom star, gambling debts and a deadly bet in a nursing home.
Theme song sung by A-Lin.
gr26-012.st:
The film grew out of Hsieh's short The Evil Inside, which won a top prize in the general category at the 37th Golden Harvest Awards in 2015; the producers say the story draws on real events, with the extent of adaptation not yet disclosed. Hsieh co-wrote it with Hsu Ling-fang and principal photography took place in 2025.

Joan Chen stars in a Taiwanese film for the first time, playing He Zhenzhen, a former showroom star known as Jin Fengna who abandoned her daughter over gambling debts. Hsieh says Chen was her first thought when the character took shape; she flew to San Francisco to meet her and read Chen's book Cat Fish. Chen calls the role a woman who crawled out of hell, and the biggest challenge was making an unsympathetic character sympathetic. The film puts maternal selfishness, evasion and remorse into a survival crisis in a nursing home.

Cinematography is by Hsu Chih-chun, music by Chen Yen-chu and the theme song is A-Lin's Baobei Airen; it screened from September 2026 including at the Kaohsiung Film Festival and opened in Taiwan on 29 October.
honors: 入选｜2026 Golden Rooster Film Screening · 拾光：华语新片展映
gr26-012.editorial: A psychological thriller with 1980s showroom-style visuals and music; it contains thriller and death themes, so check the content notes.

gr26-013.title: Zoom In, Zoom Out
gr26-013.syn: A game designer follows his missing roommate's digital traces, crossing paths with a woman as reality and virtual worlds overlap.
gr26-013.bio: Dong Jie, born in the 1990s, graduated from the Beijing Film Academy in 2019; his graduation short Recess showed at the third Pingyao International Film Festival. Zoom In, Zoom Out (发现之旅) is his first feature.
highlights: World premiere in the Venice Critics' Week competition, winning Best Innovative Film and best first feature.
The crew built the film's game themselves; key creatives are mostly university classmates.
At Pingyao: Fei Mu Honour Jury Prize and Cinephile Choice Award.
Dong Jie's first feature.
gr26-013.st:
A game designer, Shi Zi'an, travels between the real world and a game world to find the truth about a missing roommate, meeting an online friend, Yaya. Dong says the core search thread never changed, but the game elements grew in the course of writing; the team decided to build an interactive game scene with a game engine themselves, developing the game a year ahead and testing it repeatedly, because merely imitating how a game looks would not feel real. The key crew in cinematography, sound and game development are his university classmates.

The project was a top-ten Qingcong Project entry and was in the Shanghai International Film Festival's film project pitch. Shooting began on 1 November 2024 at Songjiang's Haopu studios and wrapped in early December; editing took most of a year, the final cut came in September 2025 and post-production was completed in July 2026.

It had its world premiere in the Critics' Week competition at the 83rd Venice Film Festival in September 2026, winning the Best Innovative Film award and the Bisato d'Oro for best first feature from Italian independent critics; the Critics' Week artistic director called it a manifesto film for Gen Z. Its Asian premiere followed on 27 September at the 10th Pingyao International Film Festival, where it won the Fei Mu Honour Jury Prize and the Cinephile Choice Award.
honors: 入选｜2026 Golden Rooster Film Screening · 国产新片展映

gr26-014.title: Starting Towards the Finish Line
gr26-014.syn: Children in a remote mountain village restore a buried car in the hope of reaching Lotus Town and finding a missing mother.
gr26-014.bio: Hou Jue is a mainland Chinese director and screenwriter who graduated from the directing department of the graduate school of the Moscow film institute. He directed his first film Northward Sunshine in 2019, then Kung Fu Boy, and in 2024 entered production on Farewell Vivian and Starting Towards the Finish Line.
highlights: An eight-year-old repairs a buried wreck of a car to go find his mother in town.
Outstanding work-in-progress project at the Beijing International Film Festival pitch.
Selected for the main competition of Germany's Schlingel children's film festival.
Named one of the year's top ten films at India's Aryan International Children's Film Festival.
gr26-014.st:
Written by Fan Hui, Bei Yi and Hou Jue, the film follows eight-year-old Xiaoqing in a deep-mountain Fujian village, who suspects his mother working in Lotus Town has remarried and resolves to find out; with poor transport in the mountains he stumbles on a car frame buried in silt and decides to repair it and drive there. Dapang, who wants a treat in Lotus Town, and Gezi, who has to fetch a letter for his grandmother, join him, and a volunteer teacher who notices the kids skipping school gets drawn in.

Director Jiang Ping is artistic consultant, Rao Shuguang chief supervising producer, Jiang Wusheng chief producer and Xing Xiao producer and supervisor. Xing wrote that few domestic children's films truly take a child's perspective and seem fun to children, which was his reason to join.

The project received an 'Outstanding Work-in-Progress Project' honour at the 15th Beijing International Film Festival's pitch in 2024; the film was selected for the main competition of the 31st Schlingel International Film Festival in Germany and named one of the year's ten best films at the 9th Aryan International Children's Film Festival in India.

gr26-015.title: Fatherland
gr26-015.syn: Thomas Mann and his daughter return to Germany in 1949, confronting war, exile and the divided meaning of home.
gr26-015.bio: Paweł Pawlikowski was born in Warsaw in 1957. He won the Oscar for Best Foreign Language Film with Ida (2013); Cold War (2018) won him Best Director at Cannes and Oscar nominations, and Fatherland makes him a two-time Cannes Best Director. All three films are in black and white, in a near-square frame and set in post-war Europe, and critics have read Fatherland as completing a trilogy with the earlier two. He reunites with cinematographer Łukasz Żal; Sandra Hüller and Hanns Zischler play Erika and Thomas Mann, and the script is by Pawlikowski and Henk Handloegten.
highlights: Best Director at Cannes, Pawlikowski's second after Cold War, and Poland's Oscar submission for Best International Film.
In 1949, Thomas Mann and his daughter Erika drive across a divided Germany collecting awards, through ruins and along the Cold War's fault line.
Sandra Hüller plays Erika, actress, writer and rally driver; with Hanns Zischler's Thomas Mann she builds a distant yet bound father-daughter relationship.
Black and white, Academy ratio, 82 minutes: the restrained aesthetic of Ida and Cold War.
gr26-015.st:
Fatherland had its world premiere on 14 May 2026 in the Cannes competition, and Pawlikowski won Best Director again for it; it then played at the New York Film Festival and is Poland's submission for the Oscar for Best International Film, with MUBI handling distribution. In Cineuropa's interview with the director, the film is described as focused on Thomas Mann's return from US exile to post-war Germany.

Set in 1949, it follows the Nobel laureate and his daughter Erika as they drive across a Germany divided between East and West, picking up awards; Erika is an actress, writer, rally driver and her father's right hand. Brother Klaus Mann, played by August Diehl, appears in a single scene which audience reviews describe as a memorable one-take performance. The black-and-white image and Academy ratio continue the look of Ida and Cold War; the cinematographer is Łukasz Żal.

Critics are divided: Metacritic shows a score of 86, and Cineuropa says not a single take feels superfluous, while Screen Rant and others find it too cold to connect with; the running time is only 82 minutes.
gr26-015.editorial: A little background on Thomas Mann and his children Erika and Klaus helps, but is not essential. Notice how father and daughter answer the question of 'home' differently, and the late exchange about where home is.

gr26-016.title: Gold Life
gr26-016.syn: A doctoral student and full-time mother in Dali balances a strained marriage, childcare and an uncertain future.
gr26-016.bio: Zhang Xin is a director, screenwriter and actor. Gold Life (七分熟) is her first feature, which she wrote, directed and starred in, drawn from her real experience of raising a child and writing around the time she finished her PhD.
highlights: Written, directed and starred in by Zhang, from her real life as a mother and doctoral student.
Between drama and documentary, deliberately blurring real and fictional.
World premiere at FIRST; won best narrative feature in the main competition.
Shot in Dali, largely a one-person effort in early stages.
gr26-016.st:
Zhang says the idea came in 2023 when she was alone in Dali, a place without the people or equipment to make films. At the time of her doctorate she faced a dilemma between pursuing a university post and her creative work. She chose a method between drama and documentary, letting life as it unfolded mirror the narrative on screen and deliberately blurring real and fictional.

She wanted to ask whether the plight of middle-aged women is a personal matter or the result of structural gender inequality; the film gives no answers but turns the predicament itself into courage to go on. The protagonist Zhang Xin fights with the mother who lives entirely for her and loses patience with her child, and these moral lapses are not prettified.

It had its world premiere on 19 July 2026 at the 20th FIRST International Film Festival, in the main competition, where it won best narrative feature.
honors: 入选｜2026 Golden Rooster Film Screening · 国产新片展映

gr26-017.title: Steadfast Woman
gr26-017.syn: After an abusive marriage, a single mother running a restaurant seeks independence amid prejudice and complicated new relationships.
gr26-017.bio: Zhang Pu is a director and screenwriter from Huairen, Shanxi, who graduated from the directing department of the Central Academy of Drama and is known for rural subjects and ordinary people. Steadfast Woman is the second part of his 'hometown trilogy' and began shooting together with the web series The Second Boss.
highlights: Shot in Huairen and Datong, Shanxi, with an 1980s 'Beixin Town' street built for it.
A 104-day shoot across summer, autumn and winter.
Second part of Zhang Pu's hometown trilogy.
Focuses on the growth of an ordinary woman bound by tradition.
gr26-017.st:
Shooting began on 26 August 2025 in Huairen, Shanxi, and lasted 104 days across summer, autumn and winter. The crew shot in Huairen and Datong and built an 1980s 'Beixin Town' street to recreate everyday life in Shanxi's coal-mining years. Zhang says he has met many women like Chunxia, bound by tradition and still carrying on after breakdown, and wanted to record this strength of ordinary people.

Xu Yueqing plays Chunxia, with Wang Chengyang, Wang Gongliang and Wei Chunguang among the cast; one actor says that for a long take of pressing bean noodles, she, not used to housework, relied on the director's hands-on guidance from his familiarity with northern rural life. On set the director encouraged improvised exchanges between actors.

Ma Jingjing is chief producer. The film was selected for the 2026 Golden Rooster domestic showcase and held a special screening in Xiamen.

gr26-018.title: Light Pillar
gr26-018.syn: A lonely caretaker in a fading film studio receives a VR headset in place of wages and discovers unexpected companionship.
gr26-018.bio: Xu Zao is a director and screenwriter. Light Pillar is his first animated feature, produced and starred in by Dong Chengpeng (Da Peng) and combining animation and live action; it won him the Fei Mu Honour Best Director award at the 10th Pingyao International Film Festival.
highlights: Animation and live action inverted: live action for the virtual world, animation for reality.
Produced by and starring Da Peng; Xu Zao's first animated feature.
Selected for Berlin's Perspectives section.
Won the Fei Mu Honour Best Director award at Pingyao.
gr26-018.st:
Set in a future winter, the film follows Lao Cha, a reclusive cleaner at a film studio lot whose only companion is a stray cat. Given a VR headset in lieu of wages, he enters a virtual world called 'Happy Home', where he makes new friends. The film inverts reality and the virtual: live action depicts the illusory world and animation the real one, heightening the contrast between them.

Xu has said old films are 'vanishing' but stories go on; 'what is past is prologue' is his view of creation. He says only after winning could he finally call himself a director with confidence.

The film appeared in the Perspectives section of the 76th Berlin International Film Festival in 2026 and had its Asian premiere in September at the 10th Pingyao International Film Festival.
gr26-018.editorial: An animation about loneliness, virtual companionship and old films, formally fresh and quiet in rhythm, for viewers who like experimental storytelling.

gr26-019.title: MGP: The Untamed Circuit
gr26-019.syn: A documentary follows drivers and the Macau Grand Prix, exploring the preparation, competition and human stories behind the races.
gr26-019.bio: Cao Jinling directed Macau Grand Prix, the first documentary feature to record both the front and back of the Macau Grand Prix, jointly produced by Ningbo Gaoting Pictures and Macau Xicai Culture. She has said it was her first time filming motor racing.
highlights: The first documentary feature to record both sides of the Macau Grand Prix.
Built on the 72nd race while tracing 72 years of history and archives.
Records pre-race customs of lion dances and offerings of roast pig.
Selected for China's National Film Archive Project; stars China's first F1 driver Ma Qinghua.
gr26-019.st:
Built around the 72nd Macau Grand Prix in 2025, the film follows drivers from around the world as they come to the 6.12-km Guia street circuit, prepare and race, while looking back at legendary early drivers and event staff and weaving in rare archival material to trace 72 editions of the race. Shot across Europe and Asia, it features Ma Qinghua, China's first Formula 1 driver.

It also records the race's folk traditions: before each Grand Prix, Mr Pan of the Macau Lo Leong sports association consults an almanac for an auspicious time, dots the eyes of lions and offers a roast pig to pray for the drivers' safety; the crew also met an old neighbour who came to a model shop daily and said the cars were for himself. The director says that motor racing is a Western sport but blends perfectly with Eastern civilisation.

Selected for China's National Film Archive Project and supported by several Macau government bodies and the Automobile General Association Macau-China, it had its world first screening at the Golden Rooster festival on 7 November 2026 and will open in Macau during the 73rd Grand Prix, 19–22 November.

gr26-020.title: No Hard Feelings
gr26-020.syn: A struggling ride-hailing driver and a saleswoman connect over the telephone, entangling their invented identities and hopes.
gr26-020.bio: Liu Shichuan graduated in cinematography from the Communication University of China and worked as a cinematographer; Best Condition is his feature as director, co-written with Bao Erjinna. It had its world premiere at the Shanghai International Film Festival under the title The Man Without Desire / No Hard Feelings, in the Golden Goblet Asian New Talent selection.
highlights: Premiered at Shanghai as The Man Without Desire, renamed Best Condition for the Golden Rooster festival.
Starring Zu Feng and Wang Ju, a black light comedy about male sexual dysfunction and a supplement scam.
Two strangers meet through a follow-up phone call.
In the 2026 Shanghai Golden Goblet Asian New Talent selection.
gr26-020.st:
At the Shanghai festival it was shown as The Man Without Desire, and at the Golden Rooster festival the title became Best Condition, with the English title No Hard Feelings throughout. Zu Feng plays Li Songyuan, a divorced, unemployed ride-hailing driver who in desperation over male sexual dysfunction falls into a health-supplement scam; Wang Ju plays someone who invents an identity within supplement sales. The festival describes it as a gentle light comedy about desire and dignity, taking male intimate illness as its way in with black humour as its tone.

Two strangers stuck in life's mire meet through a follow-up call: one puts a literary dream into a podcast, the other lives on a made-up identity; they draw closer and confide in each other, moving through lies and expectations toward an unavoidable reality. It runs about 116 minutes, supervised by Xu Lei with Zhao Jing as chief producer, and also features Huang Xiaolei, Zhang Zixian, Zhang Baiqiao and Huang Ziqi.

It premiered at the Shanghai International Film Festival in June 2026 and reached the Golden Rooster domestic film showcase in November.

gr26-021.title: A Girl Unknown
gr26-021.syn: A girl's upbringing links three families, raising questions about blood ties, care, identity and women's place in society.
gr26-021.bio: Zou Jing, born in 1984, worked in documentary direction and editing at Shanghai Television before her debut short Lili Alone was selected for Cannes Critics' Week in 2021 and won the Discovery Prize. A Girl Unknown is her first feature, a China–France co-production registered by Emei Film Group, Xiamen Xixi Pictures' Shanghai branch and France's Maneki Films.
highlights: Selected for the 2026 Cannes Critics' Week feature competition, also eligible for the Caméra d'Or.
Script won the Next Step prize at Cannes Critics' Week in 2024.
Starring Li Gengxi: one girl, three names, three families.
Zou Jing's first feature, a China–France co-production; closing film of the Golden Rooster festival.
gr26-021.st:
Zou Jing's own grandmother was given up for adoption, and before writing she interviewed several women with similar experiences and drew on news reports; the script took nearly four years from 2021, though the story itself is fictional. Li Gengxi's Juan passes through three adoptive families and three names, and the film uses this drifting life to ask about identity and belonging, ending with the renaming as a new beginning. Shen Jiani, Zu Feng and Cao Ruofan also appear.

The script won the Next Step feature screenplay workshop prize at Cannes Critics' Week in May 2024, reportedly the first Chinese-language script to win it, and was selected for Shanghai's 'young director recommendation' project that year; Pyramide holds international sales and French distribution. The film was registered in March 2025 and began shooting on 21 April.

In April 2026 it was selected for the Cannes Critics' Week feature competition of the 79th festival, automatically eligible for the Caméra d'Or, and is the first Sichuan-produced film selected for Cannes. It closes the 2026 Golden Rooster festival.
honors: 入选｜2026 Golden Rooster Film Screening · 国产新片展映

gr26-022.title: Algerican Road
gr26-022.syn: After a truck is stolen in the Sahara, an elderly driver and a porter encounter travelers who come to their aid.
gr26-022.bio: Rabah Ameur-Zaïmeche is a French director whose family has an Algerian migration history, though he resists letting that identity set the limits of what he is allowed to film. His features include the debut Wesh Wesh, qu'est-ce qui se passe?, Histoire de Judas, Les Chants de Mandrin, Dernier maquis and Terminal Sud, which premiered in Locarno in 2019. Algerican Road is his eighth feature; it opened FIDMarseille in 2026, which also gave him a retrospective of all his features.
highlights: Opening film of FIDMarseille 2026; the director's eighth feature.
Two truckers left without their truck are rescued on a Sahara road.
Press Prize at the Fameck Arab Film Festival.
A France-Algeria-Saudi Arabia-Qatar co-production.
gr26-022.st:
The film opened FIDMarseille in July 2026 as an international premiere. A co-production of France, Algeria, Saudi Arabia and Qatar, it received Red Sea Fund support. It is set in southern Algeria: Slimane (Slimane Dazi), an exhausted and ill old trucker, and his loader Smaïn (the director's brother Smaïl Ameur-Zaïmeche) must carry a cargo deep into the Sahara. They are attacked and their truck is stolen, then helped by a young researcher, Anna (Liah O'Prey), and her travelling companion Sofiane.

Writing on his work, Algeria's El Watan stresses that his images hold several worlds in a single shot, with religious narratives and migration history present but not reduced to labels of identity; another reviewer notes that his characters tend to care for and rescue before trying to solve anything.

The film won the Press Prize at the 2026 Fameck Arab Film Festival, with a press jury chaired by critic Charles Tesson; it opens in France on 16 December 2026 via Les Alchimistes.
honors: 入选｜2026 Golden Rooster Film Screening · 此刻：国际新片展映
gr26-022.editorial: A slow road film about desert, exhausted bodies and strangers helping each other. Do not expect road-movie thrills; it rewards patience with people and landscape.

gr26-023.title: Les Misérables
gr26-023.syn: Jean Valjean seeks redemption while pursued by Inspector Javert, linking a personal promise to the struggles of a turbulent age.
gr26-023.bio: Fred Cavayé is a French genre director known for tightly paced action and thrillers, including Mea Culpa. Les Misérables is his first take on a French literary classic, which he wrote and directed for StudioCanal, reportedly on a budget above €30 million.
highlights: World premiere in San Sebastián's official selection; a near-three-hour French production.
Lindon as Valjean and Rahim as Javert; their confrontation is the film's centre.
Opens with a young Valjean in prison and reimagines Javert as an orphanage child criminal.
Gives more weight to female characters such as Fantine and Madame Thénardier.
gr26-023.st:
The film had its world premiere in the official selection at San Sebastián in September 2026 and opened in France on 14 October, running about 2 hours 56 minutes. Vincent Lindon plays Jean Valjean, Tahar Rahim Javert, Noémie Merlant Fantine, with Camille Cottin and Benjamin Lavernhe as the Thénardiers.

It does not begin with the adult Valjean: it opens with the young Valjean in prison and Lindon takes over much later, while Javert is reimagined as a child criminal abandoned by his mother and sent to an orphanage. Rahim said at San Sebastián that he read the novel only for the project and stressed that it is an adaptation, not a remake; Cavayé's stated aim is to restore characters and nuances earlier versions dropped and give the female characters more narrative weight.

Reception is mixed: many critics praise the cast, spectacle and pace, but some French reviews find it too faithful and cautious, lacking the novel's anger. AlloCiné's press average is about 3.1 out of 5 against about 4 from audiences, and it opened at number one in France, though with far fewer admissions than The Count of Monte Cristo.
gr26-023.editorial: A classical big-screen production for those who love Hugo's story and can commit to nearly three hours. Readers of the novel can watch for what was changed; newcomers can follow it easily.
warnings: War, conflict or threat of war
gr26-023.contentNote: Available story information indicates: Financial hardship or exploitation; Confinement or displacement; War, conflict or threat of war. Detailed depiction and intensity have not been verified; consider your individual needs.

gr26-024.title: Love Massacre
gr26-024.syn: A student in the United States becomes caught in a dangerous web of love, suspicion and violence.
gr26-024.bio: Patrick Tam is a leading Hong Kong New Wave director, coming from television, with a strong visual style and a focus on psychology and atmosphere. Love Massacre was written by his long-time television collaborator Joyce Chan, and scholars have traced a line of Hong Kong film aesthetics from Patrick Tam to Wong Kar-wai.
highlights: A key Hong Kong New Wave work shifting between drama, romance and thriller.
Starring Brigitte Lin, set in San Francisco.
Empty cityscapes and colour design mirror the characters' psychology.
Written by Patrick Tam's long-time collaborator Joyce Chan.
gr26-024.st:
Set in San Francisco, the film follows college student Ivy (Brigitte Lin), who tries to help her heartbroken, delirious friend Joy (Tina Liu) and gets drawn into a relationship with Joy's brother Chu Chung (Chang Kuo-chu), only to learn he is married; suffering from a hereditary mental illness, he gradually turns violent. The film shifts among drama, romance, thriller and slasher, blending elements of European art cinema and American thrillers, and is a visually striking, unsettling work of the Hong Kong New Wave.

Almost empty streets, parks and even an amusement park create a vacuum-like, lonely city in which the characters' psychology and surroundings echo each other; colour also marks relationships, for example Ivy and another character wear blue in shared scenes, and as her romantic feelings fade the blue leaves her wardrobe and is replaced by fear. Photography is by Brian Lai.

It was released in 1981 and has recently been shown in restored form at festivals abroad.
honors: 入选｜2026 Golden Rooster Film Screening · 功夫·功夫：华语经典展映
gr26-024.editorial: A New Wave thriller in which atmosphere and visuals outweigh plot. The second half contains violence, so check the content notes.
gr26-024.contentNote: Available story information indicates: Violence or injury; Relationship conflict or coercion. Detailed depiction and intensity have not been verified; consider your individual needs.

gr26-025.title: Everytime
gr26-025.syn: A year after a teenage girl's death, her mother, sister and boyfriend attempt a family holiday shadowed by grief and blame.
gr26-025.bio: Sandra Wollner was born in Leoben, Austria, in 1983, and is a director and screenwriter. Her second feature The Trouble with Being Born (2020) premiered at the Berlinale and was controversial for its subject of robots and children. Everytime is her third feature and her first at Cannes, where it won the top prize of Un Certain Regard; Variety called it the most refined and inventive formal statement in the section. Both films deal with loss, but Screen Daily notes this one is unlikely to present the same challenges for distributors.
highlights: Top prize of Cannes Un Certain Regard, then three more awards at Sarajevo, Gent and Valladolid, and Germany's pick for the Oscar race.
In the first 15 minutes a night out ends in tragedy; after that the film gives emotion few outlets and simply watches the family go on.
Birgit Minichmayr's mother is the centre, and the press called her performance layered.
A daring conceptual turn near the end folds present and past into each other, and is what critics talk about most.
gr26-025.st:
Everytime had its world premiere on 18 May 2026 in the Un Certain Regard section at Cannes, where it won the section's top prize, the Un Certain Regard Award; it then won the Heart of Sarajevo for Best Film at Sarajevo, the Explore Award at Film Fest Gent and the Miguel Delibes Award for Best Screenplay at Valladolid. Germany has reportedly selected it for the Oscar race for Best International Feature.

The story begins fast. A Berlin family, teenage Jessie, her mother Ella and her sister Melli, are about to go on holiday in Tenerife when Jessie sneaks out for a night of partying with her boyfriend, and tragedy follows within the first 15 minutes. The film then watches how mother, sister and boyfriend go on living with loss and guilt. Screen Daily says it does not ease the audience in gradually; Variety says it lifts low-key domestic portraiture towards a big-swing, conceptually daring finale; and The Wrap calls Birgit Minichmayr's performance magnificently layered.

Produced by Panama Film and The Barricades, shot by Gregory Oke, it runs 121 minutes. Critics are not unanimous: The Hollywood Reporter thinks its best moments come a bit late.
gr26-025.editorial: A family drama of grief that asks for patience. Don't rush for answers; watch the separate losses of mother, sister and boyfriend, and the bold late move that folds present into past. It runs two hours, so allow the time.
gr26-025.contentNote: Available story information indicates: Death and bereavement. Detailed depiction and intensity have not been verified; consider your individual needs.

gr26-026.title: Her First Taste
gr26-026.syn: Around the turn of the millennium, a literary-minded teenager in Hangzhou navigates family change, first feelings and misunderstandings.
gr26-026.bio: Gong Yiwen, born in the 1990s, made Her First Taste as her first feature. She went to study in the US at 17 and returned to work in film after her bachelor's degree; the project was selected for the Shanghai festival's work-in-progress section in 2023 and won the work-in-progress grand prize at the 23rd Hong Kong–Asia Film Financing Forum.
highlights: Best Film and Best Actress in the 2026 Shanghai Golden Goblet Asian New Talent section.
Growing up in Hangzhou around 2000, with non-professional actors and documentary-style camerawork.
Won the work-in-progress grand prize at the 23rd Hong Kong–Asia Film Financing Forum.
In the Warsaw Film Festival's international competition.
gr26-026.st:
Set in Hangzhou around the turn of the millennium, the film follows high-school girl Wen Yuwen, who loves writing, as she repeatedly draws close to and misses connection with online friends, classmates, family and her own emotional world. Gong says part of it is her own experience and part comes from people around her, mostly fiction; the school and her hometown Shengzhou were fixed in the script, and the opening market, Yan'an Road bookstore and Qingchun Road snack shop are her personal memories of Hangzhou.

The director cast non-professionals close to the characters' ages and asked them to learn the script and then step outside it, speaking in their own natural way; with documentary-style camerawork and restrained acting, the film captures the girl's complicated feelings about body, family and identity, which a critic describes as youth that is 'meaningless but interesting'. It stars Ma Fufu, Liu Haoning and Zhong Mei.

In June 2026 it won Best Film and Best Actress (Ma Fufu) in the Golden Goblet Asian New Talent section of the 28th Shanghai International Film Festival, and had its international premiere in the Warsaw Film Festival's international competition on 9 October.
