In his Directors' Fortnight interview Petzold admits it is a ghost story and another variation on Hitchcock's Vertigo.

Shooting began in August 2024 with long-time collaborator Hans Fromm behind the camera. The film had its world premiere on 17 May 2025 in the Directors' Fortnight at the 78th Cannes Film Festival and then played the New York Film Festival and the Viennale. Reverse Shot's review calls it Petzold's softest film to date: its slipperiness comes not from the unknown, as in Phoenix or Transit, but from the unacknowledged.
miroirs-no-3.editorial: For fans of Petzold, European art cinema and psychological suspense. Watch the mirroring between characters: who stands in for whom, who is seen by whom. The pace is restrained and little is explained, so viewers fill in the gaps themselves.
miroirs-no-3.contentNote: Available story information indicates: Dangerous situations or accidents; Psychological distress or uncertainty; Family conflict or separation. Detailed depiction and intensity have not been verified; consider your individual needs.

the-miserable-mother.title: The Miserable Mother
the-miserable-mother.syn: A young mother trapped by housework, a Peter Pan-like boyfriend who never grows up, and a newborn baby. Fairies descend, the baby speaks, an angel appears: surreal, fantastical elements arrive one after another in song and dance. The film blends the aesthetic language of classic musicals, with the dreamy palette of Jacques Demy's The Umbrellas of Cherbourg and the bold borrowing of soap-opera structure from Chantal Akerman's Golden Eighties. Director Susanne Heinrich weaves in the language of contemporary social media for a dazzling modern musical spectacle. Beneath the singing and dancing lies a mother's inner journey to find her own boundaries.
honors: 获奖｜2026 Munich Film Festival · German Cinema New Talent Award, Best Screenplay
获奖｜2026 Shanghai International Film Festival · Golden Goblet, Outstanding Artistic Achievement
获奖｜2026 Palić Film Festival · International Competition, Special Mention
highlights: A musical about new motherhood that turns childcare, the division of labour at home and society's expectations of the 'good mother' into things that can be sung and danced.
The second part of the trilogy on female subjectivity, continuing the questions about women under late capitalism raised in Aren't You Happy?
The director also writes the lyrics; the music was made with Willi Sieger and others, and the songs and physical performance carry much of the narrative.
It won the Outstanding Artistic Achievement award at the Shanghai International Film Festival and Best Screenplay at Munich's German Cinema New Talent Awards.
the-miserable-mother.bio: Susanne Heinrich was born in Leipzig in 1985 and is director, writer and one of the film's songwriters. Her first feature, Das melancholische Mädchen (Aren't You Happy?, 2019), premiered at the Max Ophüls Prize festival and won Best Film. The Miserable Mother is the second part of her trilogy on female subjectivity, which looks at the condition of womanhood in late capitalism; the third part, The Outdated Woman, is in development.
the-miserable-mother.st:
The film is a musical: a woman who has just given birth is shut in by her own four walls, and the boundaries between inside and outside, society and individual, body and discourse begin to blur. Her partner 'Peter Pan' (Theo Colarusso) does his best to 'help' but keeps dodging her anger, literally dancing around it. Newcomer Rosa Landers plays the Mother in her biggest role to date.

It was shot in Leipzig from 11 June to 17 July 2024, with cinematography by Agnesh Pakozdi and music by Willi Sieger, produced by reynard films (Leipzig) with Coproduction Office, and runs 81 minutes. Screen Daily calls it a wry, sincere study of new motherhood, with a keen sense of fury, awe and mischief.

In 2026 it won Best Screenplay in the German Cinema New Talent strand at the Munich Film Festival and the Outstanding Artistic Achievement award in the Golden Goblet competition at the Shanghai International Film Festival, as well as a Special Mention in the International Competition at the Palić European Film Festival.
the-miserable-mother.editorial: For viewers who like formal experiment, feminism and musicals. Treat the songs as dialogue: they are both self-mockery and a rebuttal of how a mother 'should' be. The style is exaggerated, funny and sharp, and does not aim at realism.
the-miserable-mother.contentNote: Available story information indicates: Family conflict or separation; Discrimination or abuse of power; Relationship conflict or coercion. Detailed depiction and intensity have not been verified; consider your individual needs.

oh-this-unspeakable-void.title: Oh This Unspeakable Void
oh-this-unspeakable-void.syn: At twenty, Joachim is unexpectedly accepted into the renowned acting school in Munich and moves into the villa of his grandparents, Inge and Hermann. Between the bizarre challenges of drama school and his grandparents' eccentric, mostly alcohol-fuelled rituals, Joachim tries to find his place in the world, without knowing what role he actually plays in it.
honors: 获奖｜2026 German Film Awards · Best Film, 2nd Runner-up (Bronze)
获奖｜2026 German Film Awards · Best Actress (Senta Berger)
获奖｜2026 German Film Awards · Best Supporting Actor (Michael Wittenborn)
highlights: Adapted from Meyerhoff's autobiographical bestseller, it blends the oddities of drama-school life with warmth between grandparents and grandson.
Mother and son on one project: director Simon Verhoeven cast his own mother, Senta Berger, as the grandmother, and at 85 she won her first German Film Award for Best Actress.
A strong ensemble including Karoline Herfurth, Tom Schilling, Laura Tonke and Friedrich von Thun.
The Süddeutsche Zeitung called it a light-handed heavy literary adaptation; Filmstarts called it the funniest German film in years.
oh-this-unspeakable-void.bio: Simon Verhoeven was born in Munich in 1972, the son of actress Senta Berger and director Michael Verhoeven (who died in April 2024). He established himself with the comedies Männerherzen and Willkommen bei den Hartmanns (2016), the latter one of Germany's biggest recent box-office hits, followed by Alter weißer Mann (2022) and Girl You Know It's True (2023), about Milli Vanilli. Oh, This Unspeakable Void is adapted from Joachim Meyerhoff's autobiographical bestseller, co-written with Lars Hubrich; the grandmother is played by his own mother, Senta Berger.
oh-this-unspeakable-void.st:
The film is adapted from Joachim Meyerhoff's 2015 novel of the same name, the third volume of his cycle Alle Toten fliegen hoch. Twenty-year-old Joachim (Bruno Alexander) is unexpectedly accepted at Munich's renowned Otto Falckenberg School of the Performing Arts and moves into his grandparents' villa in Munich, facing the odd methods of acting training while living with a grandmother (Senta Berger) and grandfather of strong character. The cycle's second volume has already been filmed.

It was shot in Munich, Cologne and Berlin, runs 137 minutes and opened in Germany on 29 January 2026, with Karoline Herfurth, Tom Schilling, Laura Tonke and others in the cast. The Süddeutsche Zeitung called it a light-handed heavy literary adaptation, and Filmstarts called it the funniest German film in years.

It received seven nominations at the 2026 German Film Awards and won three: Outstanding Feature Film (Bronze), Best Actress for Senta Berger, who won her first German Film Award at 85, and Best Supporting Actor for Michael Wittenborn.
oh-this-unspeakable-void.editorial: For viewers who like literary adaptations, coming-of-age comedies and stories about acting. Watch the grandmother: she is the funniest and heaviest part of the film, and behind the jokes is a repeated return to the gap of the title. It runs 137 minutes at a relaxed pace.
oh-this-unspeakable-void.contentNote: Available story information indicates: Alcohol use; Family conflict or separation. Detailed depiction and intensity have not been verified; consider your individual needs.

sometimes-i-imagine-them-all-at-a-party.title: Sometimes, I Imagine Them All at a Party
sometimes-i-imagine-them-all-at-a-party.syn: Fourteen years ago, filmmaker Daniela Magnani Hüller survived an attempted femicide. Now she revisits the key moments of that period of her life. Travelling back and forth between Munich and Rio de Janeiro, she seeks out some of the people who were around her at the time and asks the questions that have haunted her for years. Carefully composed images sketch a complex picture of everything she went through.
honors: 获奖｜2026 Berlin International Film Festival · Forum, Berlinale Documentary Award Jury Special Mention
获奖｜2026 DOK.fest München · Student Award
highlights: The director draws on her own experience, refuses pity and asks who bears responsibility, placing a seemingly private event back within the justice system and society.
The film has both a factual strand and a felt one: conversations with police, doctor and teacher, and tactile imagery of dolls and butterflies.
In the Brazil chapters she reunites with her half-sister, and the shift in colour and rhythm lets the film breathe.
It won a Special Mention for the Berlinale Documentary Award, and Cineuropa called it a formally complex, sensitive and unflinchingly direct autobiographical film.
sometimes-i-imagine-them-all-at-a-party.st:
The film is an autobiographical documentary: in her last year of high school, years ago, the director was subjected to harassment, stalking and threats by a classmate and finally survived a knife attack. Years later she returns to the people involved at the time, including a policewoman, a doctor, a teacher, a schoolmate and the school's legal expert who accompanied her to court, to ask them questions again, and examines how the justice system works and where it fails to protect victims of violence. The factual strand is shot in high-resolution digital with tactile imagery woven in; when she travels to Brazil to reunite with her half-sister, grey Munich gives way to vibrant Rio and lush nature, implying a rebirth, or at least an attempt at one.

In her director's statement she says she believes one can go on living without bitterness after violence, but with an appropriate and perhaps necessary anger. The film is produced by Bildersturm Filmproduktion with ZDF Das kleine Fernsehspiel; producer Birgit Schulz, cinematographer Noah Böhm, editor Melanie Jilg.

It had its world premiere on 15 February 2026 in the Forum of the 76th Berlinale, where it shared a Special Mention for the Berlinale Documentary Award; in May it won the megaherz Student Award at DOK.fest München and opened in German cinemas on 14 May.
sometimes-i-imagine-them-all-at-a-party.editorial: The film's subject is a real act of violence, lived by the director and told in the film; it is emotionally heavy, so please consider your own circumstances before watching. For viewers concerned with gender-based violence, the justice system and self-narration. The pace is calm; watch how tenderness and anger coexist in the images.
warnings: Violence against women or domestic abuse
sometimes-i-imagine-them-all-at-a-party.contentNote: Available story information indicates: Violence against women or domestic abuse; Emotional distress or trauma. Detailed depiction and intensity have not been verified; consider your individual needs.
sometimes-i-imagine-them-all-at-a-party.bio: Daniela Magnani Hüller was born in Munich in 1995 and is a German-Brazilian filmmaker. After a bachelor's degree in media and communication she began studying documentary directing at the University of Television and Film Munich (HFF) in 2019, making several self-written, self-directed and self-edited shorts including Frei sein (2020), Atide and Driving Force (2022), Arthrocalypse (2023) and Rauswachsen (2024), and won the DOK.talent Award at DOK.fest München in 2023. Sometimes, I Imagine Them All at a Party is her autobiographical documentary feature debut, in which she returns to an attempted femicide she survived at 17.

when-pigs-fly.title: When Pigs Fly
when-pigs-fly.syn: Is my heart a part of me? Does it share my experiences? Or is it merely a lump of flesh, a muscle, a pump, an organ easily replaced by another? In our society, pigs are only considered valuable once they are dead, even though they are so similar to humans that their hearts can be used as donor organs. In a future in which hearts are grown in pigs to save human lives, the line between the two species begins to blur. Is this the moment to rethink the human–pig relationship? The film follows two veterinarians in their ambivalent relationship with pigs, and offers intimate access to an animal that is far closer to us than most people are willing to admit.
honors: 获奖｜2026 DOK.fest München · Audience Award
入围｜2026 DOK.fest München · Competition
入围｜2026 CPH:DOX
highlights: It starts from the seemingly simple question of what a pig is, and opens onto agriculture, pets, ethics and xenotransplantation.
Michael Kalb produced and the director also helped edit; it runs only 80 minutes.
Felix Riedelsheimer is the cinematographer, with sound by Philip Hutter.
It won the audience award at DOK.fest München, decided by audience votes.
when-pigs-fly.st:
Is a pig a farm animal, or something to cuddle? And if pig hearts can soon be transplanted into humans, what entirely new questions will that raise? The film starts from these questions; its working title was Ein Herz (A Heart), and it explores the most intimate and contradictory relationships between pigs and humans. The cinematographer is Felix Riedelsheimer, the editors are Melanie Jilg, Hauke von Stietencron and the director, the music is by Marja Burchard, and it is produced by Michael Kalb Filmproduktion. It runs 80 minutes in English and German.

It had its world premiere at CPH:DOX in Copenhagen on 14 March 2026 and its German premiere at DOK.fest München on 9 May, then won the kinokino Audience Award, sponsored by BR and 3sat. The award, worth 2,000 euros, is decided by audience members voting by QR code after each screening; the film led the audience ranking at one point during the festival.
when-pigs-fly.editorial: For viewers concerned with animal ethics, food and medicine. The film discusses pig farming and medical use and may include animal-related imagery whose intensity has not been verified; it is brisk at 80 minutes and suits viewers who come with questions.
when-pigs-fly.contentNote: Available story information indicates: Animal harm or death themes; Illness, treatment or care. Detailed depiction and intensity have not been verified; consider your individual needs.
when-pigs-fly.bio: Denise Riedmayr studied documentary directing at the University of Television and Film Munich (HFF) and works as a freelance filmmaker and as author, director and editor for Bayerischer Rundfunk. She received the City of Munich's Starter Film Award in 2021; her shorts include An Anna (2020) and, co-directed, Swim for Good (2018). When Pigs Fly continues her interest in lived experience and the relationship between humans and animals.

shame-and-money.title: Shame and Money
shame-and-money.syn: After losing their livelihood in the village, a Kosovar family is forced to move to the capital to find a place in a hyper-capitalist society. Shame and Money portrays hard-working people striving for a decent life under relentless pressure and long-term turmoil. Shaban, a traditional head of the household, longs to be the family's pillar, yet it is his mother's savings that keep them afloat. Accepting help from a wealthy brother-in-law brings new challenges. As his pride erodes and his dignity slips away, Shaban edges toward breaking point: how much more can he take?
honors: 获奖｜2026 Munich Film Festival · ARRI/OSRAM Award, Best International Film
获奖｜2026 Sundance Film Festival · World Cinema Dramatic, Grand Jury Prize
提名｜2026 Sydney Film Festival · Sydney Film Prize, Best Film
highlights: Sundance 2026 World Cinema Dramatic Grand Jury Prize; the jury praised the director's deep empathy for his characters at a crucial moment when they are beginning again.
RogerEbert.com called it austere yet hard-hitting, revealing the apathy of a system without melodramatic speeches.
A co-production of six countries, Germany, Kosovo, Slovenia, Albania, North Macedonia and Belgium: a typical Balkan co-produced drama.
Written with Doruntina Basha, it continues Morina's attention to Kosovar society and migration from Babai and Exile.
shame-and-money.bio: Visar Morina was born in Pristina, Kosovo, in 1979 when it was still part of Yugoslavia, and has lived and worked in Germany since 1993. His debut feature Babai (Father) won Best Director at the Karlovy Vary International Film Festival in 2015; his second, Exile (2020), was nominated for the World Cinema Dramatic Grand Jury Prize at Sundance, its script having won the German Screenplay Award in 2018. Shame and Money is his third feature and his second in Sundance's World Cinema competition, where this time he won the Grand Jury Prize. He co-wrote with Doruntina Basha and is also one of the producers.
shame-and-money.st:
The film follows Shaban (Astrit Kabashi) and Hatixhe (Flonja Kodheli), a middle-aged couple from the Kosovar countryside. After a man named Liridon steals their money and disappears, the family loses its livelihood and must move to the capital, Pristina, to find a place in a hyper-commodified city. With a restrained camera and unsentimental dialogue, Morina peels back, layer by layer, how a decent person loses dignity step by step under globalisation and late capitalism, so that the two words of the title, shame and money, pull against each other.

It is produced by Schuldenberg Films as a co-production of Germany, Kosovo, Slovenia, Albania, North Macedonia and Belgium, shot by Janis Mazuch, and runs 129 minutes.

It had its world premiere on 25 January 2026 in the World Cinema Dramatic Competition at Sundance, where Cineuropa called it an early critical standout of the section, and won the Grand Jury Prize. The jury praised his deep empathy for his characters at a crucial moment when they are beginning again. It later won the ARRI/OSRAM Award for Best International Film at the Munich Film Festival.
shame-and-money.editorial: For viewers concerned with migration, class and globalisation. Watch how the couple talk at each moment of forced compromise and how money gradually changes their sense of shame. It runs 129 minutes at a steady pace with a subdued mood.

gh63-001.syn: In 1990s Malaysia, a lonely boy named Kai follows his late mother's final wish and discovers a mysterious novel entitled The Age of Goodbyes. Through its pages, he enters the world of Du Li An, uncovering a story of love, disappearance, and family secrets that began in Ipoh in 1969. As Kai reads on, he begins to discover an unexpected connection between himself and the lives within the novel.

With the support of close friends, he begins confronting his addiction through self-awareness and openness. But even as he recognises its devastating cost, the grip of addiction continues to test his mind, his relationships, and his hope of reclaiming a healthy life.

gh63-050.title: Fjord
gh63-050.syn: The Gheorghius, a devout Romanian-Norwegian couple, resettle in a village set in a distant fjord where they become close to their neighbours, the Halbergs. Their children bond despite their different upbringings. When adolescent Elia Gheorghiu shows up at school with some bruises on her body, the community asks itself if the traditional education that the Gheorghiu children get from their parents might have anything to do with it.
gh63-050.editorial: A dispute over parenting drags out conflicts among immigration, faith and child protection. It's in no hurry to give answers, unfolding the ethical dilemma through its ensemble.

gh63-051.title: Wild Horse Nine
gh63-051.syn: Shortly before the 1973 Chilean coup, CIA agents Chris and Lee are sent from Santiago to Easter Island by their bureau chief, MJ. Amid the island's iconic statues, the longtime partners grapple with dark pasts and present conspiracies. When Chris forms an unexpected bond with two rebellious students, their mission begins to unravel, threatening to send everyone's stay in this remote paradise dangerously off course.
gh63-051.editorial: Two detectives feel each other out amid Chile's political undercurrents. You'll enjoy it if you like sharp dialogue, black humour and unreliable partners.
gh63-051.contentNote: Story information indicates: War and historical trauma; Murder and violence. Compiled from the synopsis and public information; detailed depiction and intensity have not been verified, so please consider your individual needs.

gh63-052.title: Bucking Fastard
gh63-052.syn: Sisters Jean and Joan Holbrooke are inseparable: they speak in unison, share the same dreams, and fall in love with the same man. Living entirely by their own social and emotional rules, they eventually end up in court and attracts intense media scrutiny. Seeking refuge from the trial and their heartbreak, the sisters embark on a journey together, confronting a world that struggles to understand them.
gh63-052.editorial: Two sisters acting almost in lockstep push closeness to an unsettling edge. Worth a look for fans of Herzog's obsessive characters and reality–fantasy storytelling.
gh63-052.contentNote: Story information indicates: Psychological trauma and distress; Imprisonment and legal pressure. Compiled from the synopsis and public information; detailed depiction and intensity have not been verified, so please consider your individual needs.
gh63-052.bio: Werner Herzog works across fiction and documentary. Aguirre, Fitzcarraldo and Grizzly Man follow people driven towards extraordinary extremes.

gh63-053.title: The Wizard of the Kremlin
gh63-053.syn: In the aftermath of the Soviet Union's collapse, Vadim Baranov rises from avant-garde artist to the unofficial advisor of a former KGB agent destined to become Vladimir Putin. As the spin doctor behind a new Russia, he shapes power through image and illusion, yet finds himself drawn to the elusive Ksenia. Years later, Baranov recounts a story where truth, fiction, and political strategy become inseparable.
gh63-053.editorial: From the position of a spin doctor, see how the myth of power gets made. For those interested in media, political performance and post-Soviet history.
gh63-053.contentNote: Story information indicates: Political oppression; War and historical trauma. Compiled from the synopsis and public information; detailed depiction and intensity have not been verified, so please consider your individual needs.
gh63-053.bio: Olivier Assayas's films include Irma Vep, Clouds of Sils Maria and Personal Shopper, moving between identities, image culture and international settings.

gh63-054.title: Orange-Flavoured Wedding
gh63-054.syn: The Puig family has seven children, and today is the wedding of the youngest, Jacques. It is March 1978 in the suburbs of Nantes. The father is not attending the wedding, as he has been banished from the family. The brothers and sisters, however, are all there, happy to be reunited. Jacques is marrying Martine, a love match for them both. But can love heal the wounds of childhood?
gh63-054.editorial: One wedding banquet slowly opens three generations' old wounds. Watch the choreography and dialogue rhythm of a large ensemble, and the family power beneath the festivity.
gh63-054.contentNote: Story information indicates: Domestic violence and abuse; Death and grief; Family conflict. Compiled from the synopsis and public information; detailed depiction and intensity have not been verified, so please consider your individual needs.

gh63-055.title: Gentle Monster
gh63-055.syn: Lucy, a concert pianist, has relocated her family from the city to a country house, hoping to ease her husband Philip's severe burnout. Before they can settle into their new home, an early morning police visit tears their world apart. Isolated and desperate to protect her young son, Lucy must face the situation alone, trapped between the man she loves and the fear of what he may have done.
gh63-055.editorial: The camera stays with a family shaken by a criminal accusation. Rewarding if you value performance and psychological detail. The subject involves harm to a child, so read the content notes first.

gh63-057.title: Diary of a Mad Old Man
gh63-057.syn: Recovering from a stroke, 69-year-old widower Utsugi is confined to his home and dependent on his daughter-in-law Susu for care. As his desire for her intensifies, he begins interpreting her kindness as sexual invitation. Their increasingly charged encounters blur the boundaries between seduction and delusion, intimacy and manipulation, revealing a profound longing for human connection beneath Utsugi's obsession.

gh63-068.title: Rehearsals for a Revolution
gh63-068.syn: Through five portraits of relatives and mentors, five expressions of resistance, Pegah Ahangarani sketches her life story. Drawing from personal archives, home videos, protest footage, newspapers, and recorded voices, she retraces 40 years of Iran's history. From the early days of 1979 until the war that began in 2026, she pieces together intimate and collective memories, forming the portrait of a country shaped by political repression and in constant hope for revolution.
gh63-068.editorial: Private archives re-thread forty years of political change. Across five chapters, family experience and revolutionary memory speak to each other on different levels.

gh63-069.title: Yo (Love Is a Rebellious Bird)
gh63-069.syn: After the death of her beloved friend Yo, filmmaker Anna Fitch spends a decade building a one-third- scale replica of Yo's house, where memories and imagination intertwine. Blending intimate footage from Yo's final year with creative reimaginings of her remarkable life, the film celebrates a friendship that transcends age and death while exploring the power of artistic creation to transform grief into love.
gh63-069.editorial: Making miniature houses and puppets is a way of remembering a friend. For those who like handmade materials, intimate documentary and gentle imagination.

gh63-070.title: Silenced
gh63-070.syn: After #MeToo shattered the silence surrounding gendered violence, survivors found themselves facing a new threat as defamation laws were weaponised against those who spoke out. International human rights lawyer Jennifer Robinson follows high-profile legal battles across the world, exposing how the justice system is used to silence, discredit, and financially ruin survivors and the journalists reporting their stories.
gh63-070.editorial: Puts defamation law back into the reality of survivors speaking out. For those interested in public issues and legal mechanisms: the focus is who gets to speak and at what cost.

gh63-071.title: Wishful Thinking
gh63-071.syn: Julia, an ambitious game designer, and Charlie, a struggling musician, are striving to repair their volatile relationship. After attending a couples-therapy seminar run by mysterious twin healers, they discover that the state of their relationship has supernatural effects on the world around them. With earthquakes, the stock market, and entire nations at risk, Julia and Charlie must decide whether their passionate love can survive the resulting chaos.
gh63-071.editorial: A couple's emotions can change the world, turning lovers' quarrels into fantasy comedy. Split screens and long takes make the ups and downs of a relationship visible.

gh63-071.bio: Graham Parkes works in filmmaking and independent games and co-founded GoodbyeWorld Games. Wishful Thinking is his first fiction feature.

gh63-073.title: The End of It
gh63-073.syn: In a future where ageing has been cured and death is optional, Claire decides to end her life as she approaches her 250th birthday. As Claire embraces death as her final artistic act, she is forced to confront what it truly means to live, die, and create.

Between the violence and the growing threat of exile, there is little room for quiet awakenings.

gh63-080.title: The Unknown
gh63-080.syn: David Zimmerman is approaching 40 and works as a photographer, though no one knows it. A recluse who rarely leaves home, he is dragged by friends to a wild party, where a mysterious woman catches his eye. Unable to look away, David follows her. Hours later, he wakes to discover that his life has changed completely: he is now in the woman's body.
gh63-080.editorial: A swap of identities makes watching others and knowing yourself unstable. For city-wandering, gender imagination and fantasy mystery, watch the shifts of viewpoint.

gh63-080.bio: Arthur Harari directed Onoda: 10,000 Nights in the Jungle and co-wrote Anatomy of a Fall with Justine Triet.

gh63-082.title: Vertiginous
gh63-082.syn: Jacques visits his friend Bruno with startling news: humanity may actually be living in a simulation. Bruno takes the idea seriously and begins searching for glitches in reality. As increasingly bizarre phenomena emerge around them, their ordinary world starts to unravel, raising the biggest questions about existence in a universe where seemingly anything can happen.
gh63-082.editorial: Crude computer-simulation visuals turn daily life into a glitching world. You'll enjoy it if you accept absurd logic and find your laughs in visual dislocation.

gh63-083.title: Elephants in the Fog
gh63-083.syn: In a remote Nepalese village deep in the forest, Pirati leads a house of Kinnar women, an ancient third- gender community revered and feared for their power to bless or curse. When one of her daughters disappears during a nightly elephant patrol and the police show little interest, Pirati investigates on her own, uncovering dangerous tensions that force her to choose between love and her beloved community...

But as developers threaten the village's sacred spring, Bayu must confront family tensions and his own past to protect his community.

As she grows closer to the more confident Theint, unspoken desires emerge between them in a society where love between women remains unacceptable.

Wishing for his parents, who live apart and do not speak to each other, to reconcile, his fear of losing connection to his loved ones forces Ninh to face life's unpredictable rhythms.

With her father relying on her account to clear his name, she begins searching for the truth, uncovering exploitation, deception, and her family's complicity.

gh63-090.title: The World Before
gh63-090.syn: Seventeen-year-old Jin has never left the remote island where she was born. When her childhood friend Dujae returns for his grandmother's funeral, she begins finding excuses to visit him, and their reunion gradually becomes part of her everyday life. As summer passes, the familiar roads, sea, and faces around her begin to feel different, prompting Jin to see both her island home and herself anew.

gh63-092.title: Mr. Nelson, Did You Kill People?
gh63-092.syn: Born into poverty in New York, Allen Nelson joins the Marine Corps at 18 and is sent to Vietnam, where the brutal realities of combat shatter his dreams of military glory. Returning home at 23, he is haunted by memories of the battlefield and struggles to reconnect with his family. As his life unravels, a psychiatrist at a veterans' hospital offers him a lifeline.
gh63-092.editorial: A veteran's memories carry war into postwar life. For followers of anti-war cinema; its violence and accounts of trauma call for preparation.

gh63-093.title: Children Untold
gh63-093.syn: In the ruins of post-war Tokyo, 12-year-old Kotoko loses her home and family and is left to survive alone. Realising that being a girl puts her in danger, she conceals her identity and lives as a boy, joining a group of orphaned children. As they struggle through the chaos and hardship of a shattered city, Kotoko discovers companionship, resilience, and the people willing to believe in their future.

gh63-094.title: Between Two Lovers
gh63-094.syn: Children's book author Uta has been married to Morio for three years, while continuing a relationship with her editor and lover, Junna. Unable to choose between them, nor to embrace the idea of having a child with Morio, Uta proposes an unconventional solution: the three of them should live together. Initially met with anger, her proposal takes an unexpected turn after an incident reshapes their relationship.

gh63-095.title: Fujiko
gh63-095.syn: Determined, combative, and indomitable, Fujiko is the kind of woman who scares men, especially in 1970s Japan. After enduring a tyrannical mother-in-law and a stormy divorce, she chooses to raise her daughter Mari as a single mother. Taking on a series of low-paying jobs before becoming an insurance saleswoman, Fujiko faces life's obstacles with humour, resilience, and grit, refusing to surrender to societal pressures.

gh63-096.title: In My Father's Room

Retracing his final days, she discovers a man seemingly left behind by society yet sustained by his devotion to words, the art of tea, and subtle beauty, gradually uncovering the quiet grace of his solitary world.
gh63-096.editorial: A dead man's belongings let his daughter get to know her silent father anew. For fans of art, everyday objects and restrained family stories; don't rush to a dramatic answer.

gh63-097.title: To Be Ordinary
gh63-097.syn: After an accident leaves a young man paralysed, his family struggles to rebuild their lives. His mother holds on to hope, his unemployed father becomes his caregiver, and he finds love with his physical therapist. The accident ironically brings the family closer, but his little sister hasn't forgotten that this pretty new home is built on her brother's tragedy. With fate proving unpredictable, deeper tests await both families.

Lawmakers race to enter the building and overturn the decree, while citizens gather outside to block the soldiers. As elite troops launch an assault, memories of the Gwangju Uprising resonate through the unfolding confrontation.

After surviving a racist attack herself, she defies orders from her superiors and launches her own investigation. As she reopens long-closed cases and uncovers links to a wider extremist network, Seyo is forced to confront a justice system that downplays – and at times protects – the very violence it claims to prosecute.

As love collides with ambition and prejudice, Iván embarks on a journey of self-discovery, questioning the future he has long believed was his only path.

gh63-108.syn: After 14 years on the mainland, Hein returns to the only village on a remote North Sea island. Much to his surprise, the close-knit community no longer recognises him, prompting a village court to determine whether he truly is who he claims to be. As conflicting memories fuel suspicion and hostility, Hein desperately searches for proof of his identity, only to confront a truth he has long refused to see.

gh63-109.title: The Man I Love

He is deeply loved by his devoted partner, Dennis, and his sister, Brenda. But with HIV medication offering no guarantee of survival, Jimmy rebels against his mortality, embarking on a reckless affair with a handsome young Brit.
gh63-109.editorial: New York's arts scene under the shadow of illness still has song and closeness. For those interested in how performance, friendship and care carry loss.

gh63-110.title: Tiger
gh63-110.syn: In contemporary Tokyo, 35-year-old Taiga juggles work as an erotic masseur with auditions for the gay porn industry while searching for connection. When his father's declining health draws him back home, a dispute over the family inheritance reopens old wounds. His domineering sister argues that, as a gay man without children, he deserves less, threatening to reveal the secret he has kept from their father.
gh63-110.editorial: The gap between a professional image and the identity of coming home pushes a middle-aged man to question himself. See how the need for intimacy is limited by family expectation and social systems.
gh63-110.contentNote: Story information indicates: Sexual content and nudity. Compiled from the synopsis and public information; detailed depiction and intensity have not been verified, so please consider your individual needs.
gh63-110.bio: Indian-born Anshul Chauhan worked in animation and games before directing Japanese features including Bad Poetry Tokyo, Kontora and December.

gh63-111.title: Zsazsa Zaturnnah
gh63-111.syn: Ada is a shy gay hairdresser living in a small town in the Philippines. After years of heartbreak, he resigns himself to a simple, single life. But when a magical stone from outer space transforms him into the flamboyant superhero Zsazsa Zaturnnah, Ada must battle zombies and invading Amazonistas while finding the courage to risk his heart and love again.
gh63-111.editorial: A queer superhero challenges the genre with exaggerated animation and grassroots jokes. For those who enjoy exuberant humour, and who'll watch how transformation redistributes power.
gh63-111.contentNote: Content details have not yet been reviewed. This is not an assurance of no sensitive material or suitability for all ages.
gh63-111.bio: Filipino animator Avid Liongoren works across films, advertising and music videos. His features include Saving Sally and Hayop Ka!

gh63-112.title: Tomboy
gh63-112.syn: Ten-year-old Laure has just moved with her family to a new neighbourhood. During the summer holidays, she befriends a group of local children who assume she is a boy. Embracing the identity of "Mikaël", Laure grows increasingly close to Lisa, but as their friendship deepens, maintaining the secret becomes ever more complicated. This is a newly re-edited version celebrating the 40th anniversary of the Teddy Awards.
gh63-112.editorial: One highlight of this screening is the director's re-edited version. Childhood viewpoint and identity are kept more gently; don't apply the old cut's rating to this one.
gh63-112.contentNote: Content details have not yet been reviewed. This is not an assurance of no sensitive material or suitability for all ages.
gh63-112.bio: Céline Sciamma's films include Water Lilies, Tomboy, Portrait of a Lady on Fire and Petite Maman. She also wrote My Life as a Courgette.

gh63-113.title: High Art
gh63-113.syn: Fresh-faced Syd, an assistant at a New York photography magazine, discovers Lucy Berliner, a once- renowned photographer now living in seclusion with her lover. Hoping to revive Lucy's career, Syd becomes drawn into her world of art, addiction, and desire. As professional ambition and personal attraction become increasingly entangled, both women are forced to confront the cost of love, creativity, and reinvention.
gh63-113.editorial: The 4K restoration brings back the tangle of photography, private life and artistic ambition. For those curious about indie film, queer film history and 1990s image culture.
gh63-113.contentNote: Story information indicates: Substance use and addiction; Sexual content and nudity. Compiled from the synopsis and public information; detailed depiction and intensity have not been verified, so please consider your individual needs.
gh63-113.bio: Lisa Cholodenko made her feature debut with High Art, followed by Laurel Canyon and The Kids Are All Right, alongside television work.

gh63-114.title: Oasis: Don't Look Back in Anger
gh63-114.syn: Liam and Noel Gallagher reunite for the triumphant Oasis Live '25 world tour, one of the most anticipated rock 'n' roll comebacks in years. With unprecedented access to rehearsals, backstage moments, and performances, alongside their first joint interviews in over 25 years, the documentary captures the experience and emotions of the band and their fans while exploring the profound cultural impact of Oasis and their music across generations worldwide.
gh63-114.editorial: Concert and backstage reunion together record Oasis's return. For fans who want a mass singalong on the big screen, and a look at how the brothers' relationship has shifted.
gh63-114.contentNote: Content details have not yet been reviewed. This is not an assurance of no sensitive material or suitability for all ages.
gh63-114.bio: Will Lovelace and Dylan Southern collaborate on music videos and documentaries, including No Distance Left to Run and Shut Up and Play the Hits.
gh63-114.language: English / Portuguese / Korean / Italian / Spanish / Japanese

gh63-115.title: Pulp: What Do You Do for an Encore?
gh63-115.syn: Combining footage from Pulp's 2025 tour with four decades of never-before-seen archival material, the documentary charts the Sheffield band's extraordinary journey from outsiders to cultural icons. Featuring their biggest-ever arena show, staged during the global tour for More, their first album in 24 years, it looks back at the circuitous path behind their enduring place in popular culture.
gh63-115.editorial: The encore show and archive material complement each other as they look back over Pulp's long career. For those who want to understand the band through lyrics, live show and everyday experience.
gh63-115.contentNote: Content details have not yet been reviewed. This is not an assurance of no sensitive material or suitability for all ages.
gh63-115.bio: Garth Jennings began in music videos before directing The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy, Son of Rambow and the Sing films.

gh63-116.title: The Loneliest Man in Town
gh63-116.syn: Al Cook lives surrounded by memories. His apartment and basement studio are crammed with books, videotapes and vinyl records, all that remain of a life once fully lived. When a ruthless real estate company forces him from the home he shared with his late wife, Al must let go of the treasures that define him and discover whether a new beginning is still possible.
gh63-116.editorial: An old flat holds an entire life of blues. For lovers of observational images and analogue culture: feel how moving house changes the relationship between people and things.
gh63-116.contentNote: Content details have not yet been reviewed. This is not an assurance of no sensitive material or suitability for all ages.
gh63-116.bio: Tizza Covi and Rainer Frimmel have collaborated since the 1990s. Their films include La Pivellina and Vera, combining observation and performance.

gh63-117.title: Mile End Kicks
gh63-117.syn: In the summer of 2011, Toronto music critic Grace moves to Montreal to write a book about Alanis Morissette's album Jagged Little Pill. Unable to speak French, she finds herself an outsider in the city's male-dominated indie rock scene. When she becomes entangled in a love triangle with two band members, Grace must navigate the uneasy balance between ambition, romance, and self-discovery.
gh63-117.editorial: An indie band's gig doubles as a young music critic's coming-of-age lesson. For fans of music, cringe comedy and self-searching; don't take it as only a love story.
gh63-117.contentNote: Content details have not yet been reviewed. This is not an assurance of no sensitive material or suitability for all ages.
gh63-117.bio: Canadian filmmaker Chandler Levack has journalism and criticism experience. Her films include We Forgot to Break Up and I Like Movies.

gh63-118.title: Wicker
gh63-118.syn: In a seaside village where a woman's worth is measured by her marriage prospects, a reclusive fisherwoman is ridiculed for remaining single. Fed up with her small-minded neighbours, she commissions the local basketmaker to weave her a husband. When he delivers a handsome, devoted wicker man who proves to be the perfect spouse, her unconventional romance sparks jealousy, outrage, and chaos throughout the conservative community.
gh63-118.editorial: A husband woven from wicker turns marital norms into an absurd fairy tale. For fans of black humour and handmade whimsy: who gets to decide what an ideal partner looks like?
gh63-118.contentNote: Content details have not yet been reviewed. This is not an assurance of no sensitive material or suitability for all ages.
gh63-118.bio: Alex Huston Fischer and Eleanor Wilson collaborated on Save Yourselves! before their second feature together, Wicker.

gh63-120.title: Normal
gh63-120.syn: For Sheriff Ulysses, his provisional posting to the quaint Midwestern American town of Normal was meant to be a welcome respite from both his marital woes and recent moral injuries in the line of duty. But when a botched bank robbery interrupts the municipality's tranquil pace, a dark secret is inadvertently exposed, and Ulysses soon discovers that the town is anything but its namesake.
gh63-120.editorial: A small town's calm surface is soon broken by violence. For action, black comedy and Western elements mixed together; be ready for gore.
gh63-120.contentNote: Story information indicates: Murder and violence. Compiled from the synopsis and public information; detailed depiction and intensity have not been verified, so please consider your individual needs.
gh63-120.bio: British filmmaker Ben Wheatley's films include Down Terrace, Sightseers, A Field in England and Free Fire, spanning dark comedy, horror and action.

gh63-121.title: Nightborn
gh63-121.syn: With dreams of starting a perfect family, Saga and her British husband Jon move to the isolated house where she spent much of her childhood, deep in the Finnish forest. But as soon as their baby is born, despite the reassurance of all around her, Saga knows there's something terribly wrong with her son. As their marriage starts to crack, Jon struggles to support his wife, yet only Saga suspects the terrible truth about her newborn.
gh63-121.editorial: Parenting experience entwines with Nordic monster myth. See how horror expresses physical burden, sleep deprivation and a partner drifting out of reach.
gh63-121.contentNote: Story information indicates: Horror and suspense; Psychological trauma and distress. Compiled from the synopsis and public information; detailed depiction and intensity have not been verified, so please consider your individual needs.
gh63-121.bio: Finnish filmmaker Hanna Bergholm directed Puppet Master before her feature debut Hatching. Nightborn is her second feature.

gh63-122.title: Saccharine
gh63-122.syn: First-year medical student Hana becomes obsessed with losing weight after meeting an old friend transformed by diet pills. Encouraged by her crush, a fitness influencer, she embarks on a body transformation programme before uncovering the pills' disturbing secret. As Hana's body shrinks, she is drawn into increasingly macabre acts while a sinister ghost grows ever stronger, blurring the line between physical transformation and psychological horror.
gh63-122.editorial: Body horror magnifies the pressure to be thin and self-loathing. Watch it only if you can take strong physical shock; the focus is the price of beauty norms.
gh63-122.contentNote: Story information indicates: Horror and suspense. Compiled from the synopsis and public information; detailed depiction and intensity have not been verified, so please consider your individual needs.
gh63-122.bio: Japanese-Australian filmmaker Natalie Erika James directed Relic and Apartment 7A before Saccharine, continuing her work in horror.

gh63-123.title: Sakamoto Days
gh63-123.syn: Once known as the greatest hitman in history, Taro Sakamoto abandons his deadly career after falling in love, marrying, and starting a family. Now the overweight owner of a small neighbourhood store, he finds his peaceful life shattered when a billion-yen bounty is placed on his head. As assassins descend from around the world, Sakamoto must protect his family while taking extreme care not to accidentally kill his attackers.
gh63-123.editorial: A retired assassin's home life keeps getting interrupted. For fans of manga adaptations, over-the-top action and comic timing: watch ordinary objects become weapons.
gh63-123.contentNote: Story information indicates: Murder and violence. Compiled from the synopsis and public information; detailed depiction and intensity have not been verified, so please consider your individual needs.
gh63-123.bio: Yuichi Fukuda developed in television writing and comedy before directing adaptations including Gintama and The Disastrous Life of Saiki K.

gh63-124.title: Decorado
gh63-124.syn: In the city of Anywhere, unemployed middle-aged mouse Arnold suspects his world is nothing more than an elaborate illusion. As his marriage crumbles and his best friend dies under mysterious circumstances, he becomes convinced that a powerful corporation is manipulating every aspect of his life. His growing paranoia sets him on a darkly comic journey in search of truth, freedom, and genuine connection.
gh63-124.editorial: Cute animal looks wrap an adult dystopia. Pick it if you like dark animation, and don't mistake it for a family film because of the style.
gh63-124.contentNote: Content details have not yet been reviewed. This is not an assurance of no sensitive material or suitability for all ages.
gh63-124.bio: Spanish artist Alberto Vázquez works in comics, illustration and animation. His films include Birdboy: The Forgotten Children and Unicorn Wars.

gh63-125.title: Muyi
gh63-125.syn: Muyi, 14, lives on a secluded Chinese mountain forbidden to men. With her two friends, she encounters an opera troupe renowned for The Handsome General play. As she invites them to perform in her village, an angry spirit awakens. To restore balance, Muyi embarks on a life-changing journey through ancient China, uncovering the secrets of love, courage, and self-made destiny.

screeningNotes.11/18-11:40-tp-vieshow-xinyi-hall-10: Post-screening event · Filmmakers attending (guests to be announced)

gh63-125.editorial: A girl crosses between myth and reality and comes to know the village of women anew. You'll like it if you enjoy hand-drawn art, folktale and coming-of-age adventure.
gh63-125.contentNote: Content details have not yet been reviewed. This is not an assurance of no sensitive material or suitability for all ages.
gh63-125.bio: French animator Julien Chheng trained at GOBELINS and Disney and co-directed Ernest & Celestine: A Trip to Gibberitia before Muyi.

gh63-127.title: The Butterfly Murders
gh63-127.syn: A series of mysterious murders committed by killer butterflies throws the martial arts world into turmoil. Unable to wield a sword but gifted with words, scholar Fong sets out to uncover the truth behind the crimes. Blending wuxia with detective fiction, science fiction and western influences, Tsui Hark's audacious feature debut reinvents the genre with narrative twists, kinetic editing, and irreverent energy.

screeningNotes.11/17-21:20-tp-vieshow-xinyi-hall-13: Post-screening event · Filmmakers attending (guests to be announced)

gh63-127.editorial: An early Tsui Hark that kneads wuxia, detective story and horror together. Treat its trap-filled spaces and visual misdirection as the draw, and see how the traditional jianghu is redesigned.
gh63-127.contentNote: Story information indicates: Murder and violence. Compiled from the synopsis and public information; detailed depiction and intensity have not been verified, so please consider your individual needs.
gh63-127.bio: Tsui Hark's debut The Butterfly Murders helped launch Hong Kong's New Wave. His later directing and producing reshaped popular martial-arts cinema.

gh63-128.title: Paprika
gh63-128.syn: By day, Dr. Chiba Atsuko is a research psychologist developing a revolutionary device that allows therapists to enter their patients' dreams. By night, she becomes the dream detective Paprika. When a prototype is stolen, Paprika must track down the culprit before the technology falls into the wrong hands and threatens to destroy people's minds.
gh63-128.editorial: The charm of dream-hopping lies in editing and warping images. You'll love it if you can drop real-world logic and follow Satoshi Kon's visual associations on a big screen.
gh63-128.contentNote: Story information indicates: Psychological trauma and distress. Compiled from the synopsis and public information; detailed depiction and intensity have not been verified, so please consider your individual needs.
gh63-128.bio: Satoshi Kon moved from manga and animation into directing Perfect Blue, Millennium Actress, Tokyo Godfathers and Paprika. He died in 2010.

gh63-129.title: Sense and Sensibility
gh63-129.syn: After their father's death leaves them in reduced circumstances, sisters Elinor and Marianne Dashwood must navigate love, class, and financial uncertainty in 19th-century England. While the prudent Elinor approaches life with quiet restraint, the passionate Marianne follows her heart. Ang Lee's adaptation of Jane Austen's classic explores the delicate balance between reason, emotion, and the pursuit of happiness.
gh63-129.editorial: The 4K restoration is a good chance to revisit the performances and spatial detail. Austen's marriage, property and women's lot go well with Ang Lee's restrained handling of feeling.
gh63-129.contentNote: Content details have not yet been reviewed. This is not an assurance of no sensitive material or suitability for all ages.
gh63-129.bio: Ang Lee moved from his Father Knows Best trilogy into English-language cinema with Sense and Sensibility, later directing Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon and Life of Pi.

gh63-130.title: Marie Antoinette
gh63-130.syn: In 1770, Austrian archduchess Marie Antoinette arrives in France to marry the young Dauphin, the future Louis XVI. Isolated within a royal court filled with scandal and intrigue, and under pressure to produce an heir, the teenage princess seeks escape in fashion, parties, and extravagant pleasures. But as she defies convention and embraces a life of excess, growing unrest beyond Versailles threatens the world around her.
gh63-130.editorial: Court etiquette is filmed as youth's shackles, while pop music opens another layer of period feel. For fans of costume, colour and fresh takes on history.
gh63-130.contentNote: Content details have not yet been reviewed. This is not an assurance of no sensitive material or suitability for all ages.
gh63-130.bio: Sofia Coppola's features include The Virgin Suicides, Lost in Translation, Somewhere, The Beguiled and Priscilla.

gh63-131.title: Making Marie Antoinette
gh63-131.syn: Drawing on nearly 80 hours of footage shot at Versailles in 2005, Eleanor Coppola documents her daughter Sofia directing Marie Antoinette. Narrated through Eleanor's production diaries, the film offers an intimate glimpse into Sofia's creative process and the challenges of filmmaking. Begun by Eleanor during the pandemic and completed by Sofia after her mother's death, it becomes a personal reflection on artistry, motherhood, and their relationship.
gh63-131.editorial: From a mother's footage into her daughter's film set. Paired with Marie Antoinette, it shows how creative labour is preserved under a family's gaze.
gh63-131.contentNote: Content details have not yet been reviewed. This is not an assurance of no sensitive material or suitability for all ages.
gh63-131.bio: Eleanor Coppola documented filmmaking, including Apocalypse Now. Her daughter Sofia assembled her footage and diaries to complete this posthumous work.

gh63-132.title: Nostalgia for the Future
gh63-132.syn: Guided by Charlotte Rampling's narration, a mysterious archivist delves into the 550 boxes of filmmaker Chris Marker's estate, searching for the man who hid behind pseudonyms, cats, and his own images. Moving through personal documents and film fragments, the archivist attempts to reconstruct his elusive identity, transforming Marker's archive into a living landscape of memory, where images become time machines connecting past and future.

screeningNotes.11/7-16:50-tp-vieshow-xinyi-hall-10: Post-screening event · Filmmakers attending (guests to be announced)

gh63-132.editorial: Archive, narration and editing together approach Chris Marker. For lovers of essay films; knowing his work helps, but it also works as a starting point.
gh63-132.contentNote: Content details have not yet been reviewed. This is not an assurance of no sensitive material or suitability for all ages.
gh63-132.bio: Belgian artist Brecht Debackere works in animation and experimental media. His documentary Exprmntl preceded this exploration of Chris Marker's archives.

gh63-133.title: Jacquot de Nantes
gh63-133.syn: Agnès Varda tenderly evokes the childhood of her husband, filmmaker Jacques Demy, tracing his coming of age in wartime Nantes and his growing fascination with puppet shows, fairy tales, opera, and movies. Blending narrative and documentary with clips from his films and intimate footage of Demy shortly before his death, Varda captures an artistic vocation in the making while creating a poignant love letter to her husband.
gh63-133.editorial: A fictional childhood intercuts with images of Demy's real body. For those interested in film memory and creative partnership, and in Varda's tactile gaze.
gh63-133.contentNote: Content details have not yet been reviewed. This is not an assurance of no sensitive material or suitability for all ages.
gh63-133.bio: Agnès Varda worked across fiction and documentary, from Cléo from 5 to 7 and Vagabond to The Gleaners and I.

gh63-134.title: Taste of Cherry
gh63-134.syn: Middle-aged Mr. Badii wishes to die, but in a society where suicide is considered an abomination, he needs someone willing to bury him after his death. Driving through the hills above Tehran, he approaches a succession of strangers for help, only to be turned down. Eventually, an elderly Turkish taxidermist agrees but first takes Badii on a scenic detour, offering him a different perspective on life.
gh63-134.editorial: Conversations on a drive leave the question of life and death with the audience. Watch it if you can take repetition, pauses and an open ending; if you're feeling low, read the content notes first.
gh63-134.contentNote: Story information indicates: Suicide or ending one's life. Compiled from the synopsis and public information; detailed depiction and intensity have not been verified, so please consider your individual needs.
gh63-134.bio: Abbas Kiarostami worked in film, photography and poetry. His films include Where Is the Friend's House?, Close-Up and Taste of Cherry.

gh63-135.title: Ulysses' Gaze
gh63-135.syn: A Greek-American filmmaker returns to his hometown in northern Greece, secretly searching for three missing reels shot by the pioneering Manakia brothers at the dawn of cinema. Believing the footage holds a lost innocence and truth about Balkan history, he embarks on a journey across the war-torn region. His odyssey eventually leads him to Sarajevo, where the undeveloped film may finally be waiting.

screeningNotes.11/15-10:20-tp-vieshow-xinyi-hall-12: Post-screening event · Curators’ Talk (screened together with the film)

gh63-135.editorial: A quest for old film reels is also a passage through Balkan history. Long takes and cross-border spaces take patience; save your energy and settle into the epic's rhythm.
gh63-135.contentNote: Content details have not yet been reviewed. This is not an assurance of no sensitive material or suitability for all ages.
gh63-135.bio: Greek filmmaker Theo Angelopoulos approached history through long takes, journeys and personal memory. Eternity and a Day received the Palme d'Or.

gh63-136.title: Chasing Butterflies
gh63-136.syn: Two elderly Russian aristocrats live in a vast, dilapidated château in a quiet French village, surrounded by old letters, precious antiques, and memories. Content in their gracefully fading world, they listen to news of chaos beyond the castle walls while opportunists circle around them. Thieves, antique dealers, Japanese investors, and covetous heirs all await their chance to claim pieces of the life the women represent.

screeningNotes.11/14-12:20-tp-vieshow-xinyi-hall-10: Post-screening event · Curators’ Talk (screened together with the film)

gh63-136.editorial: Time feels loose in a country castle that hides memories of class and exile. For fans of ensemble pieces, dry humour and low-plot storytelling.
gh63-136.contentNote: Content details have not yet been reviewed. This is not an assurance of no sensitive material or suitability for all ages.
gh63-136.bio: Georgian-born Otar Iosseliani later worked in France. His films include Falling Leaves, Favourites of the Moon and Monday Morning.

gh63-137.title: Elephant
gh63-137.syn: At a typical high school in Portland, Oregon, students move through an ordinary day, attending classes, meeting friends, and navigating the familiar routines of teenage life. Unaware of what is about to unfold, their paths cross and diverge as the day progresses. The everyday rhythms of school are abruptly shattered when two teenage boys arrive armed and embark on a deadly shooting rampage.

screeningNotes.11/15-18:20-tp-vieshow-xinyi-hall-11: Post-screening event · Curators’ Talk (screened together with the film)

gh63-137.editorial: Long takes through a school set ordinary moments against approaching violence. For those interested in cinematic space and multi-perspective structure; the subject involves a school shooting.
gh63-137.contentNote: Story information indicates: Murder and violence. Compiled from the synopsis and public information; detailed depiction and intensity have not been verified, so please consider your individual needs.
gh63-137.bio: Gus Van Sant's films include My Own Private Idaho, Good Will Hunting and Paranoid Park. Elephant won Cannes' Palme d'Or and directing award.

gh63-138.title: Pigs and Battleships
gh63-138.syn: In the port city of Yokosuka, where the local underworld profits from the nearby American naval base, young yakuza member Kinta joins his gang's scheme to raise pigs for the black market. His girlfriend Haruko dreams of steering him away from crime and building a future together, but Kinta refuses to abandon the gang. As rivalries, betrayal, and violence escalate, Kinta finds himself made the fall guy for those he trusted. Their desperate hopes of escape lead to a chaotic confrontation that will change both their lives forever.

screeningNotes.11/12-18:50-tp-vieshow-xinyi-hall-11: Post-screening event · Imamura Talk: Tsao Shih-han (20:40, Hall 11)

gh63-138.editorial: A gang's absurd pig-farming scheme connects to the postwar port and the garrison economy. See how Imamura cuts into social structure through low-level labour and desire.
gh63-138.contentNote: Story information indicates: Murder and violence. Compiled from the synopsis and public information; detailed depiction and intensity have not been verified, so please consider your individual needs.
gh63-138.bio: Shohei Imamura combined extensive field research with attention to marginal lives and bodily experience. The Ballad of Narayama and The Eel won Palmes d'Or.

gh63-139.title: The Insect Woman
gh63-139.syn: Born into a poor farming family in rural Japan, Tome endures hardship from childhood through the war years and post-war reconstruction. Leaving her village for the city, she enters a life of prostitution and eventually rises to become the madam of a brothel. Along the way, she survives betrayal, exploitation, and the deaths of those closest to her through an unrelenting instinct for self-preservation. As the years pass, Tome watches her own illegitimate daughter follow a strikingly similar path, suggesting that the cycle of struggle and survival may never truly end.
gh63-139.editorial: A woman's survival across the pre- and postwar years is a way into Imamura. Watch the actors' bodies and accents, and how low-life experience challenges respectable narratives.
gh63-139.contentNote: Story information indicates: Sexual violence and harassment; Financial hardship. Compiled from the synopsis and public information; detailed depiction and intensity have not been verified, so please consider your individual needs.
gh63-139.bio: Shohei Imamura combined extensive field research with attention to marginal lives and bodily experience. The Ballad of Narayama and The Eel won Palmes d'Or.

gh63-140.title: Intentions of Murder
gh63-140.syn: Sadako lives as the unacknowledged common-law wife of Koichi, a domineering librarian whose family refuses to accept her. While Koichi is away, she is raped by a burglar, Hiraoka, who returns repeatedly and becomes obsessed with her. As their disturbing relationship develops, Sadako secretly plots to kill him, even as Hiraoka urges her to run away with him to Tokyo. Torn between fear, hatred, and an unexpected awakening within herself, Sadako must decide whether to remain trapped by the life she has endured or seize the chance to change her future.

screeningNotes.11/21-18:30-tp-vieshow-xinyi-hall-11: Post-screening event · Imamura Talk: Bong Joon-ho (21:00, Hall 11)

gh63-140.editorial: Railway, snowfield and domestic space together build oppression. For viewers ready to face complicated gender power and to read the will to resist through audiovisual form.
gh63-140.contentNote: Story information indicates: Sexual violence and harassment. Compiled from the synopsis and public information; detailed depiction and intensity have not been verified, so please consider your individual needs.
gh63-140.bio: Shohei Imamura combined extensive field research with attention to marginal lives and bodily experience. The Ballad of Narayama and The Eel won Palmes d'Or.

gh63-141.title: The Pornographers
gh63-141.syn: Small-time pornographer Ogata lives in Osaka with his widowed landlady Haru, her family, and an unusual household fixture – a carp Haru believes to be her reincarnated late husband. While producing illicit films for a growing underground market, Ogata becomes increasingly infatuated with Haru's daughter Keiko, even as tension simmers with her son Koichi. As the police tighten their crackdown on pornography, Ogata struggles to maintain control while desire, obsession, and absurdity consume the fragile world he has built.
gh63-141.editorial: Peeping in the sex industry draws the audience into the act of looking. For those interested in Imamura's fieldwork method, satire of desire, and the border between fiction and documentary.
gh63-141.contentNote: Story information indicates: Sexual content and nudity. Compiled from the synopsis and public information; detailed depiction and intensity have not been verified, so please consider your individual needs.
gh63-141.bio: Shohei Imamura combined extensive field research with attention to marginal lives and bodily experience. The Ballad of Narayama and The Eel won Palmes d'Or.

gh63-142.title: Vengeance Is Mine
gh63-142.syn: Based on a true story, serial killer Iwao Enokizu murders two men, steals their money, and disappears across Japan, assuming false identities, defrauding strangers, and leaving more victims behind. Posing as a university professor, he takes refuge at an inn, where he becomes involved with its owner, Haru, and her troubled family. Meanwhile, flashbacks reveal Enokizu's turbulent childhood, imprisonment for fraud, and fraught relationship with his father and wife. As police circulate his face across the country, Enokizu continues to deceive and kill, moving from one identity to another as the nationwide manhunt gradually closes in.

screeningNotes.11/15-16:50-tp-muvie-titan-titan: Post-screening event · Imamura Talk: Nishikawa Miwa (19:10, MUVIE TITAN)

gh63-142.editorial: The course of a crime doesn't lead to a simple psychological answer. See how identity shifts, local space and performance put the killer back into the cracks of postwar society.
gh63-142.contentNote: Story information indicates: Murder and violence. Compiled from the synopsis and public information; detailed depiction and intensity have not been verified, so please consider your individual needs.
gh63-142.bio: Shohei Imamura combined extensive field research with attention to marginal lives and bodily experience. The Ballad of Narayama and The Eel won Palmes d'Or.

gh63-143.title: Black Rain
gh63-143.syn: In the aftermath of the atomic bombing of Hiroshima, Yasuko lives with her aunt and uncle, who witnessed the devastation alongside her. Five years later, as they search for a suitable husband for her, every prospective marriage is derailed by rumours that Yasuko was exposed to the radioactive "black rain" and may never bear healthy children. As those around them begin to succumb to radiation sickness, Yasuko struggles against growing isolation and an uncertain future, while her family desperately clings to hope in the shadow of a tragedy that continues to shape every aspect of their lives.

hunger-games-sunrise-on-the-reaping.title: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping
hunger-games-sunrise-on-the-reaping.release: 2026 · Mainland China release date to be announced
hunger-games-sunrise-on-the-reaping.syn:
Twenty-four years before Katniss enters the arena, the 50th Hunger Games doubles the number of tributes. A young Haymitch Abernathy is taken from District 12 and forced into a contest in which only one of 48 can survive.

Survival, trust and resistance collide for a teenager who wants to get home, long before he becomes the damaged mentor of the original films.
hunger-games-sunrise-on-the-reaping.bio: Francis Lawrence was born in Vienna in 1970 and began with music videos before directing Constantine, I Am Legend and Red Sparrow. He has directed every Hunger Games film since Catching Fire, including The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes in 2023. Sunrise on the Reaping is another return to Panem.
hunger-games-sunrise-on-the-reaping.st:
The film adapts Suzanne Collins’s 2025 novel of the same name, with a screenplay by Billy Ray, who also co-wrote the first Hunger Games. The story goes back twenty-four years before Katniss competes: the 50th Hunger Games brings the second Quarter Quell, with the number of tributes doubled to forty-eight, and Haymitch Abernathy, a boy from District 12, is chosen.

Newcomer Joseph Zada takes over the role from Woody Harrelson, alongside Whitney Peak as Lenore Dove Baird and Mckenna Grace as Maysilee Donner; the cast also includes Jesse Plemons, Ralph Fiennes, Glenn Close, Kieran Culkin, Elle Fanning, Maya Hawke and Kelvin Harrison Jr. Jennifer Lawrence and Josh Hutcherson also return. Production began in the summer of 2025 in Somiedo Natural Park in Spain.

First reactions compared it to Rogue One and Andor and praised Zada’s performance and the production design. The film is scheduled to open on November 20, 2026.
highlights: Set twenty-four years before Katniss competes, with a young Haymitch at the center.
Joseph Zada takes over from Woody Harrelson, and early reactions widely praised his performance.
The second Quarter Quell: forty-eight tributes under harsher rules than before.
Jennifer Lawrence and Josh Hutcherson return, tying the film to the original trilogy.
warnings: Teenagers forced into a lethal contest
hunger-games-sunrise-on-the-reaping.contentNote: Based on US MPA and UK BBFC theatrical advisories: violence, bloody injuries, death and disturbing scenes, smoking and teen drinking. This is not an official Mainland classification. Mainland edition differences and sensory information such as flashing or sound levels remain unverified.
hunger-games-sunrise-on-the-reaping.editorial: Series fans will find more in it, though newcomers can follow. It involves a deadly contest among minors and violence, and is emotionally heavy. Ratings and content notes are pending ahead of release.

legend-of-1900.title: The Legend of 1900
legend-of-1900.syn:
An infant abandoned on an ocean liner in 1900 is adopted by a crewman and grows into an extraordinary pianist. Without papers or a life ashore, he knows the world through the ship and its passengers.

Years later, trumpeter Max recalls their friendship, music in a storm and a piano duel—and the question of what it means to choose a life when an entire world waits beyond the gangway.
legend-of-1900.bio: Giuseppe Tornatore was born in 1956 in Bagheria, Sicily, and began with documentaries and television; Cinema Paradiso brought him the Oscar for Best Foreign Language Film. The Legend of 1900 was his first English-language feature and one of the high points of his long collaboration with the composer Ennio Morricone.
legend-of-1900.st:
The film adapts Alessandro Baricco’s 1994 theatrical monologue Novecento, with Tornatore writing the screenplay himself. It is set aboard the transatlantic liner Virginian: a foundling is found by the crewman Danny and named 1900; he grows up on the ship, never sets foot on land, and shows astonishing talent at the piano.

It was Tornatore’s first English-language film, starring Tim Roth, with Mélanie Thierry, Bill Nunn and Clarence Williams III among the cast and Lajos Koltai as cinematographer. According to published sources, it was shot partly in Odessa aboard a sixty-year-old Russian freighter and partly at Cinecittà in Rome. It opened in Italy in October 1998.

Morricone’s score won the Golden Globe for Best Original Score, and the film collected several awards at Italy’s David di Donatello and Nastro d’Argento ceremonies. The piano duel with the jazz pioneer Jelly Roll Morton is its best-known scene.
highlights: Adapted from Baricco’s monologue Novecento, with Tornatore writing the screenplay.
Tim Roth plays a piano prodigy who never leaves the ship.
Morricone’s score won the Golden Globe for Best Original Score.
The piano duel with the jazz pioneer Jelly Roll Morton is the best-known sequence.
honors: Winner | 2000 Golden Globe · Best Original Score (Ennio Morricone)
legend-of-1900.contentNote: Story information indicates infant abandonment, bereavement, war context and explosions. This restoration has not been reviewed in full; depiction intensity and sensory information such as flashing or sound levels remain unverified.
legend-of-1900.editorial: A story of music and time, suited to those who love Morricone’s score and slower storytelling. It is on the long side and emotionally weighty, with themes of parting and loss.

everest-the-other-side.title: Everest: The Other Side
everest-the-other-side.syn:
Ski mountaineers Jim Morrison and Hilaree Nelson fall in love and share an extraordinary ambition: to climb Everest’s direct North Face and ski down it.

The film follows exposure, ice and unpredictable weather, while exploring a life reshaped by loss. When a climbing partner and loved one can no longer be alongside you, continuing toward the summit takes on another meaning.
everest-the-other-side.bio: Elizabeth Chai Vasarhelyi and Jimmy Chin are a married filmmaking team. Chin is both an elite mountaineer and a cinematographer, and their documentary Free Solo won the Oscar for Best Documentary Feature, after Meru. Everest: The Other Side returns them to extreme mountaineering; Chin himself is among the climbers on the mountain and has known the film’s subjects for years.
everest-the-other-side.st:
The film’s subjects are the ski mountaineers Jim Morrison and Hilaree Nelson, who fell in love while climbing and planned to climb Everest by its north face and ski down, something never completed before. It took seven years to make, documenting an expedition in one of the most remote places on earth, with cinematography by Clair Popkin, Jimmy Chin and Christopher Murphy and editing by Bob Eisenhardt and Simona Ferrari.

During the project Nelson died in September 2022 in an avalanche while skiing down Manaslu in Nepal, and the accident was captured on film. Morrison had earlier lost his wife and two children in a plane crash, so the film becomes a work about grief and continuing on. Co-director Chai Vasarhelyi has said they wanted to look through Jim’s eyes at how one learns to live with grief.

The film had its world premiere on September 3, 2026 in the Venice Open (out of competition) section of the 83rd Venice Film Festival, later screened at festivals including Telluride, and opened in theaters and IMAX worldwide on October 30, released by National Geographic Documentary Films. Reviews praised its tension and emotional impact, while some felt it did not fully question the cost of risk.
highlights: The Free Solo team reunites, with Jimmy Chin filming on the mountain himself.
Shot over seven years; the subjects were hit by an avalanche during the project, and the film records the accident.
World premiere in the Venice festival’s out-of-competition section, released in IMAX.
The through-line is Morrison carrying his grief to finish the dream he shared with Nelson.
honors: Selection | 83rd Venice Film Festival, 2026 · Out of Competition
everest-the-other-side.contentNote: Based on UK BBFC and US MPA theatrical advisories: dangerous climbing, avalanches and accidents, death and bereavement, and infrequent strong language. Some scenes may be upsetting. Mainland edition differences and sensory information remain unverified; the US rating applies to its own edition.
everest-the-other-side.editorial: For lovers of documentary and extreme sport, best seen on an IMAX screen. It includes an avalanche accident and the death of loved ones, so viewers sensitive to death and loss should think first.

ballad-of-the-warm-grave.title: Ballad of the Warm Grave
ballad-of-the-warm-grave.syn: Over ten years, a filmmaker turns the camera toward his family, confronting his sister’s troubled past, his father’s secrets and his mother’s burdens. Reunion and separation become opportunities to understand one another.
ballad-of-the-warm-grave.bio: Zhou Junsen and Dai Kun studied film-related subjects at Sichuan Normal University. Zhou also writes fiction; Dai has worked in audiovisual production for more than a decade.
ballad-of-the-warm-grave.st: The organiser schedules a 150-minute edition, while the festival record lists 149 minutes. Screening: October 3, 2026, 17:30. Remote director discussion: 20:00–21:00.
highlights: Observe how a decade of family footage changes the meaning of silence and reunion.
A childhood housing estate gives the film its title and a place for memory.
The remote discussion offers room to ask about filming one’s own family.
ballad-of-the-warm-grave.editorial: For viewers drawn to personal documentaries and intergenerational relationships. Family trauma and bereavement are central; allow time for the film and the hour-long discussion.
