shawshank-redemption.title: The Shawshank Redemption
shawshank-redemption.release: August 28, 2026 · Mainland China debut in 4K restoration
shawshank-redemption.book: Stephen King, Rita Hayworth and Shawshank Redemption
shawshank-redemption.syn:
Banker Andy Dufresne is convicted of murdering his wife and her lover and sentenced to life at Shawshank State Penitentiary. Behind the walls he befriends Red, a long-serving inmate who knows how to get things, and over the years finds ways to survive through knowledge, patience and a little dignity.

A prison film about time, friendship and hope, it never hurries to explain how a man bears injustice; it lets the audience live through the days alongside them.
shawshank-redemption.bio: Frank Darabont was born in 1959 in a refugee camp in France to Hungarian parents and grew up in the United States. He started as a screenwriter and in 1984 made a short film of Stephen King’s story The Woman in the Room, which began his relationship with King. The Shawshank Redemption was his feature directing debut, and he went on to adapt King’s The Green Mile and The Mist.
shawshank-redemption.st:
The film adapts Stephen King’s 1982 novella Rita Hayworth and Shawshank Redemption, from the collection Different Seasons. Darabont bought the rights for a few thousand dollars and wrote the script in eight weeks; he dropped Rita Hayworth from the title to avoid actresses assuming it was a Hayworth biopic. It was made by Castle Rock Entertainment on a budget of about $25 million.

Though set in Maine, principal photography from June to August 1993 took place almost entirely at the Ohio State Reformatory in Mansfield, Ohio, a building slated for demolition whose demolition was delayed a year by the shoot. The cinematographer is Roger Deakins, the composer Thomas Newman and the producer Niki Marvin. It premiered at the Toronto festival in September 1994 and opened in the United States on September 23.

Its first run earned only about $16 million, far below cost, but it received seven Oscar nominations and kept being discovered on cable and home video until it became one of the most beloved films. It was added to the Library of Congress’s National Film Registry in 2015.
highlights: Adapted from a Stephen King novella, with Darabont writing the script in weeks.
Shot on location at the Ohio State Reformatory, photographed by Roger Deakins.
A box-office disappointment that grew into a classic through television and home video.
Seven Oscar nominations; added to the National Film Registry in 2015.

toddling-youths.title: The Toddling Youths
toddling-youths.syn: Yaqin is a girl who wants to see the world. Wang Jiong is a boy who stakes his confession on his career. Two friends fresh out of university both want to escape their families and prove themselves. As an imperfect society collides with imperfect selves and cheerfulness turns into a mask, their original ambitions waver. Where will this stumbling journey of growing up take them?
toddling-youths.bio: QI Yanyan studied at Tsinghua University and worked in television and commercial filmmaking before moving toward documentary. She directed, photographed and edited this long-term project; her short Shang An screened at FIRST in 2025.
toddling-youths.st: Filming began in 2019. Four years of observation produced nearly 800 hours of footage, followed by roughly two years of editing. The film follows a photography venture, work, family and relationships rather than a single success story.
highlights: Work and relationships are inseparable parts of growing up.
The subjects can change their minds and perform for the camera.
Long-term observation reveals changes that a snapshot cannot.

spider-man-brand-new-day.title: Spider-Man: Brand New Day
spider-man-brand-new-day.syn: Forgotten by the world after No Way Home, Peter Parker fights crime full-time while his former friends move on. Mounting pressure triggers a change in his body, and a powerful unseen enemy threatens the city and the people he loves.
spider-man-brand-new-day.bio: Destin Daniel Cretton was born in Hawaii and drew attention with the independent film Short Term 12, later directing The Glass Castle and Just Mercy and the Marvel film Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings. Spider-Man: Brand New Day is his second Marvel feature and the fourth Spider-Man film starring Tom Holland.
spider-man-brand-new-day.st:
The film is a Sony and Marvel collaboration, with Cretton taking over from Jon Watts, who directed the first three films; the screenplay is by Chris McKenna and Erik Sommers, and Amy Pascal and Kevin Feige produce. Around August 2025 the production closed streets in Glasgow for location shooting with extensive practical action, then continued at Pinewood Studios in England.

The story follows directly from No Way Home: no one remembers Peter Parker, and he protects New York alone. Besides Tom Holland, Zendaya and Jacob Batalon, the cast includes Sadie Sink, Liza Colón-Zayas, Jon Bernthal as the Punisher Frank Castle, and Mark Ruffalo. It opened in the United States on July 31, 2026.
highlights: A new director, Destin Daniel Cretton, with McKenna and Sommers still writing.
Shot with Glasgow streets closed, favoring practical action.
Continues from No Way Home, with no one remembering Peter Parker.
The Punisher, Sadie Sink and other new faces join.

the-great-skull.title: The Great Skull
the-great-skull.syn: Gu Liyan, a Shanghai graduate about to look for work, loses her father Gu Weixing to cancer. With her mother Wu Kaidi she handles funeral arrangements for the first time and unexpectedly meets the “funeral committee” her father secretly formed, setting off a chain of absurd, chaotic events. In the mess, mother and daughter slowly untie old knots and move towards new lives.
the-great-skull.bio: Liu Xiaoyang is from Fuzhou, Fujian; he studied at Zhejiang University of Media and Communications and took an MFA in film production at the Hong Kong Academy for Performing Arts. His short film Lock was shortlisted at the Beijing College Student Film Festival, and he has worked as a film planner, executive producer and first assistant director on several features. His feature script was shortlisted at the 13th FIRST Film Market pitch. The Great Skull is his feature directing debut.
the-great-skull.st:
The screenwriter Zhang Xiaoying is from Shanghai and also graduated from the film production program at the Hong Kong Academy for Performing Arts; the story draws on her own real-life experience, rooted in everyday Shanghai life. It is supervised by Xu Zheng and Zeng Jian, with Xu Zheng and Song Zuer in special appearances. Director Liu Xiaoyang explained that the title carries black humor and hoped audiences would leave with courage to go forward.

The film follows Gu Liyan, a Shanghai girl about to graduate, who after her father Gu Weixing dies of cancer handles the funeral with her forceful, face-conscious mother Wu Kaidi, and unexpectedly runs into the funeral committee her father secretly organized before his death. Ni Hongjie said speaking in the local dialect made Wu Kaidi more vivid, with many details arising on the spot; Wen Qi said the sea that recurs in the film means freedom to Gu Liyan, always just out of reach.

The film had its world premiere on June 12, 2026 in the Main Competition of the 28th Shanghai International Film Festival, then screened as the closing special screening of the 20th FIRST Youth Film Festival, and opened nationwide on September 5.
highlights: Funerals and farewells told with black humor and light comedy, avoiding melodrama.
The mother-daughter scenes between Wen Qi and Ni Hongjie are the focus of reviews.
Shanghai dialect and everyday Shanghai life, drawn from the screenwriter’s real experience.
World premiere in the Main Competition of the Shanghai festival, and the closing film of FIRST.

all-wishes-come-true.title: All Wishes Come True!
all-wishes-come-true.syn: In the Penglai immortal realm, eight mortals pose as immortals to slip into a treasure vault that only gods may enter. Facing riches “that ten lifetimes could not spend,” they quickly form a ramshackle troupe, open a temple and go hunting for treasure. Just as their dream comes true, a force coveting the vault steps out of the shadows while rifts open within the team.
all-wishes-come-true.bio: Mou Zhengyang is a director born in the 1990s, and Eight Immortals! is the first feature he has both directed and written. In a piece for People’s Daily he recalled that, like most people, he first knew the Eight Immortals through the idiom about crossing the sea: the name is famous, yet the stories are both familiar and unfamiliar, which left room for invention. The film is produced by Oriental DreamWorks, with Ying Xujun as supervising producer.
all-wishes-come-true.st:
Mou says the Eight Immortals are a rare group in Chinese myth who became immortals from ordinary human lives: not born divine, but people from the folk world with their own origins, trades and flaws. Researching the sources, he found the group was assembled from the bottom up by popular belief over nearly a thousand years from the Tang to the Ming; Iron-Crutch Li is modeled on a lame beggar, and He Xiangu appeared because people wanted a woman among them. So the film is about the struggle before ascension rather than the ease after it.

In the story, eight mortals pose as gods, dig a tunnel toward the treasure vault, and run a temple where they stumble into granting people’s wishes, drawing the attention of the Three Stars of Fortune, Prosperity and Longevity. Penglai is designed as a super-first-tier city where even immortals clock in and chase KPIs. The team drew on ancient texts describing mirages and fairy mountains; art director Gao Ranyu worked on the look, and Mou also used Penglai bonsai artifacts at the Palace Museum to design the color of the realm. In previews, he played several roles himself in a live-action storyboard.

The voice direction aimed for everyday warmth rather than polished technique. Beijing Daily reports that the young Han Xiangzi was voiced by three child actors in turn because production ran so long that the first two boys’ voices broke. The film opened on 18 July 2026 with 8.3 on Douban, and the scholar Yi Zhongtian and director Guo Fan both praised it publicly.
highlights: Watch how eight mortals with their own flaws and schemes become a team through bickering.
Penglai is built as a clock-in modern city, with workplace jokes inside the comedy.
The first half is street-level comedy; the second sharpens the fates of Zhongli Quan, Lü Dongbin and He Xiangu.
The film’s core line is about where you are going, not where you came from, which echoes the folk origins of the legend.
all-wishes-come-true.contentNote: Based on published synopses, trailers and distribution materials: fantasy combat and peril, deception and temptation. Not a full viewing review; intensity, flashing and sound levels remain unverified. This is not an official classification of the screening edition.
all-wishes-come-true.editorial: Suited to fans of Chinese animation, reimagined myth and family viewing. The first half is mostly comedy, while the second turns heavier around characters’ fates and sacrifice, so younger children may want a parent beside them.

once-upon-a-time-in-the-middle-east.title: Once Upon a Time in the Middle East
once-upon-a-time-in-the-middle-east.syn: Chef Xu Fu travels to the Middle East to support his family and repay debts. With restaurant manager Ma Junsheng, he builds a welcoming Chinese eatery. When war overturns daily life, the restaurant becomes a fragile refuge, and feeding people becomes a matter of survival and responsibility.
once-upon-a-time-in-the-middle-east.bio: Wen Muye directed Dying to Survive and Striving, and Xinhua reports he is 41. This is his third feature and is often described by media as the finale of his small-people trilogy. He co-wrote with Lang Qunli and Zhong Wei, and Ning Hao produced, continuing the core team from Dying to Survive.
once-upon-a-time-in-the-middle-east.st:
Xinhua reports that Wen began preparing this film once post-production on Dying to Survive ended. He saw news about Chinese people who opened restaurants in the Middle East, and the contrast between the death and broken families of war and the warmth and stability of food drove the idea. At first he planned something closer to a public-interest piece; after the team traveled to the Middle East for interviews, he settled on a purely Chinese viewpoint on a small person trying to make a living abroad. His guiding idea was simply to eat well.

In the story, the Chinese chef Xu Fu goes to a Middle Eastern Chinese restaurant to pay off debts, runs the Dragon restaurant with the floor manager Ma Junsheng, and is swept into turmoil when war breaks out. The crew spent six months building a Middle Eastern old town at the Qingdao Oriental Movie Metropolis; the studio says it covers over 100,000 square meters with more than 200 buildings, plus a 16.5-meter tree of life. Shen Teng took cooking training and did many of the wok scenes himself, and Jiang Qiming has a two-minute single take entirely in a foreign language linking the kitchen, dining room and street.

The film opened on 11 August 2026, passed 1 billion yuan in eight days, and rose to 8.7 on Douban. Critics read it as a juxtaposition of war and daily life; the Christmas banquet of fusion dishes is written as a satire of war’s absurdity, and some note it keeps real-world thought alongside commercial-genre appeal.
highlights: Eating well is the film’s central idea; notice how the same restaurant’s food changes meaning before and after the war.
Shen Teng cooks on screen himself, and the comic actor carries physical fear and helplessness here.
Jiang Qiming’s two-minute foreign-language take is key to understanding the restaurant’s space.
Notice the fusion dishes at the Christmas banquet, where an absurd table meets approaching danger.
once-upon-a-time-in-the-middle-east.editorial: Suited to viewers who like realist stories about ordinary people in wartime. It includes war, bombing, imprisonment and children caught in conflict, and is emotionally heavy, so those sensitive to such material should choose carefully.
once-upon-a-time-in-the-middle-east.contentNote: Based on published synopses, trailers and distribution materials: war and armed conflict, children in danger, death and displacement. Not a full viewing review; intensity, flashing and sound levels remain unverified. This is not an official classification of the screening edition.

wall-e.title: WALL·E
wall-e.release: August 19, 2026 · Mainland China release (previews from August 15)
wall-e.syn: Left behind on an abandoned Earth, WALL-E compacts rubbish and treasures the remains of human life. The arrival of the probe EVE leads him into space, where a discovery forces humanity to choose between automated comfort and learning to care for its world again.
wall-e.bio: Andrew Stanton is a Pixar veteran who directed A Bug’s Life, Finding Nemo and WALL-E, the latter two both winning the Oscar for Best Animated Feature. He is more than a director: he contributed to the story of every Toy Story film and only directed the series himself with Toy Story 5 in 2026. WALL-E’s original story was conceived by him and Pete Docter, and the screenplay was written by him and Jim Reardon.
wall-e.st:
According to Screen Daily, Stanton and his colleagues spent four years on the film and seem to have embraced nearly every no-no in the animation book: a dialogue-free first stretch, an Earth without people, and a lead who barely speaks. Sound design was by Ben Burtt, the man behind the voice of E.T. and R2-D2 in the Star Wars films, and WALL-E’s voice is his work. The film therefore tells its story almost entirely through image and sound.

It is Pixar’s first animated feature with live-action segments. Thomas Newman composed the score, and the closing song Down to Earth is by Peter Gabriel and Newman. Per Wikipedia, the budget was about 180 million dollars, a record for animation at the time, and the worldwide gross about 533 million dollars.

It won the Oscar for Best Animated Feature at the 81st Academy Awards and received five more nominations: Original Score, Original Screenplay, Original Song, Sound Editing and Sound Mixing. It also won the Golden Globe for Best Animated Feature, the Hugo for Best Long Form Dramatic Presentation, the final Nebula Award for Best Script and the Saturn Award for Best Animated Film, and Time ranked it first among the best movies of the decade.
highlights: The first half has almost no dialogue; notice how Ben Burtt’s electronic sounds give WALL-E expression.
WALL-E’s collection of small objects grounds the large environmental theme in everyday life.
The contrast between Earth and the starship makes a visual argument about loss and starting again.
It comes from the same director as Toy Story 5, so the two make an interesting pair on how they treat companionship.
honors: Winner | 81st Academy Awards · Best Animated Feature
Winner | 66th Golden Globe Awards · Best Animated Feature
wall-e.contentNote: Based on published synopses, trailers and distribution materials: environmental destruction, robot damage and peril. Not a full viewing review; intensity, flashing and sound levels remain unverified. This is not an official classification of the screening edition.
wall-e.editorial: An entry point into romance, visual comedy and ecology. For family viewing, consider the robot damage and peril as well as its gentler moments.

obsession.title: Obsession
obsession.syn: Bear uses a cheap wishing object to make his crush Nikki love him. His apparent romantic breakthrough becomes an increasingly sinister form of dependence, trapping both of them and their friends in consequences he cannot simply undo.
obsession.bio: Curry Barker is a creator who came up through online video and drew attention with the viral found-footage short Milk & Serial. Obsession is his feature directorial debut, and he also wrote and edited it, on a reported budget of only about 750,000 dollars. After its Midnight Madness premiere at Toronto it was acquired by Focus Features.
obsession.st:
The story grows from the old “be careful what you wish for” motif: Bear (Michael Johnston), who works in a music store, has long loved his childhood friend and coworker Nikki (Inde Navarrette) without daring to say so, until he gets a supernatural toy called a One Wish Willow and wishes for her to fall in love with him. The horror comes from the price of that wish and from whether love that has been granted is still love.

It had its world premiere in the Midnight Madness section of the Toronto International Film Festival on 5 September 2025, sold out every screening, and was first runner-up for that section’s People’s Choice Award; it then played Fantastic Fest and is reported to have won the Sitges People’s Choice Award. Focus Features reportedly bought it for roughly 14 to 15 million dollars, Blumhouse later joined as an executive producer, and it opened in the United States on 15 May 2026. It reportedly grossed around 370 million dollars worldwide, far above its cost.

The cinematographer is Taylor Clemons and the composer is Rock Burwell. Comedy veteran Andy Richter also appears, and critics most often discuss the way the film slides from awkward comedy into horror.
highlights: The One Wish Willow is the core device; notice how relationships warp after the wish comes true.
The horror relies less on spectacle than on a changed familiar person and intimacy slipping out of control.
Notice the slide from awkward comedy into horror, which connects to the director’s online-short background.
A low-budget independent film bought by a major distributor on festival buzz, which is part of its story.
obsession.editorial: For viewers comfortable with supernatural relationship horror. The film involves coercion and control rather than an uncomplicated romantic fantasy.
obsession.contentNote: Based on published synopses, trailers and distribution materials: coercive intimacy and control, supernatural threat, violence and bloodshed.
