empty-gun.title: V
empty-gun.syn: In 1990s Hong Kong, Wan Ziqiang pursues a shortcut out of poverty. His partnership with flight attendant Luo Jiayuan brings money and escalating danger, while a businessman and police investigators become entangled in his belief that luck can master fate.
empty-gun.bio: Han Yan has directed films including Go Away Mr. Tumor and Animal World. Empty Gun is his first crime genre film, set in Hong Kong in the early 1990s. He grew up watching Hong Kong films, especially cop-and-crook films, and after visiting the city and seeing its everyday energy he felt Hong Kong was the right place for the story.
empty-gun.st:
The story is fictional and set in early 1990s Hong Kong, a city then said to be paved with gold. The laborer Wan Ziqiang (Zhu Yilong) wants to rewrite his fate and, after meeting the flight attendant Luo Jiayuan (Wei Shiya), robs a large sum with her; the success makes him more reckless and draws him into a deeper contest with the wealthy Chen Huiyan (Tony Leung Ka-fai). The mainland police officer Qi Honggang (Tan Jianci) and the Hong Kong officer Guan Suchen (Li Shihua) work together on the case. Media read the title as a metaphor for the hero’s luck and fate.

The director has said he would not have made the film without Zhu Yilong, and Zhu himself says he has a special attachment to Hong Kong cinema, having watched classics such as Tian Ruo You Qing. The cast spans three generations: besides the leads, Kara Hui, Ni Dahong, Ye Tong, Huang Jue, Yu Haoming and Li Zhiting appear, with Hong Kong figures Li Xiuxian, Zhang Zhaohui and Lam Suet in guest roles.

The film runs 160 minutes and opened in the mainland on 19 August 2026, only five days after its release date was announced, which prompted worries about screenings. In Hong Kong it opened on 25 September uncut, and the violence and torture scenes led to a Category III rating.
highlights: The empty gun is both luck and fate; notice how the hero goes from bluffing to losing control.
The repeated duels between Wan Ziqiang and Qi Honggang drive the cat-and-mouse plot.
Early-1990s Hong Kong streets, cha chaan teng and trade details give the film its period texture.
The Hong Kong version is uncut with violence and torture scenes, so check the content notes first.
empty-gun.editorial: For viewers interested in character-driven crime stories. Allow for its long running time and violent criminal situations.
empty-gun.contentNote: Based on published synopses, trailers and distribution materials: robbery and kidnapping, guns and criminal violence, threats and coercion. Not a full viewing review; intensity, flashing and sound levels remain unverified. This is not an official classification of the screening edition.

triangle.title: Triangle
triangle.release: July 17, 2026 · Mainland China release in the uncut version
triangle.syn: After a storm overturns their yacht, Jess and her friends board an apparently deserted liner. Its corridors seem strangely familiar to her. Pursuit and death turn the search for rescue into a struggle to understand repeated events, as each attempt to change what happens gives earlier details a different meaning.
triangle.bio: Christopher Smith is a British director whose earlier films include Creep and Severance. He wrote and directed Triangle, and said in a 2024 interview that he felt its ultimate theme was regret and not being able to change something you have done.
triangle.st:
The film is set around the Bermuda Triangle off Florida: Jess (Melissa George), a young single mother, is invited by her friend Greg for a day on his sailboat. After a storm, a mysterious liner appears, and what follows cannot be explained in any ordinary way. Many critics compare it to the myth of Sisyphus and to time-loop films, yet it does not rely on stacking rules.

Although set near Miami, it was shot in Brisbane and the Gold Coast in Queensland, Australia, with a largely Australian cast. Principal photography began on 6 June 2008 at Warner Roadshow Studios and various Gold Coast locations, where a three-storey replica of a luxury liner was built at the Southport Seaway. Australian trade reports describe it as the first official co-production to receive the Producer Offset.

It premiered at London FrightFest on 27 August 2009 and opened in the UK on 16 October. Reviews were generally positive, often praising the clever script and Melissa George’s performance. She appears in almost every scene, and one critic notes she plays Jess disoriented and dreamlike from the start.
highlights: Melissa George is in almost every scene; notice the dreamlike disorientation she carries from the opening.
Set in Florida but shot in Queensland, Australia, the liner is a physically built set.
Smith says the theme is regret; rewatch the choices inside the loop with that in mind.
Cleverly structured without big spectacle, it suits fans of mind-bending mysteries.
triangle.contentNote: Based on published synopses, trailers and distribution materials: violence and repeated deaths, child abuse and peril, psychological distress. Not a full viewing review; intensity, flashing and sound levels remain unverified. This is not an official classification of the screening edition.
triangle.editorial: For viewers drawn to loops and unreliable perspectives. Beyond the puzzle, expect distress involving family trauma and children.

kung-fu-soccer.title: Kung Fu Soccer
kung-fu-soccer.syn: An underestimated women’s team enters the Supreme Invincible Cup. Captain Shuangshuang, striker Yulong and martial-arts mentor Xu Feng combine kung fu with football, but must rebuild trust and confidence before their unconventional tactics can work.
kung-fu-soccer.bio: Stephen Chow is a Hong Kong director, writer and actor whose films include Shaolin Soccer, Kung Fu Hustle, Journey to the West: Conquering the Demons and The Mermaid. He directed and wrote Kung Fu Soccer, with Lin Zicong as co-director. Media call it a spiritual follow-up to Shaolin Soccer on its 25th anniversary.
kung-fu-soccer.st:
IT Home reports that Stephen Chow announced on his 61st birthday, 22 June 2023, that he would make Shaolin Women’s Soccer, later renamed Women’s Soccer and finally Kung Fu Soccer. He also held an open global call for female performers, seeking amateurs who were smart, athletic, of good character and naturally beautiful, of any nationality. Filming began in Shenzhen on 7 March 2025 and wrapped on 2 June.

The story follows the women’s team Emei: with the Supreme Invincible Cup about to start, a group of women over 30 form a team. Captain Shuangshuang (Zhang Xiaofei) never accepts losing, and star striker Yulong (Dilraba) moves from conflict to reconciliation with her; Lay Zhang plays the kung fu coach Xu Feng, with Carina Lau and Takeru Satoh in special appearances. Former national goalkeeper Zhao Lina and former international Li Jiayue also take part.

It opened on 11 July 2026 with a first-day gross above 250 million yuan and, per Lighthouse data, broke seven record marks; the three-day total passed 568 million. Opinion was sharply split: some said Chow had slipped, some said the audience had failed to understand him, and others saw it as a deliberate willful game.
highlights: Kung fu plus football returns; compare with Shaolin Soccer to see what has and has not changed in Chow’s work.
Former national players such as Zhao Lina and Li Jiayue take part, adding realism to the pitch scenes.
Reviews are sharply split, so go in expecting Chow-style absurdity.
The theme is still never giving up: underestimated people winning the hard way.
kung-fu-soccer.editorial: For fans of exaggerated sports comedy. Its physical action is fantasy rather than a guide to real football or training.
kung-fu-soccer.contentNote: Based on published synopses, trailers and distribution materials: comic fighting and sports collisions, mockery and competitive pressure. Not a full viewing review; intensity, flashing and sound levels remain unverified. This is not an official classification of the screening edition.

three-kingdoms-luoyang.title: Three Kingdoms: The Beginning
three-kingdoms-luoyang.syn: Before the Three Kingdoms emerge, the Eastern Han court is collapsing. Young Cao Cao and Yuan Shao hope to restore order, but conflict in Luoyang and Dong Zhuo’s arrival expose the distance between their ambitions and choices.
three-kingdoms-luoyang.bio: Xie Junwei is a director at Light Chaser Animation who directed Chang’an. In a piece for People’s Daily he wrote that audiences’ love for Chang’an gave the team the confidence to keep working on historical and cultural subjects, so they decided to start a Three Kingdoms animated film series. Three Kingdoms: The Beginning is the first of three films.
three-kingdoms-luoyang.st:
The film is set in the late Eastern Han: after the Yellow Turban uprising, in-laws seize power and eunuchs corrupt the court; Cao Cao and Yuan Shao hope to use General-in-Chief He Jin to check the eunuchs, but Dong Zhuo exploits the chaos to enter the capital. Starting from the struggle for Luoyang, it skips the familiar Red Cliffs to answer where the Three Kingdoms came from. Xie says these heroes were not born heroes; they had their own paths.

Cao Cao is the main point of view. The director sees him as ahead of his time, a man who did not believe in fate in an age when everyone did. Character design director Cui Yuemei says Cao Cao has a broad lion nose and long phoenix eyes, with distinct looks for youth and middle age. Lü Bu gets the best costumes in the film, Yuan Shao is voiced by Wei Chao, and Wang Kai is among the leads.

Production took three years, with over 400 Light Chaser colleagues as the core team and more than a thousand contributors in all. The art draws on Han stone reliefs, sculptures and murals for a stern, vigorous Han look, and the team visited the Luoyang museum and sites such as Cao Cao’s tomb in Anyang. The end song, Immortals by the River, is sung by tenor Wang Chuanyue. The film opened on 10 July 2026 and stood at 8.1 on Douban in late July.
highlights: It starts from the struggle for Luoyang to show how the Three Kingdoms began, rather than retelling Red Cliffs.
Cao Cao is the main viewpoint; notice how his origins, ambition and romance are treated.
The art draws on Han stone reliefs, sculpture and murals; look for the Han feel in sets and lighting.
As the first of three films, it pairs well with Chang’an to see how the studio’s handling of history has changed.
three-kingdoms-luoyang.editorial: Suited to viewers who enjoy historical subjects and Chinese animation. It includes war and court intrigue with a fairly complex plot, so some Three Kingdoms background helps.
three-kingdoms-luoyang.contentNote: Based on published synopses, trailers and distribution materials: war and weapons, political persecution, death and civil unrest. Not a full viewing review; intensity, flashing and sound levels remain unverified. This is not an official classification of the screening edition.

toy-story-5.title: Toy Story 5
toy-story-5.syn: Bonnie’s new smart tablet Lilypad competes for her attention, challenging Jessie, Buzz and the other toys. When Jessie and Bullseye go missing, Woody returns to help Buzz find them and reconsider what it means to be there for a growing child.
toy-story-5.bio: Andrew Stanton directed Finding Nemo and WALL-E and contributed to the story of every Toy Story film, but only directed the series himself with the fifth. He co-wrote and co-directed with McKenna Harris. According to Time Out, it is his first directing job at Pixar since Finding Dory.
toy-story-5.st:
The story follows Toy Story 4: as reviews describe it, two years after Woody’s departure Jessie has become the leader of Bonnie’s toys, with Buzz as her loyal, lovestruck deputy. Bonnie’s parents buy her her first tablet, Lilypad (voiced by Greta Lee), a frog-shaped learning device that holds the child’s attention. Jessie fears being abandoned and worries about Bonnie’s growing isolation, and leads Woody, Buzz and the others in trying to rescue her from the screen.

It is the first in the series not centered emotionally on Woody; the focus moves to Jessie (voiced by Joan Cusack), continuing the backstory from Toy Story 2. Many critics found that Stanton and Harris treat the toys-versus-tech conflict with more nuance than expected. The film opened on 19 June 2026, runs 102 minutes and is rated PG in the US.

Reception was generally positive: Time Out gave it four stars, Little White Lies said it shows the franchise still has juice, while Slant criticized it as a sermonizing repeat about screen addiction. Tom Hanks and Tim Allen return with less to do than before, and a few reviewers found the huge voice cast crowded.
highlights: Jessie carries the main action line; notice how her fear of being abandoned drives the film.
Lilypad is no ordinary new toy; it changes how a child spends her time.
Bonnie’s imaginative spaces use a handmade visual design that contrasts with her real room.
From the same director as WALL-E, one film about machines and companionship, the other about toys and screens.
toy-story-5.editorial: For families and returning viewers. The fourth film helps explain Woody’s situation; companionship and screen time offer useful discussion points.
toy-story-5.contentNote: Based on published synopses, trailers and distribution materials: separation and loss, toy peril. Not a full viewing review; intensity, flashing and sound levels remain unverified. This is not an official classification of the screening edition.

the-furious.title: The Furious
the-furious.syn: When his daughter is abducted, tradesman Wang Wei joins troubled journalist Navin to penetrate a trafficking network. Each lead takes them into another dangerous space, where improvised weapons and physical endurance become the means of survival.
the-furious.bio: Kenji Tanigaki is a Japanese action choreographer turned director who built his career in Hong Kong and has worked with Donnie Yen for many years, designing action for films such as Sha Po Lang and Flash Point. He also designed action for Twilight of the Warriors: Walled In. The Furious is his third film as director.
the-furious.st:
The studio frames the film as a tribute to the golden age of Hong Kong action cinema. In the story, Wang Wei (Xie Miao), an ordinary tradesman, has his daughter kidnapped by a criminal network, gets no help from corrupt police, and sets out to find her himself, allying with the journalist Navin (Joe Taslim). It is produced by Bill Kong, who also produced Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon and Lust, Caution, through Edko Films, which also distributes in Hong Kong, Macau and the mainland; it was written by Mak Tin-shu.

Its central selling point is a pan-Asian action ensemble: Xie Miao’s wushu intensity, Joe Taslim’s judo, Joey Iwanaga’s high kicks, Brian Le’s raw power and the Indonesian action legend Yayan Ruhian each bring a distinct style. Kensuke Sonomura is credited with additional action choreography, and Thai stuntmen also took part; the director says the most powerful action is still the most primal.

The film premiered in the Midnight Madness section of the 50th Toronto International Film Festival on 6 September 2025, then screened in competition at Sitges and at Busan, and Lionsgate acquired it after Toronto. It opened in North America and elsewhere in June 2026. Critics widely praised its hard-hitting choreography and the physical commitment of its cast, while some noted the plot is familiar.
highlights: Five performers bring five martial systems; watch how the styles collide within a single scene.
The office fight between Xie Miao and Joe Taslim shows action doubling as communication between characters.
The film goes back to hard, in-camera action rather than heavy effects, inviting comparison with Hong Kong’s golden age.
The plot is simple; the point is a family-driven search and long, continuous fights.
the-furious.editorial: For viewers comfortable with relentless close combat. Child trafficking and graphic physical violence make this a demanding action film.
the-furious.contentNote: Based on published synopses, trailers and distribution materials: child abduction and trafficking, intense close combat, bloodshed and sustained pursuit. Not a full viewing review; intensity, flashing and sound levels remain unverified. This is not an official classification of the screening edition.

memento.title: Memento
memento.release: May 29, 2026 · Mainland China release of the restored version
memento.syn: Unable to form new long-term memories after an assault, Leonard pursues the man he believes killed his wife. Photographs, notes and tattoos replace the continuity he has lost. Teddy and Natalie offer help, but every clue must be trusted without its full context. Two interlocking timelines place the audience inside that uncertainty.
memento.bio: Christopher Nolan is a British director, and Memento, his second feature, brought him attention in the American film world. He has often worked with his brother Jonathan Nolan, who wrote the short story the film is based on. Nolan has said he first wrote the script in linear order and then reordered it as on screen to check the logic.
memento.st:
Per multiple accounts, in July 1996 the Nolan brothers drove from Chicago to Los Angeles, and on the way Jonathan pitched an idea about a man who cannot form memories. Christopher was drawn to it; each then wrote his own version, Jonathan as the short story Memento Mori and Christopher as the screenplay, and a few months later Christopher came up with the idea of telling it backwards. The two exchanged drafts over a long period. Because the film came out before the story was published in Esquire in March 2001, the script was eligible for the original screenplay Oscar.

The film was shot in just 25 days on a budget reported between 4 and 4.5 million dollars, and all of Carrie-Anne Moss’s scenes were shot in eight days. Reportedly every major studio passed before Newmarket backed and distributed it. It showed at Venice in September 2000 and Sundance in January 2001, and opened in New York and Los Angeles in March, shot on location in Burbank, California.

According to AFI, the film’s portrait of amnesia is not accurate; Nolan used it as a metaphorical dramatic device. It earned Oscar nominations for Best Original Screenplay and Best Film Editing, and Nolan’s script won the Waldo Salt Screenwriting Award at Sundance.
highlights: The reverse structure puts the viewer in Leonard’s position, always starting without knowing what came before.
Tattoos, Polaroids and notes are the memory system Leonard builds for himself.
The alternating black-and-white and color timelines are the key to the structure; there is no need to grasp it all on a first viewing.
Jonathan Nolan’s short story differs greatly from the film and makes an interesting companion read.
honors: 提名｜74th Academy Awards · Original Screenplay
提名｜74th Academy Awards · Film Editing
入选｜US National Film Registry (2017)
memento.contentNote: Based on published synopses, trailers and distribution materials: murder and gun violence, sexual-assault backstory, psychological manipulation. Not a full viewing review; intensity, flashing and sound levels remain unverified. This is not an official classification of the screening edition.
memento.editorial: For viewers who enjoy piecing together unreliable information. Avoid ending explanations; the story also involves violence, grief and manipulation.

papa.title: Papa
papa.release: June 27, 2026 · Mainland China release (Hong Kong release December 5, 2024)
papa.syn: Café owner Yuen Wing-nin loses his wife and daughter in a violent act committed by his son. Keeping the business open, he moves through reminders of family life while his son receives psychiatric care. Grief, anger and the wish to remain a father coexist, as memories interrupt the routines through which he tries to continue living.
papa.bio: Philip Yung (Weng Ziguang) is a Hong Kong director whose films often draw on real cases; his earlier film Port of Call won at the 2016 Hong Kong Film Awards, and according to reports Lau Ching-wan was the ceremony host that night and handed the award to the film’s newcomer Chun Hsia. Papa is Yung’s first collaboration with Lau, who he says kept him waiting two or three years after he sent the script, because the actor never reads other scripts while shooting a film.
papa.st:
The film draws on a real family tragedy that happened in 2010 in Tsuen Wan, Hong Kong, a street away from where the director grew up. After Port of Call won awards in 2016, he was commissioned by another director to do research, which is how he met the father in the case and heard many of his stories. According to the director, the real father agreed to the family’s story becoming a film but asked him to promise never to seek out his son, a promise he made and kept.

In the film, the tea restaurant owner Ruan Yongnian (Lau Ching-wan) has a happy family until his elder son (Su Wentao) suffers a sudden schizophrenic episode and kills his mother (Gu Zulin) and sister. The film does not dwell on the crime itself but follows how the father lives afterward, unable to release his grief and unable to hate the killer, interleaving non-chronological earlier moments so that viewers piece together the family’s former happiness. Su Wentao was a university student and this is his first film.

The film earned 11 nominations at the 43rd Hong Kong Film Awards, with the Best Actor, Best Supporting Actress and Best New Performer awards going to the three family members, so three of the four family members won acting prizes. Lau also won Best Actor at the Asian Film Awards and Best Actor from the Hong Kong Film Critics Society. It opened in the mainland on 27 June 2026.
highlights: The film avoids showing the crime graphically and stays with daily life afterward, as a father keeps his shop open and keeps living.
Non-chronological flashbacks let viewers piece together a family’s past happiness.
Lau Ching-wan’s restrained performance is called among his best by critics, and the details reward close attention.
The director often draws on real cases, so it pairs with Port of Call.
honors: Winner | 43rd Hong Kong Film Awards · Best Actor (Lau Ching-wan)
Winner | 43rd Hong Kong Film Awards · Best Supporting Actress (Louise Wong)
Winner | 43rd Hong Kong Film Awards · Best New Performer (So Man-to)
papa.contentNote: Based on published synopses, trailers and distribution materials: family homicide, bereavement and grief, recollections of violence. Not a full viewing review; intensity, flashing and sound levels remain unverified. This is not an official classification of the screening edition.
papa.editorial: A difficult family-trauma drama. The actions in this individual case should not be generalised to people living with mental illness.

pressure.title: Pressure
pressure.syn: In the 72 hours before D-Day, meteorologist James Stagg warns that a storm threatens the invasion. Eisenhower must choose whether to launch or delay an operation on which thousands of lives depend, with incomplete data and conflicting advice.
pressure.bio: Anthony Maras is an Australian director whose earlier work includes Hotel Mumbai. He directed and edited Pressure and co-wrote it with the original playwright David Haig. He joined the project on a visit to London, which was the final piece that let the film go ahead.
pressure.st:
The film is adapted from David Haig’s 2014 stage play Pressure, which first ran in Edinburgh and then in London’s West End. Haig wrote it after studying documents and interviewing the Stagg family, making the Scottish meteorologist James Stagg its hero. The film takes place in the 72 hours before D-Day: every piece is in place except the British weather, and the final decision rests with Supreme Allied Commander Dwight D. Eisenhower.

Andrew Scott plays Stagg and Brendan Fraser plays Eisenhower, with Kerry Condon as his aide Kay Summersby and Chris Messina as Colonel Irving P. Krick, Eisenhower’s personal weatherman. Working Title and StudioCanal produced it, Focus Features distributes it in North America, the cinematographer is Jamie D. Ramsay and the composer is Volker Bertelmann.

Reviewers called it a chamber-piece D-Day film: the battlefield is traded for a military briefing room and meteorological data becomes a ticking-clock psychological thriller. Several critics praised the performances and script, while one noted the director shows some inexperience at this scale. It opened in the United States on 29 May 2026 and runs 110 minutes.
highlights: A D-Day film about waiting for the weather, its tension coming from the briefing room rather than the battlefield.
The scenes between Scott and Fraser are the center; notice the contrast in their styles.
The rivalry between Stagg and Krick over forecasting is the key to the pressure of the decision.
Adapted from a stage play, the film keeps the dialogue-driven tension of theatre.
pressure.editorial: For viewers interested in historical decisions and scientific uncertainty. Expect a tense decision-room drama rather than continuous battlefield action.
pressure.contentNote: Based on published synopses, trailers and distribution materials: war and casualty discussions, sustained psychological pressure, battlefield peril. Not a full viewing review; intensity, flashing and sound levels remain unverified. This is not an official classification of the screening edition.

disclosure-day.title: Disclosure Day
disclosure-day.syn: Evidence that humanity is not alone draws ordinary people into a struggle over a hidden truth. Some want it revealed; others want it buried. The possibility of disclosure changes whom people trust and what the whole world must confront.
disclosure-day.bio: Steven Spielberg made alien-themed classics such as Close Encounters of the Third Kind and E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial, and Disclosure Day returns to extraterrestrial subjects. The story is his own, written up as a screenplay with David Koepp, reportedly their sixth collaboration, and John Williams scores for him for the 30th time.
disclosure-day.st:
The story unfolds through a series of mysteries: cybersecurity expert Daniel Kellner (Josh O’Connor) and his girlfriend (Eve Hewson) steal classified files from a mysterious firm called Wardex, which has worked with the US government for years to keep experiments on alien beings secret. Meanwhile Margaret Fairchild (Emily Blunt), a Kansas City TV meteorologist, suddenly begins making strange sounds on live broadcast, and the film turns into a cross-country chase with three interwoven threads.

Filming took place between February and May 2025 in New York, New Jersey and Atlanta, with cinematography by Janusz Kamiński, production design by Adam Stockhausen, costumes by Paul Tazewell and sound including Gary Rydstrom. According to one review, Blunt’s garbled alien speech was recorded with Rydstrom, without AI.

Reception is split: some critics call it Spielberg’s best film in twenty years and his most quintessentially Spielbergian, while Little White Lies gave it three stars and found it lacking his signature magic, and others found the antagonist too one-note. It opened on 12 June 2026 and runs 145 minutes.
highlights: Spielberg returns to alien subjects, which invites comparison with Close Encounters and E.T.
Blunt’s alien-speech scenes are the focus of the sound design.
The film treats disclosure like breaking news, so watch the live television sequences.
John Williams’ score is a clue to its mix of nostalgia and spectacle.
disclosure-day.editorial: For viewers drawn to alien contact and conspiracy suspense. Avoid twist explanations before watching; allow for the long running time.
warnings: alien threat and fear of the unknown
disclosure-day.contentNote: Based on published synopses, trailers and distribution materials: alien threat and fear of the unknown, pursuit and peril. Not a full viewing review; intensity, flashing and sound levels remain unverified. This is not an official classification of the screening edition.

the-backrooms.title: Backrooms
the-backrooms.release: June 26, 2026 · Mainland China; May 29 · North America
the-backrooms.syn: A strange doorway in a furniture showroom leads into an apparently endless network of rooms. Familiar decor becomes threatening as direction, distance and escape cease to behave normally. Entering to search for someone also means crossing the boundary of ordinary reality.
the-backrooms.bio: Kane Parsons is a young American creator who, in January 2022 at age 16, posted the short The Backrooms (Found Footage) to YouTube under the name Kane Pixels, made entirely in Blender and After Effects, and which grew into a series. A24 asked him to turn the universe into a feature; media reports say he was only 20 when the film was released.
the-backrooms.st:
The Backrooms began as an internet urban legend: a maze-like, endless space of office rooms. Parsons’s short series made it popular, and the millions of views led A24 to invite him to make a feature. The screenplay is by Will Soodik, based on Parsons’s series, with producers including James Wan, Shawn Levy and Osgood Perkins.

In the film, Clark (Chiwetel Ejiofor), the owner of a failing furniture store in northern California, regularly sees his therapist Mary Kline (Renate Reinsve). He discovers an entrance to another space and asks his employee Kat (Lukita Maxwell) and her boyfriend Bobby (Finn Bennett) to document it; the expedition goes wrong and Mary has to go in herself. Critics note that Clark leads the first half and Mary takes over in the second. The cinematographer is Jeremy Cox, and the score is by Parsons and Edo Van Breemen.

The film opened in the United States on 29 May 2026, runs 110 minutes and is rated R. Reception is mostly positive: some critics call it one of the most unsettling films of 2026, while others find the midpoint turn jarring and say it never fully embraces its chaotic potential.
highlights: Born of an online horror legend, the film turns the strangeness of endless space into physical sets.
Fluorescent lights, monotonous carpet and empty offices are the film’s key visuals.
Critics read in it a post-pandemic alienation, which makes loneliness and trauma a useful lens.
The shift of the lead between its two halves is an important structural change.
the-backrooms.editorial: For fans of spatial horror and internet folklore. No complete knowledge of the web series is required; consider sensitivity to confinement and prolonged dread.
the-backrooms.contentNote: Based on published synopses, trailers and distribution materials: confinement and disorientation, supernatural threat, sustained horror tension. Not a full viewing review; intensity, flashing and sound levels remain unverified. This is not an official classification of the screening edition.

no-other-love.title: No Other Love
no-other-love.book: Der Hahn ist tot by Ingrid Noll
no-other-love.syn: Agricultural researcher Zhi Ning lives a solitary routine until a literary talk introduces her to writer Kou Yi. An invitation to travel seems to promise romance, but concealed desires and shifting relationships pull the group into a dangerous chain of choices.
no-other-love.bio: The film credits Yuan Mei as executive producer and director, with Li Qiang as screenwriter and producer. Speaking of its release a decade on, Li said it was like something he once loved and put in a secret place, then could not find, and found again ten years later.
no-other-love.st:
The film was originally titled No Other Love, reportedly shot in 2016, shelved for a full decade, and released in the mainland on 28 March 2026 under the title Honey’s Needle. It centers on Zhi Ning (Yuan Quan), an agricultural-academy insect researcher who falls for the writer Kou Yi (Geng Le) at a literary lecture and, in an obsessive love, spirals out of control as people around her meet misfortune, which led it to be called a rare female-led crime film. Yuan appears almost without makeup and even with a shaved-brow look, and she reads the character’s love as emotional projection.

The cast is unusual: besides Yuan and Geng, Ning Jing, Yu Feihong, Qi Xi and Chen Chong appear. According to online articles, the released version differs from the original with recasting and reshoots: the male lead was originally played by an actor known as Mr. Dai and was replaced by Geng Le. These changes affected the film’s integrity and became part of the controversy, though the details have not been fully explained officially.

Reception is sharply divided: some call it an avant-garde work ten years ahead of its time, others criticize its logic as collapsing and its portrayal of women as stereotyped. Wenhui Daily reports that its first-week box office barely passed 10 million yuan.
highlights: The dichotomy of beneficial and harmful insects is how the heroine sees relationships and the film’s core device.
Yuan Quan’s performance, a break from her usual image, is the most discussed aspect.
The first-person narration and voice-over immerse viewers in the heroine’s self-justification.
The ten-year shelving and changes are the background to its completeness and controversy.
no-other-love.editorial: Suited to viewers who can handle extreme characters and dark material. It includes several killings, stalking and an obsessive relationship; those sensitive to such material should choose carefully, and the heroine’s obsession should not be read as a model of love.
no-other-love.contentNote: Based on published synopses, trailers and distribution materials: murder and criminal violence, obsessive and controlling relationships, emotional humiliation and distress. Not a full viewing review; intensity, flashing and sound levels remain unverified. This is not an official classification of the screening edition.

project-hail-mary.title: Project Hail Mary
project-hail-mary.release: March 20, 2026 · Mainland China and North America
project-hail-mary.book: Project Hail Mary by Andy Weir
project-hail-mary.syn: Science teacher Ryland Grace wakes alone aboard a distant spacecraft with little memory of how he got there. As experiments and returning memories reveal a threat to the Sun, he must find a way to save Earth. An unexpected friendship makes the apparently solitary mission something neither participant can solve alone.
project-hail-mary.bio: Phil Lord and Christopher Miller are an American directing duo known for 21 Jump Street, The Lego Movie and the Spider-Verse series. Project Hail Mary is their first feature behind the camera since they were removed from Solo, and critics called it their first truly adult film. They also produce alongside Ryan Gosling and others.
project-hail-mary.st:
The film is adapted from Andy Weir’s 2021 novel of the same name; Weir also wrote The Martian. According to Wikipedia, MGM was nearing a deal in March 2020 with Ryan Gosling attached to star and produce, with the rights reportedly acquired for about 3 million dollars; in May 2020 Phil Lord and Christopher Miller were hired to direct. Because they were committed to Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse, the screenplay went to Drew Goddard, who had been Oscar-nominated for adapting The Martian.

The story follows the high-school science teacher Ryland Grace (Ryan Gosling), who wakes on an interstellar spacecraft with no memory of why he is there and befriends an alien creature called Rocky as they try to save humanity. Rocky is largely done with physical puppetry rather than pure CG, which critics call one of the film’s greatest achievements, and the cinematography by Greig Fraser, who won an Oscar for Dune, is also praised.

The film premiered in London on 9 March 2026 and opened in the United States on 20 March, runs 156 minutes and is rated PG-13. Rotten Tomatoes’ first reviews were widely glowing, calling it the first real blockbuster of the year, while Variety’s reviewer found it baggy and derivative of films you have seen before.
highlights: Rocky is mostly a physical puppet; notice how his scenes with Gosling build a friendship.
Scientific problem-solving is a pleasure it shares with The Martian.
Greig Fraser’s cinematography makes space feel real and handmade.
How the film compresses a 500-page novel is another angle for comparison.
project-hail-mary.editorial: For viewers who enjoy scientific problem-solving and unlikely friendship. Avoid ending explanations and allow for the long running time.
project-hail-mary.contentNote: Based on published synopses, trailers and distribution materials: space peril and oxygen risks, isolation and loss of companions, global catastrophe threat. Not a full viewing review; intensity, flashing and sound levels remain unverified. This is not an official classification of the screening edition.

dragonfly.title: Dragonfly
dragonfly.syn: Elsie, an elderly woman living alone, is recovering from a fall when her younger neighbour Colleen steps into her life with company she has long lacked. As the two lonely women grow close, the warmth slowly turns toward something unpredictable. Rooted in social realism, the film exposes the pressure and danger loneliness can breed.
dragonfly.bio: Paul Andrew Williams was born in Portsmouth in 1973. His debut feature was London to Brighton (2006); Song for Marion (2012) won the screenplay award at the third Beijing International Film Festival. His work also includes Bull (2021), bringing vulnerable lives and social observation into tense genre storytelling.
dragonfly.st:
Dragonfly had its world premiere at Tribeca on June 6, 2025, where Andrea Riseborough and Brenda Blethyn shared the international narrative performance award. It subsequently won Best International Feature at Galway and the Golden Hitchcock at Dinard. At the 2026 Beijing International Film Festival, it won Best Film, Best Screenplay and a shared Best Actress award.

The production notes focus on people neglected by the state or their families and on the limits of social care. At the Beijing discussion, the producer described establishing the women as a source of comfort to one another before outside pressures disturb that balance.
honors: 获奖｜2026 Beijing International Film Festival · Tiantan Best Film, Best Screenplay and Best Actress (shared by Andrea Riseborough and Brenda Blethyn)
获奖｜2025 Tribeca Festival · Best Performance in an International Narrative Feature (shared)
获奖｜2025 Galway Film Fleadh · Best International Feature
获奖｜2025 Dinard British and Irish Film Festival · Golden Hitchcock
warnings: Loneliness and neglect of the elderly
dragonfly.editorial: Recommended for viewers drawn to performance-led drama, British social realism and psychological suspense. Watch how acts of care shift power between the women and how other people's assumptions affect trust. Reviews praise the leads while differing over the later change in tone.
dragonfly.contentNote: References IFCO advisories for the Irish theatrical edition: strong violence, strong language and suicide-related scenes, alongside published material on loneliness and neglect. The touring edition has not been reviewed in full; editing differences, flashing and sound levels remain unverified. This is not the screening edition's official classification.
highlights: Riseborough and Blethyn build the relationship through everyday gestures and pauses.
Care, loneliness and institutional responsibility give the suspense a social dimension.

three-goodbyes.title: Three Goodbyes
three-goodbyes.syn: Marta, a high-school teacher in Rome, and Antonio, a chef, split up after an argument that seems trivial. Alone, Marta loses her appetite and begins to notice something is wrong with her body. The film follows how she faces goodbyes: to a lover, to her earlier self, to life itself.
three-goodbyes.bio: Isabel Coixet is a Spanish writer-director whose work often explores women's lives, intimacy and mortality. Her films include My Life Without Me, The Secret Life of Words and The Bookshop. This adaptation continues her attention to farewells and the sensory experiences of ordinary life.
three-goodbyes.st:
World premiere: TIFF Special Presentations, September 8, 2025. It opened the 70th Valladolid International Film Festival in competition and was selected for the 2026 Beijing Tiantan competition.

The film draws on three stories from Michela Murgia's autobiographically inflected collection Tre ciotole and was filmed in Rome. The original title means Three Bowls. At the Beijing discussion, its producer explained how the adaptation retains food, music and popular culture alongside illness and separation, treating limited time as a reason to rediscover life.
honors: 入选｜2025 Toronto International Film Festival · Special Presentations
入围｜2025 Valladolid International Film Festival · Main Competition (opening film)
入围｜2026 Beijing International Film Festival · Tiantan Main Competition
three-goodbyes.editorial: Recommended for viewers interested in women rebuilding their lives, literary adaptation and everyday emotion. Appetite, walking through Rome and music make bodily experience part of the story. Critics value the acting and emotional detail, while some find the structure conventional.
three-goodbyes.contentNote: Based on published synopses and distribution materials: Break-up and illness; Death and farewell. Not a full viewing review; intensity, flashing and sound levels remain unverified. This is not an official classification.
highlights: Food and the loss of appetite connect physical change with emotional change.
The adaptation joins three stories from Murgia's collection in a Roman setting.

isabel.title: Isabel
isabel.syn: Isabel is a sommelière in São Paulo's fine-dining scene, working at a two-Michelin-star restaurant but weary of a controlling boss and a list built for crowd-pleasing. She quits to open a natural-wine bar of her own. Her plans fail to ferment as expected, and she must choose between playing it safe and one bold chance.
isabel.bio: Gabe Klinger was born in São Paulo in 1982 and has worked as a film teacher, critic and programmer. A Berlinale Talents alumnus, he directed Double Play: James Benning and Richard Linklater (2013), which won the Venice documentary-on-cinema award, and Porto (2016).
isabel.st:
World premiere: Berlinale Panorama, February 16, 2026; subsequently selected for the Beijing Tiantan competition.

Klinger co-wrote the film with its star Marina Person, also a filmmaker and former MTV presenter. Shot on 16mm, it explores São Paulo and natural-wine culture. Isabel's taste for imperfect wines parallels her wish for an independent working life; starting a business becomes a process of trying, failing and beginning again.
honors: 入选｜2026 Berlin International Film Festival · Panorama
入围｜2026 Beijing International Film Festival · Tiantan Main Competition
isabel.editorial: Recommended for viewers who enjoy city portraits, adult women's lives and light comedy. Notice the relationship between film grain, natural wine and accepting imperfection. Reviews appreciate its tone and social observation, while some find the story slight.
isabel.contentNote: Based on published synopses and distribution materials: Workplace pressure; Financial strain. Not a full viewing review; intensity, flashing and sound levels remain unverified. This is not an official classification.
highlights: 16mm photography gives São Paulo's restaurants and streets a tactile presence.
Marina Person co-wrote the character she plays, linking work, taste and independence.

two-people-one-life-and-a-dog.title: Two People in One Life and a Dog
two-people-one-life-and-a-dog.syn: An elderly couple of intellectuals in St. Petersburg, separated from their children, have kept warmth, patience and forgiveness through loneliness and a difficult past. Through plain daily routine and sparring conversation, the film traces the long warmth of a life shared, with a small dog wandering into the frame as part of the household.
two-people-one-life-and-a-dog.bio: Andrey Zaytsev, born in Moscow in 1975, works in documentary and fiction. A Siege Diary (2020) won the Moscow festival's main prize and earned him Best Director at the 11th Beijing International Film Festival. His other films include 14+ and its sequel. He wrote, directed, produced and edited this film.
two-people-one-life-and-a-dog.st:
World premiere: Moscow International Film Festival Main Competition, April 22, 2025; winner of the festival's Audience Award. It was released in Russia on October 16, 2025 and selected for the 2026 Beijing Tiantan competition.

At the Beijing discussion, Zaytsev spoke of an older generation's understanding of marriage and its love for others. The Russian title plays on Jerome K. Jerome's Three Men in a Boat (To Say Nothing of the Dog). Books, conversation, humour and visitors connect the elderly couple with a changing world.
honors: 入围｜2025 Moscow International Film Festival · Main Competition
获奖｜2025 Moscow International Film Festival · Audience Award
入围｜2026 Beijing International Film Festival · Tiantan Main Competition
two-people-one-life-and-a-dog.editorial: Recommended for viewers who enjoy actor duets, daily routines and relationships across generations. Watch the literary references and the way younger visitors alter the atmosphere. Responses vary between admiration for the leads' rapport and reservations about the simple structure.
two-people-one-life-and-a-dog.contentNote: Based on published synopses and distribution materials: Ageing and loneliness; Estrangement from children. Not a full viewing review; intensity, flashing and sound levels remain unverified. This is not an official classification.
highlights: The leads portray a lifetime together through conversation, humour and habits.
A St Petersburg apartment, books and records preserve the texture of a generation.

ky-nam-inn.title: Ky Nam Inn
ky-nam-inn.syn: Saigon, 1985. Khang, a young translator from the North rising within the new regime, is assigned to translate The Little Prince. At home he meets Ky Nam, a quiet widow next door and a remnant of the defeated South. When an accident forces her to rely on him, the inn fills with cooking, literary references and unspoken longing.
ky-nam-inn.bio: Leon Lê, born in Vietnam in 1977, worked in dance, singing and Broadway performance before turning to filmmaking. His debut feature Song Lang (2018) won the Most Promising Director award in Beijing's Forward Future section. Ky Nam Inn reunites him with Lien Binh Phat, writer Nguyen Thi Minh Ngoc and cinematographer Bob Nguyen.
ky-nam-inn.st:
World premiere: TIFF Special Presentations, September 7, 2025. It screened in Busan's A Window on Asian Cinema and won Hawaii's Kau Ka Hōkū Award. In 2026 it entered Beijing's Tiantan competition and won Best Director at the Asian Art Film Festival in Macao.

The starting point was a woman the director knew who cared for neighbours while privately struggling. The film places that contrast in Saigon in 1985, a time linked to his childhood and Vietnam's social transformation. Shot on 35mm, it uses The Little Prince, meals, old songs and shared work to express unspoken feelings.
honors: 入选｜2025 Toronto International Film Festival · Special Presentations
入选｜2025 Busan International Film Festival · A Window on Asian Cinema
获奖｜2025 Hawaii International Film Festival · Kau Ka Hōkū Award
入选｜2026 Palm Springs International Film Festival
入围｜2026 Beijing International Film Festival · Tiantan Main Competition
获奖｜2026 Asian Art Film Festival, Macao · Best Director (Leon Lê)
ky-nam-inn.editorial: Recommended for viewers ready for a long, unhurried romance and a portrait of neighbourhood life. Cooking, washing dishes, music and translation offer ways into its restrained emotions. Film at Lincoln Center highlights its compositions; the Hawaii jury praised its interplay of poetry, music and literature.
ky-nam-inn.contentNote: Based on published synopses and distribution materials: Post-war political pressure; Widowhood and loneliness. Not a full viewing review; intensity, flashing and sound levels remain unverified. This is not an official classification.
highlights: 35mm photography evokes the old buildings and daily textures of Saigon in 1985.
Translation and food connect private longing with post-war social change.

our-girls.title: Our Girls
our-girls.syn: Two longtime couples escape to the Austrian Alps, but a serene getaway descends into chaos after an accident involving a child. When it comes to saving your own child, is there any line you wouldn't cross? Their once-solid bond begins to fracture, and decent people do things that are far from acceptable.
our-girls.bio: Mike van Diem is a Dutch writer-director whose debut Character won the 1998 Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film. Our Girls adapts Lykele Muus's 2019 novel We Do What We Can, using an ensemble cast and extended scenes to explore parental loyalty and moral compromise.
our-girls.st:
The film opened the Netherlands Film Festival on September 26, 2025. It won three Golden Calves, including Best Feature, Leading Performance and Screenplay, and Best Director in Warsaw. The Dutch film critics named it their best Dutch film of 2025.

In a Filmkrant interview, van Diem said casting director Marina Wijn recommended Muus's novel. He was attracted to the possibilities for four actors to confront one another. Moving an argument to a mountain bench and keeping all four people in a restaurant scene allow concealment and self-justification to emerge through performance.
honors: 入选｜2025 Netherlands Film Festival · Opening Film
获奖｜2025 Golden Calf · Best Feature Film
获奖｜2025 Golden Calf · Best Leading Performance (Thekla Reuten)
获奖｜2025 Golden Calf · Best Feature Screenplay
提名｜2025 Golden Calf · Best Sound Design
获奖｜2025 Warsaw International Film Festival · Best Director
评选｜Dutch Film Critics Association · Best Dutch Film of 2025
入围｜2026 Beijing International Film Festival · Tiantan Main Competition
warnings: Moral dilemmas within family and friendship
our-girls.editorial: Recommended for viewers interested in family ethics, ensemble acting and dark humour. Notice when friends become negotiating opponents and reasonable explanations expose private interests. VPRO Cinema praised the film's sharp black comedy and moral ambiguity.
our-girls.contentNote: Based on published synopses and distribution materials: Accident involving a child; Moral dilemmas within family and friendship. Not a full viewing review; intensity, flashing and sound levels remain unverified. This is not an official classification.
highlights: The open Alpine landscape contrasts with increasingly confined relationships.
Long scenes allow all four adults to change the balance of an argument.

in-my-parents-house.title: In My Parents' House
in-my-parents-house.syn: Holle, a therapist interested in alternative ways to help the sick, must balance her professional life with her ageing parents and her older brother, whose condition is worsening. While her other siblings turn away, she senses a much bigger silence in the family. Shot in black and white, the film speaks to the guilt and helplessness of caregiving.
in-my-parents-house.bio: Tim Ellrich was born in Osnabrück in 1989. His first fiction feature, In My Parents' House, was his graduation film at Filmakademie Baden-Württemberg. Drawing on his family experience, it won a Special Jury Award in Rotterdam's 2025 Tiger Competition.
in-my-parents-house.st:
World premiere: IFFR Tiger Competition, February 3, 2025; winner of a Special Jury Award. It also entered the 15th Beijing Tiantan competition.

The film draws on Ellrich's mother and her relationship with a brother living with schizophrenia, including the last part of his life. It was filmed in the family home familiar to the director. Black-and-white photography and restrained use of dialogue and music give weight to domestic space and repeated tasks such as ironing and brushing teeth.
honors: 入围｜2025 International Film Festival Rotterdam · Tiger Competition
获奖｜2025 International Film Festival Rotterdam · Special Jury Award
入围｜2025 Beijing International Film Festival · Tiantan Main Competition
in-my-parents-house.editorial: Recommended for viewers interested in family caregiving and restrained images. Watch the rooms and repeated actions: when does helping turn into control, and who carries responsibility? IFFR's programme notes stress the caregiver's fatigue and the claustrophobia of duty.
in-my-parents-house.contentNote: Based on published synopses and festival materials: family caregiving pressure and conflict. Not a full viewing review; intensity, flashing and sound levels remain unverified. This is not an official classification.
highlights: The family home connects personal memory with the practical labour of care.
Black-and-white images and ordinary gestures build tension without easy judgments.

the-summer-book.title: The Summer Book
the-summer-book.syn: Nine-year-old Sophia has recently lost her mother and spends the summer on a small island in the Finnish archipelago with her father and her aged grandmother, a spirited artist nearing the end of her life. Amid island light and nature, grandmother and child face life and death together and slowly find their way of being together.
the-summer-book.bio: Charlie McDowell is an American director. His adaptation of Tove Jansson's 1972 novel was written by Robert Jones and filmed in Finland, with cinematography by Sturla Brandth Grøvlen and music by Hania Rani.
the-summer-book.st:
World premiere: BFI London Film Festival Special Presentations, October 12, 2024. It was also selected for the 15th Beijing Tiantan competition.

In the sales pressbook, McDowell recalls reading Jansson in his twenties and remembering childhood summers on an island off Massachusetts. Filmed in Finland on 16mm with natural light, the island becomes a participant in the story: waves, storms and long summer days respond to the grandmother, child and father at different stages of life.
honors: 入选｜2024 BFI London Film Festival · Special Presentations
入围｜2025 Beijing International Film Festival · Tiantan Main Competition
the-summer-book.editorial: Recommended for viewers who enjoy nature, relationships between grandparents and children, and a low-key narrative. Follow the light, wind and small reactions. Critics praise Glenn Close and the meditative images, while some find the novel's poetry difficult to translate to film.
the-summer-book.contentNote: Based on published synopses and distribution materials: Bereavement and grief; Ageing and death. Not a full viewing review; intensity, flashing and sound levels remain unverified. This is not an official classification.
highlights: 16mm and natural light shape the island's changing atmosphere.
Three generations respond differently to the same loss; weather and daily routines become narrative rhythms.

elevator-to-the-gallows.title: Elevator to the Gallows
elevator-to-the-gallows.syn: Julien and his lover Florence plot to kill her husband and stage it as a suicide. But when Julien returns to retrieve a forgotten rope, he is trapped in an elevator during a power cut. Meanwhile a young couple steal his car and are drawn into another murder. Florence searches the Paris streets alone for the lover who never arrives, as the perfect plan unravels through a chain of accidents.
elevator-to-the-gallows.bio: Louis Malle (1932–1995) was a French filmmaker whose work spanned documentary and fiction, in France and the United States. His fiction feature debut, Elevator to the Gallows, was followed by films including The Lovers, The Fire Within and Au revoir les enfants. He shared the New Wave's appetite for location shooting and formal experimentation while pursuing an independent path.
elevator-to-the-gallows.st: Released in French cinemas on 29 January 1958, the film had already won the 1957 Prix Louis-Delluc. Adapted from Noël Calef's novel by Malle and Roger Nimier, it combines noir plotting with the modern atmosphere of Paris at night. Miles Davis and his musicians recorded their score while watching projected footage in a Paris studio, completing the session in one night. The film is widely regarded as an important precursor to the French New Wave.
honors: 获奖｜1957 Prix Louis-Delluc · Best Film
elevator-to-the-gallows.editorial: For viewers drawn to film noir, jazz and cities after dark. Watch the contrasting rhythms of confinement in the lift and Moreau's wandering through Paris, linked by Davis's trumpet. The crime mechanics can strain plausibility, but the music, photography and sense of loneliness remain distinctive.
highlights: Literature and noir: Malle and Roger Nimier adapted Noël Calef's novel, turning an apparently meticulous murder plan into several intersecting journeys through the night.

Sound and city: Miles Davis and his musicians played to projected footage, matching the characters' waiting with jazz phrasing and pauses. The recording took one night, building on preparation rather than entirely spontaneous invention.
Moreau on screen: Her nocturnal walks give the city lights, her face and the music room to carry emotion beyond the demands of the plot.
elevator-to-the-gallows.contentNote: Based on published synopses and distribution materials: Murder disguised as suicide; Car theft and a killing. Not a full viewing review; intensity, flashing and sound levels remain unverified. This is not an official classification.
elevator-to-the-gallows.book: Elevator to the Gallows by Noël Calef

la-haine.title: Hate
la-haine.syn: After a riot in a Paris suburb, a young man badly hurt by police fights for his life in hospital. His three friends Vinz, Hubert and Said drift between the estate and central Paris, through confrontation, humiliation and aimless waiting. Vinz finds a revolver lost by a police officer and vows to avenge his friend. Over one long day, anger and unease build, and the line of violence draws steadily closer.
la-haine.bio: Mathieu Kassovitz is a French director, writer and actor. La Haine, one of his most influential early films, earned him the Best Director award at Cannes. Its visual energy draws on American genre cinema while confronting life in the French suburbs. He has continued to work both behind and in front of the camera.
la-haine.st: Premiered in competition at Cannes on 27 May 1995, winning Best Director, before its French theatrical release on 31 May. It received the César awards for Best Film and Best Editing the following year. Kassovitz began writing after Makome M’Bowole was shot dead in police custody in Paris in 1993. The film channels that anger into a day and night in three friends' lives, moving between their housing estate and central Paris through a tightly timed, black-and-white urban journey.
honors: 获奖｜1995 48th Cannes Film Festival · Best Director (Mathieu Kassovitz)
入围｜1995 Cannes Film Festival · Main Competition (Palme d'Or)
获奖｜1996 21st César Awards · Best Film; Best Editing
获奖｜1995 European Film Awards · Young European Film
warnings: Street confrontation and racial and class tension
la-haine.editorial: For viewers interested in street culture, youth ensembles and formally bold social cinema. Notice how the friends move between humour and hostility, and how urban spaces and police encounters mark their place in the city. Its genre energy comes with violence, strong language and steadily mounting unease.
highlights: A real starting point: Kassovitz began writing after Makome M’Bowole died in police custody in Paris in 1993, turning questions about police violence into three young men's day and night.
Space and rhythm: Clocks, mirrors, rooftops, transport and enclosed rooms chart the friends' movements between the estate and central Paris, asking where they can go and who sees them.
Genre energy: Mobile camerawork and popular music give the film its street rhythm, while jokes, impressions and arguments ground its social concerns in the friends' everyday relationships.
la-haine.contentNote: Based on published synopses and distribution materials: Police violence and firearms; Street confrontation and racial and class tension. Not a full viewing review; intensity, flashing and sound levels remain unverified. This is not an official classification.

rosetta.title: Rosetta
rosetta.syn: Young Rosetta lives in a trailer park with her alcoholic mother. She searches desperately for work, hoping to escape poverty through her own labour and lead an ordinary life like everyone else. Repeated dismissals and rejections put that simple wish out of reach. When a young man offers help, the pressure to survive pushes her into a hard choice. The film follows her footsteps, portraying a girl's stubborn pursuit of work, dignity and belonging.
rosetta.bio: Belgian brothers Jean-Pierre and Luc Dardenne began in documentary and have long explored work, poverty and individual moral choices. Following La Promesse, Rosetta developed their camera's close attention to bodies and actions, earning them their first Palme d'Or.
rosetta.st: Premiered in competition at Cannes on 22 May 1999 and won the Palme d'Or by a unanimous jury decision the next day. Émilie Dequenne shared the Best Actress award for her screen debut and later received a César nomination for Most Promising Actress in 2000. The camera stays close to Rosetta's movements and breathing, making her search for work a physical experience. Repeated tasks—finding a job, carrying water and moving gas cylinders—bind the need to survive to the desire for dignity.
honors: 获奖｜1999 52nd Cannes Film Festival · Palme d'Or (unanimous jury decision)
获奖｜1999 52nd Cannes Film Festival · Best Actress (Émilie Dequenne, shared)
提名｜2000 25th César Awards · Most Promising Actress (Émilie Dequenne)
获奖｜1999 Belgian Film Critics Association · André Cavens Award for Best Belgian Film
warnings: Physical struggles with police and an employer
rosetta.editorial: For viewers interested in labour, young women's lives and the Dardennes' filmmaking. Follow Rosetta's movements and search for work before judging her troubling choices: compassion and moral discomfort coexist here. The close handheld camera and relentless anxiety make this an intense viewing experience.
highlights: A camera close to the body: Following Rosetta's shoulders, steps and breathing limits our view of the world. Social pressure is felt physically before its wider structures come into focus.
Work and dignity: Job hunting, fetching water and carrying gas cylinders recur throughout. Work becomes her gateway to an ordinary life, entangling survival with moral choices.
Performance through action: Dequenne's tense physical presence carries the story. The film neither rushes to explain Rosetta's psychology nor turns her into an easily lovable symbol of poverty.
rosetta.contentNote: Based on published synopses and distribution materials: Poverty and an alcoholic parent; Physical struggles with police and an employer; Betrayal and a moral dilemma. Not a full viewing review; intensity, flashing and sound levels remain unverified. This is not an official classification.

ponette.title: Ponette
ponette.syn: Four-year-old Ponette loses her mother in a car crash that also injures her. She cannot grasp what death means and will not accept that her mother is gone for good. Her father, relatives and little friends try to comfort her in their own ways, but no explanation dispels her confusion and longing. Convinced her mother will return, she keeps talking to her, prays to God, and searches for reunion with a child's imagination and stubbornness. Between reality and fantasy, she travels alone through loss, faith and growing up.
ponette.bio: Jacques Doillon is a French writer and director, born in Paris in 1944. His films frequently explore children, adolescents and the conflicts within close relationships. Known for The Little Gangster and Ponette, he builds emotional drama from small changes in speech, gesture and behaviour.
ponette.st:
Ponette screened in competition at the 53rd Venice Film Festival in September 1996, where Victoire Thivisol won the Volpi Cup for Best Actress and the film received the FIPRESCI Prize. Its precise first screening date remains unconfirmed. It opened in France on 25 September 1996.

Before completing the screenplay, Doillon spoke with young children about death and their mothers. A child psychoanalyst followed the performers during production. The film draws on children's own ways of speaking and understanding: religious explanations, playground exchanges and stubborn hope coexist without resolving neatly into an adult lesson.

The camera frequently stays close to the children's eye level, treating play, silence and imagination as meaningful emotional actions. ACMI highlights this perspective and the performances that sustain it. Roger Ebert awarded the film 3.5 out of four stars. Production footage later became Jeanne Crépeau's separate Canadian documentary Playing Ponette (2007); that film's title and production details should not be confused with this feature.
honors: 入围｜1996 Venice Film Festival · Main Competition
获奖｜1996 Venice Film Festival · Volpi Cup for Best Actress (Victoire Thivisol)
获奖｜1996 Venice Film Festival · FIPRESCI Prize
获奖｜1996 Venice Film Festival · OCIC Award (shared with The Funeral)
获奖｜1997 New York Film Critics Circle · Best Foreign Language Film
ponette.editorial: For viewers drawn to a child's perspective and finely observed performances. Notice how Ponette keeps asking, waiting and playing as she searches for her own way to understand loss. The story concerns a young child's grief after her mother's death and can be emotionally demanding.
highlights: A child’s questions make the experience of loss immediate and difficult to dismiss.
Victoire Thivisol moves delicately between playfulness and grief.
Conversations about death and faith turn abstract questions into actions children can understand.
ponette.contentNote: Based on published synopses and distribution materials: Bereavement and a child's grief; Aftermath of a car crash. Not a full viewing review; intensity, flashing and sound levels remain unverified. This is not an official classification.

amour-2012.title: Amour
amour-2012.syn: Georges and Anne are retired music teachers in their eighties, living together in their Paris apartment. An illness gradually weakens Anne and changes their daily life completely. Honouring his wife's wish not to return to hospital, Georges takes on the burden of care alone. As ageing, pain and loss close in, the couple must face the hardest test love can bring.
amour-2012.bio: Michael Haneke is an Austrian writer and director, born in Munich in 1942. After working in theatre and television, he developed a rigorous cinema of violence, spectatorship and intimate relationships. Both The White Ribbon and Amour won the Palme d’Or. Here, his precise observation centres on the daily life of an elderly couple.
amour-2012.st:
Amour had its world premiere in competition at the 65th Cannes Film Festival on 20 May 2012 and won the Palme d’Or. In 2013 it received the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film, alongside nominations for Best Picture, Director, Actress and Original Screenplay. It also won five César Awards: Film, Director, Actor, Actress and Original Screenplay.

At Cannes, Haneke described his starting point as the difficulty of facing the suffering of someone one loves. He was posing a question rather than supplying a solution to ageing. He conceived Georges for Jean-Louis Trintignant, with Emmanuelle Riva and Isabelle Huppert completing the central family. Pianist Alexandre Tharaud also appears.

Long takes and the enclosed apartment make physical change, silence and the labour of care central to the drama. The film avoids easy reassurance. Critical responses particularly praised the leading performances; Amy Taubin highlighted the precision of the filmmaking and the delicacy of the acting.
honors: 获奖｜2012 Cannes Film Festival · Palme d’Or
获奖｜2013 Academy Awards · Best Foreign Language Film
提名｜2013 Academy Awards · Best Picture, Director, Actress and Original Screenplay
获奖｜2013 César Awards · Best Film, Director, Actor, Actress and Original Screenplay
获奖｜2012 European Film Awards · Best Film, Director, Actress and Actor
获奖｜2013 BAFTA Film Awards · Film Not in the English Language; Leading Actress (Emmanuelle Riva)
提名｜2013 BAFTA Film Awards · Director; Original Screenplay
amour-2012.editorial: For viewers interested in performance, intimate relationships and the ethics of care. Notice the couple’s surviving humour, courtesy and shared habits: they make their predicament painfully specific. The film addresses stroke, loss of independence, end-of-life care and death, with a slow pace and considerable emotional weight.
highlights: Two veteran performers convey decades of shared life through small gestures.
The familiar apartment gradually becomes a boundary around care and solitude.
Love is examined through everyday responsibility and unresolved ethical questions.
amour-2012.contentNote: Based on published synopses and distribution materials: Illness, ageing and caregiving; Death and loss. Not a full viewing review; intensity, flashing and sound levels remain unverified. This is not an official classification.

les-miserables-2019.title: Les Misérables
les-miserables-2019.syn: Stéphane joins the anti-crime squad in Montfermeil, a Paris suburb, patrolling with two veteran colleagues. He soon sees the tense, fragile balance between residents, local powers and the police. While tracking a stolen lion cub, an officer wounds a boy, and a drone captures it all. The struggle over that footage lets long-simmering tensions in the neighbourhood slip out of control.
les-miserables-2019.bio: Ladj Ly is a French filmmaker born in 1978. Beginning with documentaries and shorts, he has long filmed the Clichy–Montfermeil neighbourhood where he grew up, working with collaborators including artist JR. His 2017 short Les Misérables became the basis of this first fiction feature, bringing an insider’s perspective to the tensions between policing and neighbourhood life.
les-miserables-2019.st:
Les Misérables premiered in competition at the 72nd Cannes Film Festival on 15 May 2019, sharing the Jury Prize with Bacurau. It subsequently received an Academy Award nomination for Best International Feature Film and won four César Awards in 2020: Film, Male Newcomer, Editing and the Public Award.

Developed from Ly’s 2017 short of the same name, the feature was inspired by an incident of police violence he had filmed. It was shot in the Paris suburb where he grew up. Its title echoes the setting and social concerns of Victor Hugo’s novel, rather than adapting its plot.

A patrol gradually exposes competing neighbourhood interests before everyday friction escalates into confrontation. Ground-level footage and drone images shift the viewer’s position, making evidence and control of the image crucial. Cannes’s introduction emphasised Ly’s attention to residents and police; Time praised the film’s ability to immerse viewers in its world. Reviews also noted its accumulating energy and explosive final act.

入围｜2019 Cannes Film Festival · Main Competition (Palme d'Or)
获奖｜2020 César Awards · Best Film, Best Editing, Most Promising Actor (Alexis Manenti), Audience César
获奖｜2019 European Film Awards · European Discovery (FIPRESCI Prize)
获奖｜2020 Goya Awards · Best European Film

warnings: Police violence and a wounded boy
les-miserables-2019.editorial: For viewers interested in urban space, social realism and tense genre storytelling. Watch how the same encounter looks to officers, teenagers and witnesses, and how recording an image changes the balance of power. The film includes injuries to minors, police violence and group confrontations; its later sections are particularly intense.
highlights: A new officer’s first patrol gradually reveals the neighbourhood’s competing powers.
A drone turns questions of evidence and ownership of images into a central visual theme.
Urgent thriller pacing connects a local incident with a wider social predicament.
les-miserables-2019.contentNote: Based on published synopses and distribution materials: Police violence and a wounded boy; Neighbourhood clashes and mob violence. Not a full viewing review; intensity, flashing and sound levels remain unverified. This is not an official classification.

anatomy-of-a-fall.title: Anatomy of a Fall
anatomy-of-a-fall.syn: Writer Sandra lives in the French Alps with her husband Samuel and their visually impaired son Daniel. One day Samuel is found dead below their chalet, and Sandra becomes the prime suspect. As the investigation and trial proceed, the couple's quarrels, their creative rivalry and the secrets of family life come out one by one. Daniel, both a boy who has lost his father and a key witness, must choose between memory, doubt and trust in his mother.
anatomy-of-a-fall.bio: French filmmaker Justine Triet explores the friction between private lives and public judgment. Her features include Age of Panic, In Bed with Victoria and Sibyl. Her fourth feature, Anatomy of a Fall, was co-written with Arthur Harari.
anatomy-of-a-fall.st: World premiere: Cannes Competition, 21 May 2023; winner of the Palme d’Or. Triet and Harari developed the screenplay over three years, consulting a criminal lawyer. She wrote Sandra for Hüller and withheld the ending from the young actor to preserve his uncertainty. Budget constraints led to shooting with an Alexa and vintage lenses rather than 35mm film.
honors: 获奖｜2023 Cannes Film Festival · Palme d'Or
获奖｜2024 Academy Awards · Best Original Screenplay

获奖｜2023 European Film Awards · Film, Director, Actress, Screenwriter and Editing

warnings: Family quarrels and allegations of domestic violence
anatomy-of-a-fall.editorial: For viewers who enjoy courtroom drama and ambiguous characters. Listen to how testimony turns shared memories into competing narratives. Language, recordings and the child’s perspective complicate every judgment. The long, dialogue-driven film rewards patience.
highlights: Marriage, creative work and the unequal division of time enter the courtroom.
Recordings and offscreen sound become evidence.
Hüller, Arlaud and Machado-Graner keep the legal suspense rooted in family life.
anatomy-of-a-fall.contentNote: Based on published synopses and distribution materials: Death and a trial; Family quarrels and allegations of domestic violence; A child compelled to testify. Not a full viewing review; intensity, flashing and sound levels remain unverified. This is not an official classification.

parallel-tales.title: Parallel Tales
parallel-tales.syn: Novelist Sylvie begins secretly watching the neighbour across from her in search of inspiration for a new book. She hires a young man, Adam, to help with her daily life, never imagining that this stranger will transform her life and her writing. As relationships shift, the fiction she writes and her real life interweave and the once-clear boundary blurs, until the imagined story outruns everyone's reality.
parallel-tales.bio: Iranian filmmaker Asghar Farhadi builds moral dilemmas from ordinary events and conflicting accounts. A Separation and The Salesman won Oscars for Foreign Language Film. Parallel Tales returns him to France after The Past, turning his attention to the relationship between imagination and everyday life.
parallel-tales.st: World premiere: Cannes Competition, 14 May 2026, alongside its French theatrical release. Later festival appearances include Sydney, AFI FEST and Hamburg. Loosely inspired by Kieślowski’s Dekalog: Six, it places a novelist opposite a group of film foley artists. Young assistant Adam connects their apartments as writing, sound effects and dual identities blur reality and fiction.
honors: 入围｜2026 Cannes Film Festival · Competition (Palme d’Or)
入围｜2026 Sydney Film Festival · Official Competition
parallel-tales.editorial: For viewers intrigued by voyeurism and narrative puzzles. Festival programmers praise its imaginative maze; several premiere reviews found its structure more convincing than its characters. Watch how observing others changes their lives.
highlights: Huppert leads an ensemble with several dual roles.
Foley work questions how realism is manufactured.
A novelist’s curiosity becomes an ethical dilemma.
parallel-tales.contentNote: Based on published synopses and distribution materials: Voyeurism and boundary-crossing; Emotional manipulation and betrayal. Not a full viewing review; intensity, flashing and sound levels remain unverified. This is not an official classification.

style-kaleidoscope.name: Style Kaleidoscope
style-kaleidoscope.blurb: From Bergman’s road memories to Tarkovsky’s apocalyptic prayer, from Fei Mu’s city wall to Tsui Hark’s jianghu, seventeen works spanning 1947 to 2025 share one screen — a map of “style.”

cinema-2026.name: 2026 Now Showing

sparrow-tribe-space.name: Sparrow Tribe Film Space
sparrow-tribe-space.blurb: Sparrow Tribe is an independent screening and curating collective, best known over the past decade for its “blind-box screenings.” After four quiet years, it set out again around National Day 2026 with an offline arthouse space of its own: Sparrow Tribe Film Space. This page collects the space’s screening schedule and will be updated as sessions are announced.

golden-rooster-2026.name: 2026 Golden Rooster Film Screening

german-film-2026.name: 2026 German Film Festival
german-film-2026.blurb: The 2026 Festival of German Cinema in China arrives in Hangzhou from November 14 to 23 at CINEMA CIRCLE (Hangzhou Heng Long), with ten acclaimed titles from the past two years of international festivals.
